283. Reversible gates and exact phase-labelled support

A reversible gate has a nonempty finite word map with distinct sources and distinct targets, together with a nonempty phase-successor trace. Inversion swaps each source and target while retaining row order and the phase trace. The inverse satisfies the same admission conditions; applying the row inversion twice recovers the original gate.

An admitted state has nonempty branch support, distinct words and a distinct phase cycle containing at least two labels. Every branch phase belongs to that cycle. A nonempty phase action shifts the registered phase index by the trace length modulo the cycle length. The native preservation proof establishes that the action retains every word in its original order, retains the phase cycle and returns another admitted state.

Complete support generation uses every word of the declared position count over the registered alphabet, in literal product order. The source permits a singleton alphabet; that domain is preserved. Generated-support membership is equivalent to the exact word length and membership of every label in the declared alphabet.

These components pass 818 comparisons against the pinned V3 operations, including rejected inputs and exact phase results. All 38 declarations in this component audit have zero axiom dependencies. Gate application, the complete inverse state trace and the other reversible-model components are included in the completed reversible-model entry.

For gate map \(G\) and successor trace \(u\), admission is
\[
 G\ne[],\quad\operatorname{distinct}(\pi_1G),\quad
 \operatorname{distinct}(\pi_2G),\quad u\ne[].
\]
Inversion maps \((x, y)\mapsto(y, x)\), swaps the two uniqueness conditions, retains \(u\), and satisfies \((G^{-1})^{-1}=G\) in the original row order. A state \((B, C)\) requires nonempty branch list \(B\), distinct branch words, distinct phase cycle \(C\) with \(|C|\ge2\), and every branch phase in \(C\).

For \(C_i\) the phase at index \(i\), phase action is
\[
 (w, C_i)\longmapsto(w, C_{(i+s)\bmod d}),\qquad
 d=|C|,\quad s=|u|\bmod d.
\]
Phase lookup and the modulo bound prove that the result remains in \(C\). Mapping this action over branches retains the exact word list, and therefore its nonemptiness and distinctness; state admission is preserved. Complete support over alphabet \(A\) and \(n\) registered positions satisfies
\[

\]
The original positive, distinct alphabet guard permits \(|A|=1\).

284. Exact inverse phase and branch reconstruction

For a phase-cycle length d, an original phase index below d and a shift s below d, the source inverse shift is zero when s is zero and d−s otherwise. Native constructive arithmetic proves that the forward modular shift followed by this inverse returns the original index. Distinct phase labels then identify the original phase exactly.

The complete branch transformation combines a registered word lookup with this phase action. When target words are distinct, reversing the word-map rows recovers each source word. The branch-level inverse theorem restores every original word and phase pair in order, including all retained branches.

The implementation passes 3,264 additional comparisons against original V3 gate application and inverse-state results. The 17 additional declarations have zero axiom dependencies. Wrapper admission and domain preservation are established by the integrated round-trip derivation below.

For \(d>0\), \(i<d\) and \(s<d\), define the exact inverse shift
\[
 \bar s=\begin{cases}0,&s=0,\\d-s,&s\ne0.\end{cases}
\]
The modular reconstruction is
\[
 ((i+s)\bmod d+\bar s)\bmod d=i.
\]
When \(s=0\), reduction returns \(i\). Otherwise \(s+(d-s)=d\); moving the first remainder through addition reduces the expression to \((i+d)\bmod d=i\). Distinct phase-cycle labels make phaseIndex of a selected label recover its unique original index, so this arithmetic identity restores the original phase.

For the word map, a forward lookup \(G(w)=v\) and distinct target words imply \(G^{-1}(v)=w\). Combining the two inverses gives
\[
 (w, C_i)\xmapsto{G, s}(v, C_{(i+s)\bmod d})
 \xmapsto{G^{-1},\bar s}(w, C_i).
\]
Induction over the branch list restores each head pair and then the tail, proving equality of the entire original ordered branch list.

 ((u, C_i),(v, C_j))

288. Complete repetition fault-mask enumeration

For a generated fault-depth trace of length d, the repetition encoder retains 2d + 1 copies of the held label. The fault census enumerates every position selection of size zero through d, in the original combination order, and records the changed word and its decoded label.

The native enumeration theorem establishes that a mask occurs exactly when it is a source-order sublist of the full position range with length at most d. It applies to arbitrary widths and depths. The decoder preserves the original rejection conditions: empty words, labels outside held/returned, and tied counts.

All 18 translated definitions and proved results have zero axiom dependencies. The implementation passes 1,322 original-source comparisons, including all 168 census rows for widths 3, 5 and 7 across both held labels. Arbitrary-depth correction is established in Section 289.

For ordered position list \(P\), the combinations recursion is
\[
 C(P, 0)=[[]],\qquad C([], k+1)=[],
\]
\[
 C(p::P, k+1)=[p::m\mid m\in C(P, k)]{+\!\!+}C(P, k+1).
\]
The first branch includes the current position and the second omits it, preserving the original combination order. Induction on \(P\) proves
\[
 m\in C(P, k)\iff m\text{ is a source-order sublist of }P\land|m|=k.
\]
Concatenating these lists for \(k=0,\ldots, d\) over \(P=[0,\ldots, w-1]\) therefore gives
\[
 m\in\operatorname{Masks}(w, d)
 \iff m\text{ is a sublist of }[0,\ldots, w-1]\land|m|\le d.
\]
An admitted depth trace has nonempty distinct labels and length \(d\); encoding returns \(w=2d+1\) copies of the selected held/returned label. Changing a word tests each successive position against \(m\), preserving word length. The decoder first checks nonempty support and allowed labels, then rejects equal held/returned counts and otherwise returns the strictly more numerous label.

289. Arbitrary-depth repetition correction

For every admitted repetition encoding with fault depth d, every mask in the complete census changes at most d positions among 2d + 1 retained labels. The opposite-label count is bounded by the mask length, and the two label counts sum to the full word length. The original label therefore has a strict majority.

The native correction theorem applies to both held and returned labels at arbitrary finite depth. The complete census returns precisely its source-ordered changed words, each paired with the original decoded label; no mask is omitted. All 14 correction definitions and theorems have zero axiom dependencies.

The eight original operational witnesses are also reproduced: complete support, phase action, joint composition, predecessor merging, nonfactorability, observation with retained record, inverse recovery, and exhaustive repetition correction at widths 3, 5 and 7. Their complete named output agrees with V3. All 16 witness declarations have zero axiom dependencies.

Let \(r\) be the opposite-label count and \(c\) the original-label count after applying a census mask \(m\). The change recursion proves
\[
 r\le|m|\le d,\qquad c+r=2d+1.
\]
For the count bound, a changed head consumes one occurrence of its position from the mask; removing that position does not affect any later position. Induction bounds the remaining opposite labels. The second identity follows because each word position contains exactly one of the two labels.

If \(c\le r\), then \(c+r\le2r\le2d\), contradicting \(c+r=2d+1\). Hence \(r<c\), and the original decoder returns the original label for both encodings. Induction over the complete ordered mask list now gives
\[
 \operatorname{Census}(a, D)=
 \operatorname{ok}\bigl(
 [(\operatorname{change}(m,\bar a, a^{\, 2d+1}), a)
       \mid m\in\operatorname{Masks}(2d+1, d)]\bigr).
\]
Here \(a^{\, 2d+1}\) denotes list replication, \(\bar a\) the other held label, and \(d=|D|\). The result covers every admitted finite depth and every enumerated mask, including the empty mask.

 \mathcal G=\prod_{i=1}^{8}[\mathrm{rejected},\mathrm{admitted}],
 \qquad|\mathcal G|=256,\qquad
 \operatorname{survives}(g)\iff\bigwedge_i g_i=\mathrm{admitted}.
\]
The source identifier comparison equals this coordinate criterion. Complete enumeration and the conjunction therefore establish the single all-admitted survivor.

Forward execution has an identity constructor and a successor retaining the current state, admitted gate and exact application result:
\[
 B_0\xrightarrow{G_1}B_1\xrightarrow{G_2}\cdots
 \xrightarrow{G_k}B_k,\qquad
 P=[B_0,\ldots, B_{k-1}].
\]
Each gate's round-trip theorem supplies its inverse step. Inductively invert the tail first, then the head, yielding
\[
 B_k\xrightarrow{G_k^{-1}}\cdots\xrightarrow{G_1^{-1}}B_0,
 \qquad |P|=k,\qquad |B_k|=|B_0|.
\]
Every inverse step uses the registered inverse phase action. Concatenation of forward traces concatenates both gate and predecessor lists.

The interpreter decodes a codeword to a name, looks up that name's request \((B_0,[G_i])\), and runs this exact gate evaluator. Under unique registry names, admitted encoding and an exact decoder, each registered request has an admitted codeword \(c\) satisfying
\[
 \operatorname{interpret}(c)
 =\operatorname{some}(\operatorname{evaluate}(B_0,[G_i])).
\]
For an admitted Forward trace, evaluation returns precisely \((P, B_k)\); inverse execution and both counts above therefore transfer to that interpretation.

The registry and code support are theorem parameters. Encoding validation and exact decoding supply, for every registry member, a supported codeword decoding to its name. Unique registry names make lookup recover that particular request. `exactRequest` then substitutes the decoder and lookup equations into the interpreter; induction on Forward substitutes the successful gate evaluation. Neither the registry size nor the gate-list length is fixed by the operational comparison census. \[
 x\in E_h\Rightarrow\operatorname{decode}(x)=\operatorname{ok}(\mathrm{held}),

\]
For a nonempty declared mask, the complete mask-membership theorem supplies the size bound used by correction. Thus both reconstruction and disjointness are consequences of the retained decoder on the specified error family.

323. Exact Fold return and binary multiplicative order

For q>0, let h_q(x) be the held representative of x modulo q: h_q(x)=x mod q when that remainder is nonzero, and h_q(x)=q otherwise. The executed recurrence is
\[
r_0=p,  r_{k+1}=h_q(2r_k)
\]
Induction gives r_k ≡ p·2^k (mod q): the initial step is p≡p·1, and doubling the induction identity gives r_(k+1)≡2p·2^k=p·2^(k+1). For a reduced input, gcd(p,q)=1. Because held representatives are unique in {1,…,q},
\[
r_k=p \iff  p\cdot 2^k\equiv p \pmod{q}
\]
\[
\iff  q\text{ divides }p(2^k-1)
\]
\[
\iff  q\text{ divides }2^k-1
\]
\[
\iff  2^k\equiv 1 \pmod{q}
\]
The cancellation uses gcd(p,q)=1. Taking the least positive k on both sides identifies first Fold return with first binary multiplicative order whenever that return exists. For odd q>1, existence follows from the finite-carrier argument below; the even-denominator transient is treated separately.

For every supplied positive reduced part p/q through the One, native repeated double-and-cast execution satisfies rank_k modulo q = p times 2^k modulo q. The complete-denominator representative is retained when a remainder vanishes. Reducedness permits cancellation of p: an exact return to the original held rank occurs if and only if 2^k modulo q equals 1 modulo q. The first-positive-return and first-positive-order predicates therefore have the same least index. These identities hold at arbitrary supplied finite depth; they do not use a bounded prime list. For a reduced starting rank p, an equality r_i=r_j with 0≤i<j<ℓ would imply 2^(j−i)≡1, contradicting minimality. Hence its complete cycle C(p) has exactly ℓ members.

For any cycles C(p), C(s), suppose r_i(p)=r_j(s). Each cycle has period ℓ, so advancing within the cycle by the complementary index ℓ−j expresses s as an iterate of p. The same reasoning expresses p as an iterate of s. Thus C(p)=C(s). Every reduced rank lies in its own cycle, and distinct cycles are disjoint. If R_q={r:1≤r<q, gcd(r,q)=1} and C is the number of cycles, successive removal of complete cycles therefore gives
\[
|R_q| = \ell  C
\]
For prime q, each 1≤r<q is coprime to q, so |R_q|=q−1 and
  q−1 = ℓ C, hence ℓ divides q−1.
This is a finite partition derivation for each admitted denominator, independent of the finite witness table.

For every admitted odd denominator above the One, the finite carrier forces a first binary return. If no return occurred through the carrier bound, one more executed position than there are held ranks would have to remain distinct, contradicting the exact finite count. The original order loop therefore terminates, and its returned count is the first binary multiplicative order. For every reduced numerator, the original orbit loop returns a complete ordered trace of exactly this length.

The executed cycles preserve reducedness. Two cycles that share a rank have identical members; every reduced rank belongs to its own cycle. Removing complete cycles successively from the full reduced-residue support proves that the residue count equals orbit length times orbit count. For a prime denominator, every positive rank below the prime is reduced, so the period divides one less than the prime. These are arbitrary supplied finite-denominator results, not conclusions extrapolated from the witness census.

The orbit loop also terminates for positive held parts with even denominators: each fresh step adds a distinct held rank, and the finite carrier bounds the number of additions before repetition. 327. Exact positive-ratio composition

Let N(a,b) denote division of a positive numerator and denominator by their greatest common divisor. Its normalized pair (u,v) satisfies av=ub. For an arbitrary reduced positive ratio x=(n,d), define its reciprocal y=N(d,n) and composition x·y=N(ny_n,dy_d). Value preservation for y gives dy_d=y_n n=ny_n. The composite therefore has equal positive raw numerator and denominator, and normalization gives (1,1). Every admitted positive ratio composed with its reciprocal returns the One, including ratios above the One.

For positive counts a,b,c, the raw product of the views a/b and b/c is N(ab,bc)=(u,v). Value preservation gives abv=ubc. Associativity and commutativity place the common positive factor b on the same side; applying finite division by b and the identity (bk)/b=k gives av=uc. Thus this composite represents a/c exactly. For any positive m, the raw product of m/1 and 1/m is (m·1,1·m); commutativity makes the sides equal, and normalization yields (1,1). This reconstructs the One from m corresponding equal parts.

These native component results have thirteen audited definitions and theorems with zero axiom dependencies. The full source entry additionally includes shorter separation, complement, local transport and finite-family cycle composition.

The same telescoping law holds for actual composition after normalizing both input views. Let x=N(a,b), y=N(c,d), and z=compose(x,y). Value preservation gives ax_d=x_n b, cy_d=y_n d, and (x_n y_n)z_d=z_n(x_d y_d). Put e=x_d y_d>0. Multiplying and rearranging the first two identities gives (ac)e=(x_n y_n)(bd). Multiplication by z_d and substitution of the third identity therefore yield e(ac z_d)=e(z_n bd). Exact positive cancellation gives ac z_d=z_n bd. Specializing the second view to N(b,c) gives ab z_d=z_n bc; cancellation of b gives a z_d=z_n c. Thus normalization of either input and the composite preserves the telescoping relation itself.

328. Unique positive holding complement

For a generated count m>1, write m=k+2 and define h=N(k+1,k+2), the exact (m−1)-of-m part. A positive ratio x=n/d is the holding complement of the equal part 1/m precisely when x+1/m=1. Clearing the positive denominator dm gives the entirely positive-side equation
\[
nm+d=dm
\]
Expanding dm=d(k+1)+d and removing the same terminal d from both sides forces nm=(k+1)d. Normalization of h gives h_n m=(k+1)h_d, so h satisfies the holding equation. If any other positive ratio x satisfies it, multiply its forced equality by h_d and the equality for h by d. Rearranging gives m(nh_d)=m(h_n d). Cancellation by positive m yields nh_d=h_n d, establishing uniqueness of the exact rational value. At m=2, h=N(1,2)=(1,2), the half-One witness. The condition m>1 is precisely the positive-complement domain: at m=1 the holding equation would require n+d=d, which admits no positive numerator. These seven native definitions and theorems have zero axiom dependencies; the source entry's other relation and cycle requirements remain separate.

331. Least common return of every positive finite cycle family

For supplied positive periods a,b, let g=gcd(a,b). The actual native least-common-multiple operation is L=ab/g. Since g divides both a and b, exact division yields L=a(b/g)=b(a/g). Thus a divides L, b divides L, and L>0. Also gL=ab.

To prove minimality, let c>0 be any shared return, so a divides c and b divides c. Then ab divides both ac and bc. The constructive greatest-common-divisor property gives ab dividing gcd(ac,bc). Positive scaling gives gcd(ac,bc)=c·gcd(a,b)=cg. Therefore cg=abk=gLk for a finite count k. Cancelling the positive g gives c=Lk, so L divides every positive shared return and L≤c. This establishes the first common return, not merely one common multiple.

For a nonempty supplied finite family, retain its first period p and the remaining finite list P. Define J(p,[])=p and J(p,q::P)=J(lcm(p,q),P). Induction proves positivity and the exact characterization, for every positive n,
  J(p,P) divides n ⇔ p divides n and every period in P divides n.
The empty-tail case is the single cycle. At a successor, divisibility by lcm(p,q) is equivalent to simultaneous divisibility by p and q, by the two-period result; the induction hypothesis handles the remaining list. Applying the characterization to n=J(p,P) shows that every supplied period returns there. Applying it to any other positive shared return n shows J(p,P) divides n and hence J(p,P)≤n. The original witness is J(2,[3,4])=12. All sixteen native definitions and theorems in this derivation have zero axiom dependencies; the construction uses no completed infinite family or fixed period table.

335. Exact finite-difference identities

Put q=2^k and h=1/q at a positive generated depth k. For the centered quadratic construction, clearing the denominator q² gives
\[
(q+1)^{2}+(q-1)^{2}=2q^{2}+2
\]
Thus (1+h)²+(1−h)²=2+2h², and the centered second difference divided by h² is exactly 2. The native proof establishes the denominator identity for q=m+1 by distributivity and exact addition; it is not inferred from the finite witness list.

For the forward cubic construction, clearing q³ gives
\[
(q+2)^{3}+q^{3}=2(q+1)^{3}+6q+6
\]
Equivalently (1+2h)³+1=2(1+h)³+6h²+6h³. Its forward second difference divided by h² is therefore 6+6h, with exact positive error E_k=6/2^k. The native error carrier is the normalized positive fraction N(6,2^k); its numerator and denominator satisfy 6E_d=E_n2^k. The denominator successor is 2^(k+1)=2^k+2^k. These seven audited component declarations have zero axiom dependencies.

For normalized E_k=(a_n,a_d) and E_(k+1)=(b_n,b_d), value preservation gives 6a_d=a_n2^k and 6b_d=b_n(2^k+2^k). Multiplying these identities by the opposite denominators and cancelling the positive 2^k yields (b_n+b_n)a_d=a_n b_d. Therefore 2E_(k+1)=E_k exactly. Since b_n a_d>0, it follows that b_n a_d<a_n b_d, proving strict decrease in the actual normalized representation.

There is also a finite certificate for every supplied positive rational tolerance a/d. Induction gives n+1≤2^n: at the successor, n+2≤2(n+1)≤2·2^n. Choose the finite depth K=6d. Then 2^K≥K+1>6d, so E_K=6/2^K<1/d≤a/d. The native proof multiplies through by the positive denominators and cancels only positive factors, establishing E_n d<a E_d for the normalized error pair. K is a sufficient generated certificate depth computed from the supplied tolerance; it is not a fitted scientific parameter or a claim of optimal depth. Thus the error can be certified below every supplied positive rational tolerance without introducing zero as an attained error or an ungenerated limit value. The finite-difference component now has eleven audited declarations with zero axiom dependencies.

338. Complete finite traces and the typed object boundary

\[
p\in T_n \iff  \exists k\le n, p=r_k
\]
Every record is a positive exact Part, so p∈T_n implies p_numerator>0. Moreover |T_n|=n+1<n+2=|T_(n+1)|: every reached finite trace has a strictly longer generated successor. This is an arbitrary supplied finite-depth construction, with no largest-stage object.

344. General odd-denominator vacuum recurrence

For any supplied denominator q > 1 with q mod 2 = 1, let r_k be the held rank obtained after k executions of the original binary Fold from unit rank r_0 = 1. The existing exact rank calculation gives

\[
 0<r_k\le q,\qquad r_k\equiv 2^k\pmod q,\qquad
 \gcd(r_k,q)=1.
\]

The first inequality follows from the positive held-rank transition. Reducedness follows from gcd(1,q) = 1 and coprimality of every binary power with odd q. Exact held-rank recovery identifies return with the binary order condition:

\[
 r_k=1\iff 2^k\bmod q=1\bmod q.
\]

If no positive return occurred through q steps, cancellation of the common binary factor would make all q+1 positions r_0,…,r_q distinct. They lie in the complete q-member positive rank carrier, contradicting its finite cardinality. Ascending search therefore supplies a first period p with

\[
 0<p\le q,\qquad r_p=1,\qquad
 \forall j,\ 0<j<p\Longrightarrow r_j\ne1.
\]

The executed transition then gives r_(p+k) = r_k. Repeated removal of a complete period yields

\[
 r_k=r_{k\bmod p}\qquad(k\ge0).
\]

Thus positivity and exact recurrence persist at every finite continuation, without a cutoff on denominators or Fold depth. Each generated odd successor q = 2n+3 satisfies q > 1 and q mod 2 = 1 by the exact remainder identity (3+2n) mod 2 = 3 mod 2 = 1, so the same first-return theorem applies for every supplied n. Five native theorems establish these statements with no axiom dependencies. The executable odd-denominator wrapper and its complete registered entry checks are separate from these general recurrence theorems.

346. Exact Fraction and held-rank recurrence correspondence

Let c_q(n) denote the original positive cast: repeatedly subtract q while the retained numerator is greater than q. Each subtraction preserves the remainder, so induction on the actual removal trace proves

\[
 c_q(n)\bmod q=n\bmod q.
\]

For positive n and q, the cast lies in 1,…,q. The held-rank Fold is

\[
 F_q(n)=\begin{cases}q,&2n\bmod q=0,\\2n\bmod q,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}
\]

It lies in the same held-rank interval and has remainder 2n mod q. Two ranks in 1,…,q with equal remainders are equal: a nonzero remainder names the rank itself, while zero names the retained whole q. Hence

\[
 c_q(n+n)=F_q(n).
\]

Write N(n,q) for the original normalized positive Fraction n/q. The already derived normalization and Fold-cast identity now yields the exact state equation

\[
 \operatorname{Fold}(N(n,q))=N(c_q(n+n),q)=N(F_q(n),q).
\]

For the unit orbit define x_k = N(r_k,q), where r_k is the actual held-rank iteration from section 344. Then Fold(x_k) = x_(k+1). The rank return r_p = 1 supplied for every odd q > 1 therefore gives x_p = x_0. This is equality of the actual normalized Fraction states, including their positive-cast convention, rather than only equality of modular residues. 350. Complete reference-equivalence classes and retained records

The equivalence properties and the separate observation record are those of the quantity carrier itself. If an observation o lies in both Q_a and Q_b, symmetry gives R(o.carrier,b), and transitivity with R(a,o.carrier) gives R(a,b). For any observation x, transitivity in both directions then yields
\[
 Q_a(o)\land Q_b(o)\Longrightarrow R(a,b),\qquad
 R(a,b)\Longrightarrow\bigl(Q_a(x)\iff Q_b(x)\bigr).
\]
Conversely, suppose membership agrees for all observations. Apply the membership equivalence to the observation with carrier b and any held record. Reflexivity gives membership in Q_b, hence R(a,b). Therefore
\[
 \bigl(\forall o,\ Q_a(o)\iff Q_b(o)\bigr)\iff R(a,b).
\]
Disconnected anchors consequently have no common member. The classes cover all admitted observations and are either disjoint or have identical membership, without constructing a quotient that erases records. If x and y belong to Q_a, kind preservation gives kind(x.carrier)=kind(a)=kind(y.carrier). Replacing only an observation's record leaves its membership unchanged; distinct records remain separately held by the underlying observation constructor. 351. Exact same-dimension reference transport

A reference retains its name and canonical dimension form. An admitted comparison from reference a to reference b carries both the equality D(a)=D(b) and a positive normalized ratio x. The dimension form is a held form, independent of the ratio's numerical value. If D(a)≠D(b), an admitted comparison would supply the contradictory equality, so no such comparison can be constructed.

For x=n/d with n,d positive, reversing the comparison exchanges the reference endpoints, reverses their dimension equality and uses the already derived normalized reciprocal. Writing N for exact normalization,
\[
 x^{-1}=N(d,n),\qquad
 x\,x^{-1}=N(1,1).
\]
For comparisons a→b with ratio x and b→c with ratio y, transitivity gives D(a)=D(c), and the composite ratio is
\[
 z=N(n_xn_y,d_xd_y),\qquad
 (n_xn_y)d_z=n_z(d_xd_y).
\]
The cross-product identity is the normalization-preserving composition theorem, valid at arbitrary admitted positive counts. For views N(n,m) and N(m,k), its existing exact cancellation theorem gives
\[
 n_z\,k=n\,d_z,
\]
so the intermediate reference cancels in value while both input comparisons remain available in the finite chain.

A chain begins with one comparison and extends by appending a comparison whose starting reference is the current endpoint. Its evaluated comparison is defined by
\[
 C([a\to b])=C_{ab},\qquad
 C(P\mathbin{+\!+}[b\to c])=C(P)\circ C_{bc}.
\]
The constructor retains the prior chain and the appended comparison. 352. Finite canonical dimension composition

The registered dimension statement describes canonical finite products and exact quotients of independent quantity kinds. Represent a generated description by a kind label, a product of two descriptions, or an exact quotient of two descriptions. Its support is the finite list of kind labels appearing in that description, retaining both operands at every composition. No measured value enters this construction.

For a held kind k, retain a numerator count n and denominator count d. A matching kind contributes (1,0), and an absent kind contributes (0,0). Products add like-side counts; quotients exchange the second operand's sides:
\[
 C_k(ab)=(n_a+n_b,d_a+d_b),\qquad
 C_k(a/b)=(n_a+d_b,d_a+n_b).
\]
These are counts of occurrences in the finite description. Their zero denotes absence of a factor, not a physical zero magnitude. Cancellation gives the canonical residual pair
\[
 R(n,d)=(n-d,d-n).
\]
At least one residual side is absent: if n≤d, n−d=0; otherwise d≤n and d−n=0. Induction on the common appended count c proves
\[
 R(n+c,d+c)=R(n,d).
\]
Thus a common numerator/denominator factor cancels exactly without choosing a numerical scale or using a signed physical magnitude.

Write F_k(p)=R(C_k(p)) for the held form of description p at kind k. Descriptions share a dimension precisely when their forms agree at every kind. Reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity follow from equality of the residual pairs. Distinct primitive labels cannot be identified: at label k, the description k has pair (1,0), whereas a different primitive q has pair (0,0). This retains the independence of the kind carriers.

Finite count addition proves product commutation and association. Exchanging denominator orientation proves
\[
 (a/b)/c \sim a/(bc),\qquad a/(b/c)\sim(ac)/b.
\]
Here ∼ means equality of all held kind forms. For (ab)/b, the counts at each kind are n_a+n_b+d_b and d_a+d_b+n_b. Reordering the same appended support and applying common-factor cancellation gives
\[
 (ab)/b\sim a,\qquad a/a\sim 1.
\]
The final notation denotes absence of every residual factor, not an extra primitive quantity. Likewise, the counts of (a/b)(b/c) contain the common addition n_b+d_b on both sides. Removing that addition proves
\[
 (a/b)(b/c)\sim a/c.
\]
These identities hold for every supplied finite description, including composite denominator descriptions.

353. Complete finite decision of held dimension identity

Let S(p) be the complete generated support of a description p. Induction on its construction proves that k∉S(p) implies C_k(p)=(0,0), hence F_k(p)=(0,0). For products and quotients, absence from the appended support implies absence from both operand supports, and the count equations preserve the absent pair.

The executable comparison checks every label in S(a)++S(b):
\[
 B(a,b)=\bigwedge_{k\in S(a)\mathbin{+\!+}S(b)}
             [F_k(a)=F_k(b)].
\]
If B is true, finite-list induction supplies equality at each listed kind. Any unlisted kind is absent from both supports and has pair (0,0) on both sides. Therefore the finite comparison establishes equality at every kind. Conversely, equality at every kind supplies every conjunction member, so finite-list induction makes B true:
\[
 B(a,b)=\mathrm{true}\iff
       \forall k,\ F_k(a)=F_k(b).
\]
Duplicate occurrences and support order do not omit a kind: the comparison retains the complete operand supports, and repeated equality checks preserve the result. Distinct primitive kind labels are rejected by the finite comparison because its soundness would otherwise contradict primitive independence. The construction, cancellation identities and complete finite decision are established by 31 native theorems; all 39 declarations in this component have zero axiom dependencies.

356. Operational realization with a complete retained trace

A realization step from reference a to reference b contains the admitted same-dimension comparison, its exact positive ratio x, source identity σ and observation record ρ. A finite process begins with one step and extends only by a step whose starting reference is the current endpoint. For a process P and appended step s, define its resulting comparison and trace by
\[
 R([s])=s.\mathrm{comparison},\qquad
 R(P\mathbin{+\!+}[s])=R(P)\circ s.\mathrm{comparison},
\]
\[
 T([s])=[\mathrm{row}(s,x)],\qquad
 T(P\mathbin{+\!+}[s])=
 T(P)\mathbin{+\!+}[\mathrm{row}(s,R(P\mathbin{+\!+}[s]).\mathrm{ratio})].
\]
Each row holds the from-reference, to-reference, source identity, observation record, local factor and cumulative ratio. The row constructor preserves both endpoints and both source fields exactly. The composition operation is the normalized positive ratio composition of Section 351; hence, writing x=n_x/d_x and y=n_y/d_y,
\[
 \mathrm{ratio}(R(P\mathbin{+\!+}[s]))
 =N(n_xn_y,d_xd_y),
\]
where x is the prior cumulative ratio and y the appended comparison ratio.

Let H(P) be the ordered list of source-identity/record pairs and let L(P) count steps. The first-step equations are H([s])=[(σ_s,ρ_s)] and L([s])=1; extension appends that pair and increases the count by one. The finite-list identities
\[
 \mathrm{map}(f,X\mathbin{+\!+}[x])
 =\mathrm{map}(f,X)\mathbin{+\!+}[f(x)],\qquad
 |X\mathbin{+\!+}[x]|=|X|+1
\]
follow by induction on X. Applying them at each process extension proves
\[
 \mathrm{map}((σ,ρ),T(P))=H(P),\qquad |T(P)|=L(P)>0.
\]
Thus the trace is nonempty, retains every comparison record in order and preserves its entire prior prefix on extension. The resulting comparison carries D(a)∼D(b), and its normalized ratio has positive numerator. Twelve native theorems establish these statements with zero axiom dependencies. Source identity here is the retained identity field; the trace theorem preserves supplied records and does not manufacture empirical observations.

358. Complete retention of measurement uncertainty

A source-bound alternative consists of its relation, source identity and the recorded verdict of whether it remains admissible. Let a(x) denote that verdict. The uncertainty support is the complete ordered retention operation
\[
 U([])=[],\qquad
 U(x::X)=
 \begin{cases}
 x::U(X),&a(x)=\mathrm{true},\\
 U(X),&a(x)=\mathrm{false}.
 \end{cases}
\]
The admissibility verdict is part of the supplied measurement record. It is not a fitted choice made by this retention operation.

Define a valid retention derivation by three rules: the empty input retains the empty output; an admitted head must be retained; a rejected head must be removed. Induction on X constructs such a derivation for U(X). Induction on any valid derivation proves its output equals U(X). Therefore two valid retention derivations for the same input cannot select different supports.

List induction also proves both directions of the exact support statement:
\[
 x\in U(X)\iff x\in X\ \land\ a(x)=\mathrm{true}.
\]
The forward direction establishes source membership and admissibility; the reverse establishes that no admitted source alternative is omitted. A rejected alternative cannot belong to U(X), since membership would make its Boolean verdict both true and false. Finally, induction on X proves
\[
 U(X\mathbin{+\!+}Y)=U(X)\mathbin{+\!+}U(Y).
\]
Thus the construction preserves all admissible alternatives in source order, including their retained identities. Eight native theorems establish construction, exactness, unique selection, complete membership and concatenation with zero axiom dependencies.

360. Exact source-byte hashing equivalence

The empirical source check computes SHA-256 over the complete held byte array. Its block-local lookup is related to the original absolute lookup by the finite-list identity
\[
 \mathrm{get}(\mathrm{drop}(B,o),j)=\mathrm{get}(B,o+j).
\]
Induction on o proves the identity for every byte list B and index j, including the original out-of-range lookup behavior. Applying it to each of the four byte positions in every initial schedule word makes all 16 initial words identical. The remaining 48 schedule words use the same recurrence, so the entire block schedule agrees. Identical schedules and unchanged rounds imply identical block state updates. Induction over the block-offset list then gives
\[
 \forall B:\mathrm{ByteArray},\quad
 \mathrm{digest}_{\mathrm{window}}(B)=\mathrm{digest}_{\mathrm{original}}(B).
\]
Padding, constants, rounds and digest formatting remain the original operations. Six native theorems establish the lookup, schedule, block and whole-digest equivalence without axiom dependencies. Consequently each measurement experiment's source-match predicate equals its original predicate for every supplied source byte array. The complete snapshot is still hashed; the equivalence does not replace the bytes with a stored digest.

361. Dimensional consistency at every finite comparison

The source dimensional-consistency statement requires canonical path identity at each compared or joined pair, and restricts conversions to reversible exact same-dimension reference maps. The path construction and complete finite decision are those of Sections 352–353. For the full ordered list P of comparison pairs, define
\[
 A([])=\mathrm{true},\qquad
 A((p,q)::P)=B(p,q)\land A(P),
\]
where B is the proved finite comparison of canonical dimension forms. Define lawfulness by
\[
 \mathcal L(P)\iff
 \forall(p,q)\in P,\ \forall k,\ F_k(p)=F_k(q).
\]
Induction on the entire list proves both directions. If A is true, its first conjunct supplies canonical equality for the head pair, while the induction hypothesis supplies it for every tail pair. Conversely, lawfulness supplies the first finite comparison and the induction hypothesis supplies the remaining conjunction. Hence
\[
 A(P)=\mathrm{true}\iff\mathcal L(P).
\]
No comparison is selected or dropped. If a retained pair has unequal canonical forms, assuming A(P) true contradicts that pair's inequality; therefore A(P) is false. If P and Q are each lawful, induction on P proves lawfulness of P++Q, preserving the full comparison list.

An admitted conversion from reference a to reference b retains both D(a)∼D(b) and its exact positive normalized ratio x. Its inverse is the original reverse comparison b→a with reciprocal ratio. Symmetry of canonical path identity supplies the inverse dimension relation. The exact normalized ratio theorem gives
\[
 a\xrightarrow{x}b\xrightarrow{x^{-1}}a,
 \qquad N(x\,x^{-1})=\frac11.
\]
Here the displayed equality means the actual composed normalized fraction has numerator 1 and denominator 1. It follows from the previously proved reciprocal-return identity, rather than a numerical approximation. For a→b and b→c, transitivity of the retained dimension relations yields a→c, and soundness/completeness of B makes its finite dimension check pass. Unlike endpoint forms exclude an admitted conversion because such a conversion would carry the contradictory dimension relation.

For a full calibration chain P:a→b, the composition theorem in Section 359 supplies D(a)∼D(b); applying finite-comparison completeness gives B(D(a),D(b))=true. 363. Complete observed events and retained change

The mechanics source follows the completed measurement chain. A physical event retains the complete observed source state; a change retains both endpoint observations and the source-bound action connecting them. The construction below is uniform in the held state carrier and uses the already defined observation record. It does not replace that carrier with a finite answer classifier or a reported numerical inscription.

Write an observed event as E=(s,ρ), where s is the complete supplied carrier state and ρ is its held observation record. A transition from a to b holds source identity σ and action record A. Its retained row is
\[
 R(a\to b)=(a,b,σ,A).
\]
Both complete events remain present, including both observation records. Projecting a row recovers each of these coordinates. If either endpoint, source identity or action record differs, equality of the two rows would imply equality of that coordinate by projection, a contradiction. Reconstructing the row from its four projections returns the exact original row.

An event path begins at one observed event and extends by one transition from its current endpoint. Its event sequence E(P), transition rows T(P) and source/action ledger H(P) satisfy
\[
 E([a])=[a],\quad T([a])=[],\quad H([a])=[],
\]
\[
 E(P\mathbin{+\!+}[b\to c])=E(P)\mathbin{+\!+}[c],
\]
\[
 T(P\mathbin{+\!+}[b\to c])=T(P)\mathbin{+\!+}[R(b\to c)],
\]
\[
 H(P\mathbin{+\!+}[b\to c])=H(P)\mathbin{+\!+}[(σ_{bc},A_{bc})].
\]
The endpoint indices ensure that the appended transition starts at the previous endpoint. Let n(P)=|T(P)|. The append-one length identity proves n(P+[b→c])=n(P)+1. Induction on the path then proves
\[
 |E(P)|=n(P)+1,\qquad E(P)\ne[],\qquad
 \mathrm{map}((σ,A),T(P))=H(P).
\]
Thus every extension preserves all earlier events and transitions, appends exactly one generated change, and retains every source/action record in order. Fifteen native theorems establish these base, successor, retention and distinguishability properties without axiom dependencies.

364. Duration from generated recurrence

A held reference recurrence contains its starting observation, returning observation and complete event path C. It retains the equality of the returning and starting carrier states, while the observation records remain separately held. Its generated transition count m=n(C) is positive. No absolute background time coordinate enters the construction.

For a measured event path P, let n=n(P). The source distinction between absent change and positive duration is represented by separate constructors:
\[
 \Delta(P;C)=
 \begin{cases}
 \mathrm{EmptyOne},&n=0,\\
 \mathrm{Positive}(N(n,m)),&n>0,
 \end{cases}
\]
where N is the previously derived exact positive fraction normalization. The zero in the branch condition counts the absence of transitions; it is not a numerical physical duration. The positive constructor carries a fraction whose numerator is proved positive and whose denominator is nonzero.

For one observed event there is no transition, so Δ([a];C)=EmptyOne. Conversely, if Δ(P;C)=EmptyOne, a positive transition count would put the result in the distinct positive constructor. Therefore
\[
 \Delta(P;C)=\mathrm{EmptyOne}\iff n(P)=0.
\]
Appending a transition gives n+1 and excludes the Empty One case. For n>0, writing N(n,m)=u/v, exact normalization proves
\[
 nv=um,\qquad u>0.
\]
The reference recurrence compared with itself gives N(m,m)=1/1: both normalized numerator and denominator are exactly 1.

Changing the held reference from a recurrence of m transitions to one of k transitions composes the generated ratios. If z=N(n,m)\circ N(m,k), the exact telescoping theorem gives
\[
 z_{\mathrm{num}}\,k=n\,z_{\mathrm{den}}.
\]
The intermediate recurrence cancels in value while both source paths remain available. The event-count identity |E(P)|=n(P)+1 connects duration to the retained ordered path. Eleven native theorems establish absence, positive duration, exact normalization, reference return, reference-unit One and reference-change telescoping with zero axiom dependencies.

365. Reference-relative location and held displacement orientation

A location retains its reference identity, complete supplied support and observation record:
\[
 L=(r,S,ρ).
\]
Changing either the reference identity or the support distinguishes the location, because equality would preserve each projection. Rebuilding L from its three projections returns L exactly. This is a reference-relative record; no unobserved absolute position is added.

A displacement holds two such locations, their admitted exact positive separation x and which endpoint holds the orientation:
\[
 d=(L_1,L_2,x,h),\qquad h\in\{\mathrm{first},\mathrm{second}\}.
\]
The separation is the supplied exact quantity relation, not a fitted coefficient. Both endpoint reference identities and both observation records remain held. Define opposite(first)=second and opposite(second)=first. The two finite cases establish opposite(opposite(h))=h and opposite(h)≠h.

Reversing the comparison orientation is
\[
 \mathrm{reverse}(d)=(L_1,L_2,x,\mathrm{opposite}(h)).
\]
It preserves the positive magnitude and the entire source pair, changes the held orientation, and returns d when applied twice. Orientation reversal introduces no negative physical length.

Relabelling the written endpoint order is a separate description operation:
\[
 \mathrm{swap}(d)=(L_2,L_1,x,\mathrm{opposite}(h)).
\]
Checking the two held-endpoint cases proves that this operation preserves the actual held location. It also preserves x and is involutive. The distinction between reversing a comparison and exchanging the written endpoint order keeps orientation and description identity explicit. Fourteen native theorems establish the record, positivity, retention and orientation properties without axiom dependencies.

366. Exact speed and oriented velocity

The source speed relation divides the retained exact separation by a positive generated duration. Velocity retains that rate together with the displacement orientation. For separation x=n_x/d_x and duration t=n_t/d_t, define
\[
 q=N(n_xd_t,d_xn_t).
\]
Both products are positive because x and t are admitted positive fractions. Normalization supplies the exact cross-product identity
\[
 (n_xd_t)q_{\mathrm{den}}=q_{\mathrm{num}}(d_xn_t),
 \qquad q_{\mathrm{num}}>0.
\]
This constructs the quotient from the two retained quantity relations without an added numerical scale.

The native velocity record retains the displacement, both endpoint events, the complete event path, the reference recurrence and the proof that the path contains a transition. Its speed is the quotient above with t=N(n(P),n(C)); its orientation is the held displacement endpoint. Reversing that orientation leaves the displacement magnitude, event path and reference recurrence unchanged. Hence
\[
 \mathrm{speed}(\mathrm{reverse}(v))=\mathrm{speed}(v),
\]
\[
 \mathrm{orientation}(\mathrm{reverse}(v))
 =\mathrm{opposite}(\mathrm{orientation}(v)),\qquad
 \mathrm{reverse}(\mathrm{reverse}(v))=v.
\]
The duration trace and reference are retained by equality of the complete corresponding fields, rather than by equality of a reported number alone.

The dimension description is the generated quotient of the separation and duration descriptions. For each kind k, if their numerator/denominator occurrence counts are (a,b) and (c,d), its counts are
\[
 C_k(D_{\mathrm{speed}})=(a+d,b+c).
\]
This is the exact quotient construction of Section 352, retaining both dimension carriers. Equality of two unreduced quotient descriptions implies equality of each supplied operand description; their canonical comparisons still use the proved reduction relation. Eleven native theorems establish the exact rate, positivity, orientation, retained records and dimension-description properties with zero axiom dependencies.

370. Source-bound inertial continuation

The inertia construction retains the complete velocity carrier v, including displacement, orientation, generated path and reference recurrence. A transfer record is a triple t=(source identity, action record, resulting carrier). The V3 provenance rule has two admitted continuation forms: retain v when no transfer is present, or retain the result of the supplied source-bound transfer. With the absence marker denoted by none,
\[
 S(v,\mathrm{none})=v,\qquad
 S(v,\mathrm{some}(t))=t.\mathrm{result}.
\]
The inductive admissibility relation has exactly these retained and transferred constructors. Elimination of its constructors proves that every admitted continuation w satisfies \(w=S(v,s)\). Consequently, if an admitted w differs from v, then there exists a retained transfer t with \(s=\mathrm{some}(t)\) and \(w=t.\mathrm{result}\). The absence marker is a structural alternative; it is not a zero-valued motion carrier.

For a finite ordered transfer-option list L, define the complete succession and source ledger recursively:
\[
 F(v,[])=v,\qquad F(v,s::L)=F(S(v,s),L),
\]
\[
 Q([])=[],\quad Q(\mathrm{none}::L)=Q(L),\quad
 Q(\mathrm{some}(t)::L)=t::Q(L).
\]
Induction on L establishes \(Q(L)=[]\Rightarrow F(v,L)=v\). The empty list is reflexive. An absent-transfer successor reduces to the induction hypothesis; a present-transfer successor gives a nonempty ledger and cannot satisfy the premise. This proves preservation of the complete velocity, and hence preservation of its exact speed and held orientation. The same recursion proves
\[
 F(v,L\mathbin{+\!+}R)=F(F(v,L),R),\qquad
 Q(L\mathbin{+\!+}R)=Q(L)\mathbin{+\!+}Q(R).
\]
Ten native component theorems establish these statements with zero axiom dependencies. The original 256-form program, complete blind empirical method and four independent-validator cases also agree with V3. The inertia entry is complete following its acceleration dependency.

\[
 C(P,v)=\operatorname{map}(p\mapsto(p,v),P).

\[
 \operatorname{map}(\pi_1,C(P,v))=P,\qquad |C(P,v)|=|P|,

 (p,w)\in C(P,v)\iff p\in P\;\land\;w=v,
\]
\[
 C(P\mathbin{+\!+}Q,v)=C(P,v)\mathbin{+\!+}C(Q,v).
\]
These identities retain the order and multiplicity of every supplied occurrence. No output cell can introduce an unregistered inertial part or a different motion label. Projection recovers the complete input support; the first cell of a nonempty support recovers v, so neither source coordinate is erased.

 p=\operatorname{normalizePositive}(n_mn_u,d_md_u).

The normalization theorem proves

 (n_mn_u)d_p=n_p(d_md_u),\qquad n_p>0.

The orientation is retained directly from the complete velocity carrier. The pair-cell record retains that carrier as well as m and P; no fitted coefficient or signed magnitude is introduced. 372. Exact oriented scalar changes

The admitted scalar operations used here are the existing V3 operations in sft/mathematics/calculator/values.py. Their domain consists of structural Empty One and an exact positive rational magnitude paired with either forward-held or counter-held orientation. In particular, a stored numerical zero or negative magnitude is not added to the domain. Reversal exchanges the two orientation labels and leaves the positive magnitude unchanged; reversing twice returns the same complete scalar.

For positive magnitudes x=p/q and y=r/s, define
\[
 A=ps,\qquad B=rq,\qquad D=qs>0.
\]
When the orientations agree, addition retains that orientation and normalizes (A+B)/D. When the orientations differ, the complete comparison has three branches:
\[
 A>B:\quad(o_x,\operatorname{normalizePositive}(A-B,D)),
\]
\[
 B>A:\quad(o_y,\operatorname{normalizePositive}(B-A,D)),
\]
\[
 A=B:\quad\mathrm{EmptyOne}.
\]
Strict comparison proves the retained numerator positive in each nonempty branch. For the left-held remainder z=n_z/d_z, normalization proves
\[
 (A-B)d_z=n_zD,
\]
while exact removal reconstructs the original common support:
\[
 Bd_z+n_zD=Ad_z.
\]
The right-held branch gives the symmetric identities. The result is Empty One exactly when the cross-products coincide. Equality, left dominance and right dominance therefore exhaust the original positive-rational domain. Empty One is an additive identity, and the source subtraction is
\[
 x\mathbin{\ominus}y=x\mathbin{\oplus}\operatorname{reverse}(y).
\]
In particular, x⊖x is Empty One for every admitted scalar, including Empty One itself. Both the operation and its result retain the original held-orientation convention.

For an admitted positive forward duration t=a/b, the original division first constructs the exact reciprocal b/a and then multiplies. If the numerator magnitude is m=n/d, the resulting reduced magnitude z satisfies
\[
 (nb)d_z=n_z(da),\qquad n_z>0.
\]
Division preserves the numerator's held orientation; an Empty One numerator remains Empty One. The positive-duration type excludes division by structural absence, matching the source boundary. These statements are universal native proofs over the complete admitted scalar domain. A separate fresh execution replay compares 18,258 results with the unchanged pinned V3 operations: 51 reversals, 2,601 additions, 2,601 subtractions and 13,005 positive-duration rates, including both held orientations and exact cancellation. This finite replay checks execution correspondence; the universal arithmetic identities are established by the kernel proofs.

373. Acceleration from the complete velocity comparison

The endpoint velocities retain the displacement support, exact separation, original motion interval, reference recurrence, observation and held orientation defined in Sections 363–366. The comparison does not replace them with an answer-only rate.

The two displacement orientation labels are renamed bijectively as forward-held and counter-held for the original scalar operations. Both round-trip identities are proved. Reversing the displacement orientation corresponds exactly to scalar reversal, with the speed unchanged.

Let N>0 be the generated comparison-path transition count and K>0 the held reference recurrence count. The duration τ=n_τ/d_τ is obtained by the original exact normalization:
\[
 \tau=\operatorname{normalizePositive}(N,K),\qquad
 Nd_\tau=n_\tau K.
\]
The acceleration value is then computed, rather than supplied as an independent field:
\[
 \Delta v=v_{\mathrm{after}}\mathbin{\ominus}v_{\mathrm{before}},\qquad
 a=\Delta v\mathbin{/}\tau.
\]
The difference is the complete oriented operation of Section 372. If it is Empty One, division retains Empty One. If it is the held positive magnitude m=n_m/d_m, the reduced rate n_a/d_a retains its orientation and satisfies
\[
 (n_m d_\tau)d_a=n_a(d_m n_\tau).
\]
Together with Nd_τ=n_τK and positivity, this is exactly the generated comparison m/(N/K), without a fitted scale. An unchanged complete velocity gives Empty One by universal self-subtraction. Different endpoint carriers or different retained source/action ledgers distinguish the complete acceleration records even when a numerical projection happens to agree. The original path keeps all source-bound transitions and endpoint observations.

 W=F\mathbin{\otimes}X.

For two positive magnitudes f=n_f/d_f and x=n_x/d_x, normalization gives

 w=\operatorname{normalizePositive}(n_fn_x,d_fd_x),\qquad

The held-orientation rule is the original multiply_scalar rule: matching orientations give forward-held, and differing orientations give counter-held. Its four cases are exhaustive. Reversing one factor reverses the product orientation without changing its positive magnitude; reversing both factors preserves the product. The same admitted source arithmetic therefore handles the absence boundary without introducing a numerical zero or negative magnitude.

Thus every supplied transfer row retains the complete displacement, with its references, support, observation and orientation.  D_F=(M\cdot(L/T))/T,\qquad D_W=D_F\cdot L,

 D_E=((M\cdot L)\cdot L)/(T\cdot T).

377. Angular motion: exact phase in a retained closed recurrence

Let C be a finite observed recurrence with N > 0 source-bound transitions, returning to the same complete carrier. Its traversal retains a held orientation h. A position is an observed event together with an initial path P and remaining path Q satisfying P joined to Q = C. Consequently,

\[
\operatorname{changes}(P) ++ \operatorname{changes}(Q) = \operatorname{changes}(C)
\]
k + r = N,    k = count(P),    r = count(Q),    k ≤ N.

This decomposition retains every transition and its order. The phase magnitude at a present position is the normalized exact part k/N; its orientation is h. An initial path with no transition has structural Empty One. The terminal position has phase magnitude N/N = 1, while its observed carrier equals the starting carrier. Thus returning to the same carrier does not discard the completed traversal.

If normalize(k,N) = (u,v), Lean proves k v = u N and u ≤ v. No irrational angular unit enters this construction. For two ordered positions, the connecting observed interval I must satisfy P_before joined to I = P_after. The full interval ledger is retained, and k_before + count(I) = k_after. With a held clock recurrence of M transitions,

tau = count(I)/M,
\[
\Delta\phi = \phi_{\mathrm{after}}\mathbin{\ominus}\phi_{\mathrm{before}}
\]
\[
\omega = \operatorname{dividePositive}(\Delta\phi,\tau)
\]

The subtraction and division are the previously derived exact held-orientation scalar operations. For a present phase change of magnitude a/b and positive duration c/d, the normalized rate p/q satisfies (a d) q = p (b c); its held change orientation is preserved. The mathematical construction covers every finite admitted path decomposition, independently of the finite candidate grammar.

Here \(x\mathbin{\ominus}y=x\mathbin{\oplus}\operatorname{reverse}(y)\) is the oriented FoldScalar operation of §372; equality yields EmptyOne, and division retains that case.

379. Complete constituent weighting and the composite centre

Each constituent retains its complete momentum carrier, positive inertial content m_i and reference-relative oriented separation x_i. Every weighted term is generated by the original scalar product,

\[

The constituent list is nonempty and every m_i is positive, so M is positive. Each normalized weighted product obeys its cross-product identity. The weighting ledger stores (constituent_i,w_i) for every occurrence. Projecting its first coordinates recovers the original constituent list exactly. Composite momentum retains the disjoint ordered junction of all constituent momentum records, including repeated-valued occurrences.

A grouping is a finite tree of constituents whose junction joins both complete leaf lists. For any groups A, B and C,

The assembled complete carrier is equal under this regrouping; its weighted centre and momentum junction are consequently equal. Evaluation retains the complete leaf order throughout, so regrouping cannot omit, duplicate or silently reorder a constituent.

380. Closed mechanical transfer and exact carrier conservation

A closed interaction ledger records each transfer occurrence as (source, destination, carrier, source identity, action record). Its carrier is the entire derived momentum or energy-transfer record. Distinct occurrences remain distinct even when their carrier values agree.

For a ledger indexed by its finite occurrences I, let c_i be the retained carrier. The departure and arrival supports are

\[

C_{\mathrm{in}}=[c_i\mid i\in I].

\[
C_{\mathrm{out}} = C_{\mathrm{in}}
\]
\[
\operatorname{length}(C_{\mathrm{out}}) = \operatorname{length}(C_{\mathrm{in}})
\]
\[
F(C_{\mathrm{out}}) = F(C_{\mathrm{in}})
\]

for every aggregate F on the complete retained carriers. This establishes conservation of the complete support, not merely equality of a selected scalar total. A successor transfer appends its source, destination and full carrier without altering the earlier ledger. The result applies within V3's declared closed-transfer boundary: every recorded outgoing carrier has its recorded incoming counterpart. Source, destination and provenance remain separately distinguishable.

388. Oriented electric transport and the magnetic response record

The magnetic construction retains a complete electric charge q and an observed motion v, including both endpoints, positive separation, clock comparison and the entire source/action path. The held orientation takes two values, forward and counter, with reversal j. In particular, j(j(h)) = h. The response orientation is the same two-fibre composition used by the exact Fold scalar carrier:

\[
\mathrm{forward}\text{ composed with }\mathrm{forward}=\mathrm{forward}
\]
\[
\mathrm{forward}\text{ composed with }\mathrm{counter}=\mathrm{counter}
\]
\[
\mathrm{counter}\text{ composed with }\mathrm{forward}=\mathrm{counter}
\]
\[
\mathrm{counter}\text{ composed with }\mathrm{counter}=\mathrm{forward}
\]

Writing r(q,v) for this composition of held charge and held motion gives

\[
r(j(q),v) = j(r(q,v))
\]
\[
r(q,j(v)) = j(r(q,v))
\]
\[
r(j(q),j(v)) = r(q,v)
\]

These identities follow by all four orientation cases. Conversely, the forward/forward convention and the two separate reversal identities determine the response on every pair: the forward/counter value follows by motion reversal, the counter/forward value by charge reversal, and the counter/counter value by both. No fitted magnitude enters this determination.

The source distinguishes the along-motion role from the transverse response role. The magnetic response record retains the latter together with the transported charge, full motion and observed response. The roles remain distinct, so the response cannot be relabeled as the along-motion record. This is the original held relational description; no numerical angle or imported metric field equation enters the construction. Reversing either held orientation preserves the positive charge amount and the complete propagation path while reversing the response orientation.

For a finite response ledger R = [r_1,...,r_n], the generated ledger retains each tuple (transport_i, observation_i, role_i, held_i). Projection recovers [transport_1,...,transport_n] exactly. Appending one accessible response appends its complete tuple and preserves every preceding record. For each retained path p, projection of its complete change rows onto source/action pairs equals sourceRecords(p); the number of transitions is positive by the transported-motion boundary.

389. Linked magnetic change and complete cyclic electric work

A linked magnetic change retains the before and after response records, source identity and original change record. The closed generated boundary is an ordered recurrence p with an explicitly held traversal. Its terminal carrier equals its initial carrier. Every transition s of p retains its full observed mechanical work transfer W(s), including force and displacement, rather than only an extracted number.

If L denotes the complete linked change and h the held traversal, the cyclic record is

C(L,p,W) = [(L,s,h,W(s)) : s in changes(p)].

Projection onto the transition component yields exactly changes(p). Therefore every original boundary occurrence is present, no additional transition is admitted, and the complete source/action projection equals sourceRecords(p). Projection onto the linked-change component retains L at every occurrence, preserving the common change provenance around the entire cycle.

The induced electric interaction for each transition uses the charge q carried by the after-response of L and the complete work W(s):

\[
E_L(s) = (q,W(s))
\]
\[
\Delta V_L(s) = \operatorname{normalizeCharge}(\operatorname{energyChange}(W(s)),q)
\]

Thus no additional electric source is introduced by the cyclic construction. Both endpoints and the force/work trace remain available in W(s), and the potential operation is the previously established exact charge normalization. A different linked change or a different complete boundary gives a distinct cyclic record. The construction preserves the source's relational work correspondence without importing a differential flux equation.

J(P)=\mathop{\operatorname{concat}}_{i=1}^{n}[(s_i,e\!\to\!m),(s_i,m\!\to\!e)].

The base list is empty; appending a source occurrence adds its two retained legs. The construction records the two response families on one common propagation history, retaining their different observation roles. A changed electric interaction or changed magnetic record is distinguished by the joint carrier.

D_a ~ D_b if and only if O_a = O_b.

Equality of observable records immediately gives reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity. Arbitrarily replacing lambda preserves O and therefore preserves equivalence. pi(D_a) = pi(D_b) if and only if D_a ~ D_b.

Every observable is represented by (O,[]). Consequently a canonical representative requires neither a chosen privileged internal labeling nor a quotient axiom. The subtraction is the source's repeated positive-predecessor operation. Its general identity is predecessorSteps(r + k + 1,k) = r + 1. Boolean, nonpositive and exhausted inputs retain the original rejection boundaries; no signed proof magnitude is introduced.

395. Interaction classes from complete source, carrier and response traces

The physical signature of an interaction description is the complete ordered triple

\[
\Sigma=(\text{conserved source labels},\ \text{propagation carriers},\ \text{observable response traces})
\]

Its descriptive name remains separate. Two descriptions belong to the same class exactly when their complete signatures are equal. Names alone cannot distinguish classes: (Sigma,name_a) and (Sigma,name_b) have the same canonical signature for every pair of names.

Native equality gives reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity. Equality of the complete signatures preserves each source, propagation and response sequence. Conversely, equality of all three sequences reconstructs equality of the signature. If any of the three complete sequences differs, equivalence is excluded.

For a finite input ledger [d_1,...,d_n], the canonical occurrence ledger is [Sigma(d_1),...,Sigma(d_n)]. Every original occurrence has its canonical class present, and every output occurrence comes from an original description. Equal signatures identify the same class even when multiple original occurrences or names remain in the ledger. The construction does not discard duplicate observations or infer new interaction kinds from names. The registered PDG comparison retains the original observed-class boundary; the generic trace theorem does not assign a universal class count to arbitrary inputs.

396. Exact interior change and boundary flow

Let I(x) record whether a generated support node lies inside the held region. Every original transfer t retains its named source s(t), destination d(t), complete carrier, source identity and action record. The complete outward and inward ledgers are selected by

O = [t : I(s(t)) = true and I(d(t)) = false],
J = [t : I(s(t)) = false and I(d(t)) = true].

The membership theorems are biconditionals: a transfer occurs in O precisely when it occurs in the original network and satisfies the outward conditions; the corresponding statement holds for J. Thus no crossing is omitted or invented. Inward selection is outward selection for the complementary region, with both endpoints retained.

Let D be the number of transfers departing from an interior node and A the number arriving at an interior node. Complete finite-network induction gives

\[
D + |J| = A + |O|
\]

The proof checks all four endpoint-membership cases. An interior-to-interior transfer adds one to both D and A. An interior-to-exterior transfer adds one to D and |O|. An exterior-to-interior transfer adds one to A and |J|. An exterior-to-exterior transfer changes none of the four counts. This equality expresses continuity without introducing a negative proof magnitude.

The result retains complete carriers as well as counts. Interior losses are source-side records of O, and boundary outflow is the recipient-side record of the same O. Projection onto carriers gives exactly equal ordered lists. Interior gains and boundary inflow similarly project to the same complete carrier list from J. Source identities, actions and distinct transfer occurrences remain available throughout; equal-valued transfers are not silently merged.

397. Action and reaction as paired held transfer records

For every complete transfer t, construct the source-loss and recipient-gain records

\[
L(t) = (\operatorname{source}(t),\operatorname{carrier}(t),first,\operatorname{sourceIdentity}(t),\operatorname{action}(t))
\]
\[
G(t) = (\operatorname{destination}(t),\operatorname{carrier}(t),second,\operatorname{sourceIdentity}(t),\operatorname{action}(t))
\]

The two records retain the same full carrier and provenance, while their held roles are distinct and opposite:

\[
\operatorname{carrier}(L(t)) = \operatorname{carrier}(G(t))
\]
\[
\operatorname{held}(G(t)) = \operatorname{opposite}(\operatorname{held}(L(t)))
\]

Both named endpoints are retained. When the carrier is the previously derived full momentum record, the magnitude at each end is the same positive fraction. Opposite held roles therefore do not require a negative momentum proof quantity.

For a complete network T, the paired ledger [(L(t),G(t)) : t in T] has exactly |T| entries. Projection onto source-side carriers equals projection onto recipient-side carriers, occurrence by occurrence. Appending a transfer appends its complete pair and preserves the earlier paired history. This is the original reciprocal closed-transfer construction, including the retained motion and source records inside each momentum carrier.

398. Period and frequency from complete recurrence counts

A wave retains a closed, oriented recurrence and a complete held-reference recurrence. Let N > 0 be the wave recurrence's transition count and M > 0 the reference count. The exact period is

\[
T = \operatorname{normalize}(N,M)
\]

and frequency is its positive reciprocal f. If T has reduced numerator p and denominator q, then N q = p M. If f has reduced numerator a and denominator b, reciprocal normalization gives q b = a p. Combining the two identities and cancelling the positive p yields

\[
M b = a N
\]
\[
f = \operatorname{normalize}(M,N)
\]

Consequently the exact normalized product T f is One: its numerator and denominator are both 1. The proof holds for every positive generated recurrence/reference pair. Both period and frequency remain positive; no floating or irrational cycle value is introduced.

The recurrence's last carrier equals its first carrier. A held phase position retains an initial and remaining path whose concatenation is the complete original recurrence. Therefore the phase record preserves the full source/action history as well as the count ratio.

400. Exact wavelength, period and propagation speed

v = \lambda /T = \lambda  f

(l_n t_d) v_d = v_n (l_d t_n)
\]

All factors belong to the admitted positive domain. The reduced positive-ratio uniqueness theorem establishes that any candidate satisfying this same exact relation equals v. Thus the three-carrier closure is unique for the retained spatial and temporal repeat; it does not select a fitted speed.

The full displacement endpoints and temporal recurrence remain in the construction. 401. Complete labelled wave superposition

The source composition retains every independently generated wave trace on shared support. Write L=[l_1,...,l_m] and R=[r_1,...,r_n], where each record may carry its complete source, frequency, phase and support. The disjoint junction is

\[
J(L,R) = [\operatorname{inl}(l_1),...,\operatorname{inl}(l_m)] ++ [\operatorname{inr}(r_1),...,\operatorname{inr}(r_n)]
\]

The two projections select their own branch and remove only its injection label. Recursion on the lists gives

\[
pi_L(J(L,R)) = L,     pi_R(J(L,R)) = R
\]
\[
|J(L,R)| = |L| + |R|
\]

The injections are individually injective and have disjoint images: inl(l) cannot equal inr(r). Consequently coincident extracted values do not identify distinct source occurrences. If J(L,R)=J(L',R'), applying the two projections gives L=L' and R=R'. These reconstruction identities establish complete preservation and uniqueness of the labelled composition. No constituent is discarded, duplicated or replaced by a fitted amplitude.

402. Common-cell phase-labelled predecessor merging

Each predecessor retains its observation cell, full incoming trace, held orientation and positive exact support. Merging is defined at a shared observation cell and retains the ordered pair of complete predecessors alongside the resulting support. The support operation is the previously established exact held-scalar addition.

For positive fractions x=a/b and y=c/d, matching held labels produce

\[
x+y = (ad+cb)/(bd)
\]

reduced by the exact normalization operation. The normalized numerator N and denominator D satisfy (ad+cb)D=Nbd. For opposed labels the comparison is between the positive cross-products ad and cb. Equality closes the support distinction to EmptyOne; ad>cb retains the first held orientation with positive remainder (ad-cb)/(bd); ad<cb retains the opposite orientation with positive remainder (cb-ad)/(bd). These subtractions denote the corresponding admitted positive remainder branches, not negative scientific quantities.

Thus exact opposed closure is equivalent to ad=cb. In either unequal branch, recomposing the remainder with the smaller support reconstructs the larger support. Closure of the observed distinction does not erase either predecessor: projecting the merged observation recovers both original records and their common cell. Distinct source traces remain distinct records even when the merged support is equal.

403. Aperture selection and complete reachable-support regeneration

Let P be the complete finite list of incident propagation paths, A(p) the registered aperture decision and S(p) the generated successor list for path p. The retained paths and regenerated output are

\[
\begin{aligned}
R_A(P)&=[p\in P\mid A(p)=\mathrm{true}],\\
G_A(P)&=\operatorname{concat}_{p\in R_A(P)}[(p,q)\mid q\in S(p)].
\end{aligned}
\]

Induction on P establishes exact aperture membership:

p in R_A(P) iff p in P and A(p)=true.

The full flattened successor generation then gives both directions of

(p,q) in G_A(P) iff p in P, A(p)=true and q in S(p).

Every registered reachable successor therefore appears, and every generated output has a retained incident origin. If A(p)=false, no pair (p,q) can occur. The list construction preserves occurrence order and multiplicity, including different incident paths arriving at the same output cell.

For actual local propagation records, each output carries its complete generated path. Every transition in that path satisfies the registered adjacency relation, by induction over the propagation constructors. This supplies the locality of the regenerated support without imposing a continuum field solution or deleting source paths after their arrival cells coincide.

404. Held transverse polarization

A polarized recurrence retains the complete radiation carrier, including its joint electromagnetic response, energy, momentum, recurrence and held polarization label. Reversal changes the held polarization label and retains the other fields. With the two held orientations denoted h_1 and h_2,

\operatorname{opp}(h_1)=h_2,     \operatorname{opp}(h_2)=h_1

For the full carrier reversal R this yields R(R(p))=p. Its energy carrier, momentum carrier and recurrence are unchanged:

Because frequency is derived from that same recurrence and reference clock, f(R(p))=f(p). The transverse role extracted from the joint magnetic response is likewise unchanged. 405. Recurrence-labelled support response and dispersion

A registered support response assigns each retained recurrence label its complete spatial repeat, temporal wave, causal arrival path and phase decomposition. For a finite label list L and registered response rule r, the complete response ledger is

D(L,r) = [(ell,r(ell),v(r(ell))) | ell in L].

Every arrival path retains adjacency at each transition, and the initial and remaining phase paths concatenate to the whole original recurrence. The registered support response, rather than an added universal correction, determines the label dependence.

c_a≠c_b and n>0 imply n c_a≠n c_b.

406. Exact recurrence matching and resonance

Retain the full driver and supported recurrence paths on their common generated refinement, with positive counts a and b and their held phase labels phi_d and phi_s. The least common return is

\[
L = \operatorname{lcm} (a,b) = a (b/\gcd (a,b)) = b (a/\gcd (a,b))
\]

Both a and b divide L and L is positive. Exact phase-aligned matching at a generated return n is

Matched(n) iff n>0, a divides n, b divides n and phi_d=phi_s.

If the phases agree, L is a matched return. Every matched n is divisible by L, hence L≤n. Any positive matched return that is least among all matched returns must equal L, by the two inequalities. This proves uniqueness of the least exact refinement without a tolerance band.

If phi_d≠phi_s, Matched(n) is false for every n under that retained phase pairing. This is an exclusion of unmatched phases from coherent transfer, not erasure of the driver or supported traces. For a list N of matched returns the transfer ledger is

T(N) = [(n,driver,supported,phi_d,phi_s) | n in N].

Its length equals |N|, every row has equal held phase labels, and appending a matched return appends exactly one complete transfer record while preserving all prior records. The original recurrence paths remain in every row, so repeated aligned transfer carries its full source correspondence.

407. Wave energy and held momentum along a causal path

A transported wave retains its full radiation carrier K, source event s, remote arrival event r, complete adjacent propagation path P, held propagation orientation h and source action record. The momentum orientation is the retained path orientation. The closed transfer is

(s,r,K,sourceIdentity,actionRecord).

E_{\mathrm{loss}}=E_{\mathrm{gain}},     W_{\mathrm{loss}}=W_{\mathrm{gain}},     M_{\mathrm{loss}}=M_{\mathrm{gain}}

The accounting roles are opposed while the transported momentum remains the original held carrier. Every transition q along P is recorded with (q,K,h). Projecting these records recovers the complete transition list of P, and each row retains K and h. Every path transition satisfies the original adjacency relation.

For an arbitrary finite network of these transports, the outgoing and incoming carrier lists are equal occurrence by occurrence:

\[
\operatorname{outgoingSupport}(network)=\operatorname{incomingSupport}(network)
\]

This conservation identity retains the full energy and momentum records at both ends and along the causal path. It does not replace them with independently assigned endpoint scalars. Remote work is thereby paired with its corresponding source transfer and transported recurrence.

408. Physical quantum support and preparation

The physical state retains the admitted Fold state: a finite list of distinct words with held phase labels, together with the original nontrivial phase cycle. For generated alphabet A and position list P, the original complete-support operation supplies

support(state) = words(A,|P|).

R = [((w,phi),s,H) | (w,phi) in state.branches].

Projection onto the first field recovers state.branches exactly. Projection of any row onto its source and preparation fields yields s and H. A changed source identity or preparation trace distinguishes the complete physical state even when an extracted word support agrees. 409. Closed reversible physical evolution

Closed evolution uses the original admitted gates and their successful applications. A gate carries its finite one-to-one word map and generated phase-successor trace. Let G=[g_1,...,g_n] be the actual gate schedule, S_0 the prepared state, S_n the terminal state, and H the retained predecessor-state list.

Induction over the successful application trace constructs the backward derivation using the same gates in reverse order and their original inverse operations:

Forward(S_0,G,H,S_n) implies Backward(S_n,reverse(G),S_0).

Each inverse application reconstructs the preceding full word-and-phase state. The same induction proves

\[
|H|=|G|,\qquad|\operatorname{branches}(S_n)|=|\operatorname{branches}(S_0)|
\]

The complete branch correspondence is stronger than a count identity:

b in S_n.branches iff there exists a in S_0.branches with BranchTrace(cycle,G,a,b).

Thus every final branch has an actual original predecessor trace, and every branch generated by that trace is retained. The physical evolution record additionally holds the original source identity and full preparation. Reversibility does not discard phase action or reconstruct an answer-only support.


The registered empirical protocol for this entry uses its separate exact action/energy relation. For positive input intervals A=[a_l,a_u] and E=[e_l,e_u], the capability-closed program predicts

\[
T=[a_l/e_u,a_u/e_l]
\]

The eight original instructions read the four endpoints, form the two ordered quotients, pair them and emit the interval. The external action and energy inscriptions are parsed as exact rational measurement records; an official decimal prefix is bounded by its next decimal place and the original uncertainty is retained. The duration target remains committed until the prediction is sealed.

The current pinned comparison yields

\]

The exact overlap test is not(t_u < o_l or o_u < t_l). It accepts this released target interval and rejects the displaced control [t_u+1,t_u+2]. All input, program, output, trace, custody and receipt hashes retain the original source protocol. These measured correspondence inputs remain separate from the preceding native reversible-evolution derivation.
