523. Periodic recurrence: complete outer traces and counted return

The periodic recurrence entry retains the complete generated outer support at each atomic-number coordinate. For a prepared boundary p and generated trace family G, the admitted support is
  S(p,G) = {t in G : phaseAction(p,t) = p}.
Each retained transition has both endpoints in S(p,G). The existing finite-recurrence theorem supplies admission when the generated trace completes the held orientation cycle. The occupation record preserves exchange traces: identical constituent words in the same cell cannot satisfy the alternating exchange condition, because exchanging that pair fixes it while the opposite held orientation differs from itself. Thus the outer carrier retains the finite boundary closure and exclusion derivations already established in the quantum construction.

Let O be the complete registered family of outer chemical observations and let L_O(a) = [f(a) : f in O] retain every full transition trace. The equivalence relation is
  a ~_O b  iff  for every f in O, f(a) = f(b).
Induction over O proves both directions of
  a ~_O b  iff  L_O(a) = L_O(b).
The empty observation list contributes no distinction; adjoining an observation requires its equality together with equality of every previously held observation. Reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity follow componentwise. Equivalent representatives therefore define the same complete class. Any relation preserving all registered observations factors through this equivalence; no additional class rule is introduced.

At atomic-number coordinates Z(a) and Z(b), the return condition and its counted period are
  R_O(a,b) iff Z(a) < Z(b) and a ~_O b,
  P(a,b) = Z(b) - Z(a).
For every return, P(a,b) > 0 and P(a,b) + Z(a) = Z(b). The earlier complete class and the ordered successor distance jointly determine the witness; an assumed fixed period cannot replace the trace-equality test. A changed registered trace rejects the proposed return.

The complete finite search examines earlier records in their held order. At each record it tests the strict coordinate order and equality of the complete observation ledger. The first successful test returns that earlier record; otherwise it continues through the remaining records. Induction proves that a returned record belongs to the history and satisfies R_O, and that an empty result is equivalent to the absence of a return at every earlier record. Consequently every successor either closes a witnessed return or extends the nonreturning trace. Appending the successor retains every earlier pair of records and its return witness. The ordered-history binding identifies the outer records with the existing atomic-number successor sequence.

  g(a) = [a]_O,

  Z(a) < Z(b), L_O(a) = L_O(b),

The joint coordinate is (g(a),d(H)); its computable class representation is (L_O(a),d(H)). Both components are retained with the complete element record.

525. Valence: attained maximum of complete joining and substitution support

The carrier is a retained atom or chemical fragment together with its declared chemical context. Every generated trace records whether it is a combination or substitution, its univalent partners and its source trace.   n(t) = 1 + |partners_rest(t)| > 0.

  select(p,t) = t if n(p) < n(t), and p otherwise.
The running maximum follows the original enumeration in order:
  M(p,[]) = p,
  M(p,t::R) = M(select(p,t),R).
This preserves the earlier witness on a tie and replaces it exactly when the fresh realized count is greater.

Induction over the remaining support proves that M(t_0,R) belongs to t_0::R and that
  for every t in t_0::R, n(t) <= n(M(t_0,R)).
The result is therefore an attained maximum, not an imported or typical count. If another retained witness u also bounds the entire support, the two inequalities imply
  n(u) = n(M(t_0,R)).
The numerical valence is unique even when more than one trace realizes it. A proposed typical count smaller than a realized member contradicts the maximum bound and is rejected.

For an appended generated trace f, induction gives the exact successor equation
  M(t_0,R ++ [f]) = select(M(t_0,R),f),
  V(R ++ [f]) = n(f) if V(R) < n(f), and V(R) otherwise.
Appending preserves the complete earlier support, carrier and context. Combination and substitution use the same retained boundary and comparison carrier; no context-free value or correction is introduced.

526. Ion formation: closed transfer and held net orientation

The chemical carrier remains an atom or a molecular record with retained constituent nuclei and chemical identity. Each electric transfer records an incoming or outgoing direction, a held fibre label, its source identity and its full action trace. It creates one edge between the particle and its boundary. The same held label occurs at both ends of that edge. Applying the existing complete network conservation theorem yields equality of the full outgoing and incoming label supports, including multiplicities and source records.

Net accounting uses two natural tallies A and B, with cancellation represented by comparison rather than a signed proof magnitude. An incoming first-fibre transfer contributes to A and an incoming second-fibre transfer to B. An outgoing transfer contributes to the opposite tally. For a transfer t, write h(t) for its incoming held label or the opposite label when outgoing. The exact update is
  add((A,B),first) = (A+1,B),
  add((A,B),second) = (A,B+1),
  account(c,[]) = c,
  account(c,t::R) = account(add(c,h(t)),R).
Every contribution therefore has a paired boundary edge; it is not unpaired charge creation.

The net result is determined completely by the two tallies:
  net(A,B) = first-held with magnitude A-B when B<A;
  net(A,B) = second-held with magnitude B-A when A<B;
  net(A,B) = neutral when A=B.
The existing subtraction induction proves that the retained difference is positive in either charged branch. Antisymmetry of the natural order proves the converse neutral criterion. Thus an ion is exactly a carrier whose accounted tallies differ. The two one-unmatched-label bases, (1,0) and (0,1), establish the two held orientations; the empty tally is bookkeeping, not a negative proof quantity.

Induction over the complete transfer history establishes
  account(c,R ++ [t]) = add(account(c,R),h(t)).
The next charge state is the net classification of this exact updated pair. Appending retains the chemical carrier and every prior transfer. For an atomic carrier, the existing electron-change theorem explicitly preserves proton count: Z(changeElectrons(a,e)) = Z(a). Molecular constituent nuclei and the molecular identity record remain in the unchanged carrier. A transfer can also neutralize a carrier; the ion predicate follows the resulting tally equality rather than assuming permanent ion status.

The original grammar enumerates all 256 products of the eight ion axes, retaining the two held fibres, positive count domain, original eliminations, unique survivor and identity/conservation/signed controls. 527. Known periodic boundary: complete release census and extensible endpoint

The known periodic boundary retains a complete atomic-number successor sequence together with the release date, source identifier, source hash and extraction trace. Each row carries its element, isotope and source records. Let R be the complete sequence and z its last coordinate. The established successor construction gives
  Z(first) = 1,
  Z(next) = Z(prior)+1,
  |R| = Z(last) = z.
Induction proves that the final row belongs to R and every listed row r satisfies Z(r) <= z. The endpoint is therefore attained within the complete census. If another listed row bounds all rows, antisymmetry gives its coordinate equal to z; the greatest listed coordinate is unique.

A new officially validated row with coordinate z+1 extends the retained sequence:
  R' = R ++ [r_new],
  z' = z+1.
Every prior element row remains in R'. Since z < Z(r_new), the old upper-bound theorem proves that r_new is absent from R; the extension construction proves that it belongs to R'. This establishes precisely why absence beyond one release does not supply a theorem of impossibility. Source date and source identity remain explicit metadata of each release, rather than a terminal scientific rule.

The source's 256 grammar alternatives retain complete census, greatest listed coordinate, element identity, date, all rows, open successor, source trace and no-extra-rule axes. 528. Exact chemical composition: identity-bearing positive partition of One

Each composition component retains an identity and an ExactPart. The identity must contain a non-whitespace character; surrounding whitespace is preserved rather than used to merge distinct labels. The part is a reduced rational n/d with 0<n<=d and d>0. Thus a present component has a positive part, while an absent component is omitted from the support.

For the complete ordered component family C, the native operation preserves V3's two admission stages. First C must be nonempty and its identities distinct. Second its exact sum must equal One. No normalization correction is applied. Using an exact numerator/denominator accumulator, the initial arithmetic state is (N,D)=(0,1), and each component n/d updates it by
  N' = N d + n D,
  D' = D d.
Consequently N'/D' = N/D + n/d. Induction over the component list gives the exact total; closure is N=D. The existing positive-part partition proofs connect this same natural-number accumulation to the rational partition operation. The bookkeeping numerator at the initial empty sum is not a present zero-valued chemical component.

The complete admission condition is therefore
  accept(C) iff C is nonempty, every identity is distinct, and N(C)=D(C).
On acceptance the output is exactly C. Empty or duplicate support is rejected before the closure test; a nonclosing exact sum is rejected without altering any part. Equality of two part values does not imply equality of their constituent identities. The original Python operation and the native Lean operation agree on the source witness (A,1/3),(B,2/3), equal-part distinct labels, duplicate identities, underfilled and overfilled totals, blank and Unicode-whitespace identities, distinct whitespace/case-sensitive labels, and large exact fractions.

For a parent p and positive subparts a,b, exact splitting is the cross-product identity
  (n_a d_b + n_b d_a)d_p = n_p d_a d_b.
The previously proved partition refinement theorem implies
  sum(B ++ [p] ++ T)=1  implies  sum(B ++ [a,b] ++ T)=1.
If the refined component identities are distinct, the chemical operation therefore accepts the refined complete support. A singleton component equal to One supplies the base. Induction over the typed finite refinement history proves closure after every finite sequence of such splits. The source boundary is retained, and the parent component list is appended to the provenance history, preserving the identities and part records from which the refinement was derived.

The original eight-axis grammar retains all 256 alternatives, exact eliminations, unique survivor, closure and one-closure/identity/zero controls. Its sealed consequence is compared only afterward with the registered IUPAC M03722 observation through the original generated_law.py validator. The original candidate program, independent adverse cases and every empirical validation field/hash are checked separately from the general composition and refinement proofs.

529. Elemental conservation through a complete reaction word

A reaction species retains a structural reactant/product side, a nonblank chemical identity, a positive multiplicity, and a nonempty list of distinct elemental identities with positive counts. The source side-family, side-label, identity and elemental-support guards are preserved. Every named boundary carrier must be present in this same complete word; there is no unrecorded correction to the totals.

For an element label e, the formula count of species s is
  E_e(s) = sum over its elemental rows (a,n) of n when a=e, and zero otherwise.
With positive species coefficient c_s, the total on held side q is
  T_q(e,W) = sum over s in W with side(s)=q of c_s E_e(s).
The zero in this accounting expression represents absence from the named support, not a participating species with a zero coefficient. All participating multiplicities remain positive.

The native dictionary operation follows the original ordered accumulation. For each matching-side species, it multiplies each formula count by the species coefficient, adds the contribution to an existing element key, or inserts that key at its first occurrence. The lookup proof first establishes
  lookup(e,addCount(a,n,D)) = lookup(e,D) + (n if a=e, else 0).
Induction over elemental rows then gives
  lookup(e,accumulateElements(c,F,D)) = lookup(e,D) + c E_e(F).
Induction over the species word yields
  lookup(e,sideTotalsFrom(q,W,D)) = lookup(e,D) + T_q(e,W).
Thus the actual source dictionary accumulation is connected to the per-element conservation theorem, rather than being replaced by a separately asserted balance label. Unknown side names produce an empty dictionary, as in the source operation.

Let L(W) contain every elemental label in every retained species formula. The finite checker tests T_reactant(e,W)=T_product(e,W) for every e in L(W). The proof also covers every label not in that list: induction over the complete word shows that both totals are zero there. Consequently
  checkAll(L(W)) iff for every element label e, T_reactant(e,W)=T_product(e,W).
Combined with the exact side and nonempty guards,
  reaction_is_balanced(W) iff W is nonempty, both held sides occur, and every elemental total agrees.
An unequal total at any element therefore rejects the word, even if other elements or a bulk mass comparison agree.

An identity-preserving pair consists of one species and the same identity, formula and positive coefficient on the opposite held side. It contributes equal amounts to both totals. Exact list composition gives
  T_q(e,W ++ V) = T_q(e,W) + T_q(e,V).
Hence appending such a paired carrier to a closed word preserves equality for every e. The complete prior word remains retained. This provides the source base and successor closure while preserving the original species/formula records.

Fresh native execution agrees with V3's ReactionSpecies guards, both complete side dictionaries and reaction_is_balanced on 16 cases. These include the original AB + A to A2B witness, removal of its product, unbalanced labels, changed coefficients, reordered source words, duplicate or blank elemental labels, empty support, invalid side/family, and large exact counts. The original 256 grammar alternatives, decisions, closure, operational controls and independent adverse cases are retained. The post-seal IUPAC S06026 comparator uses the original generated_law.py validator and is checked against every original output field and hash.

530. Positive stoichiometric coefficients and primitive reduction

A reaction word retains each species identity, its reactant/product side, its element-count map and its positive integer multiplicity. For multiplicities c₁,…,cₙ, the original common-factor reduction is the fold
  g₁=c₁,  gⱼ₊₁=gcd(gⱼ,cⱼ₊₁),  g=gₙ.
Every cⱼ is positive, so g>0. Induction through the gcd fold proves both g∣cⱼ for every participating species and d∣g whenever d divides all cⱼ. Thus the reduced multiplicities pⱼ=cⱼ/g are positive integers and cⱼ=g pⱼ. Species identity, orientation and formula remain unchanged.

For any element label e, let aⱼ(e) be its retained count in species j. The total on side s is Tₛ(e;c)=Σⱼ:side(j)=s cⱼaⱼ(e). Substituting cⱼ=g pⱼ gives Tₛ(e;c)=g Tₛ(e;p). A balanced input satisfies g Tᵣ(e;p)=g Tₚ(e;p); cancellation of the positive g proves balance of the reduced word for every element label. The nonempty and both-side guards are preserved as well.

The gcd scaling identity gives gcd(c₁,…,cₙ)=g gcd(p₁,…,pₙ). Since the left side is g and g>0, cancellation yields gcd(p₁,…,pₙ)=1. This connects the reduction directly to V3's primitive_coefficients acceptance test: the reduced word is balanced and its common factor is One.

For any positive integer k, gcd(kc₁,…,kcₙ)=k g, and
  (k cⱼ)/(k g)=cⱼ/g=pⱼ.
Consequently all common rescalings have the same primitive representative. If a primitive vector and its common multiple are both primitive, their gcds give k·1=1, hence k=1. This is the source's explicit unique-up-to-common-multiple construction. Only participating positive multiplicities occur; side is retained structurally rather than encoded by signed counts.

The extension retains the same conditions on the entire enlarged word. Whenever the enlarged positive word balances all element constraints, the same gcd construction supplies its primitive representative. An unbalanced extension is rejected by the original balance guard. No new balancing exception or empirical adjustment enters that reduction.

The entry's eight original binary axes retain all 256 alternatives: formula-bound support, held positive sides, element balance, primitive scale, omitted nonparticipants, uniqueness under common rescaling, retained formula/reduction trace and extension without an extra rule. The original entry experiment and independent validator retain their original controls and empirical boundary.

531. Limiting component: complete tied support and consumption boundary

For each participating input j, let its exact available share be aⱼ=nⱼ/dⱼ and its positive required multiplicity be cⱼ. Its progress boundary is
  rⱼ=aⱼ/cⱼ=nⱼ/(dⱼcⱼ).
All denominators and numerators are positive. The existing exact normalization preserves this rational value. Comparison therefore uses integer cross-products: rᵢ≤rⱼ if and only if nᵢdⱼcⱼ≤nⱼdᵢcᵢ. The native order proof connects these cross-products to the normalized exact-part order; no rounding or tolerance occurs.

For a nonempty finite ratio word, define m(r₁)=r₁ and m(r₁,…,rₖ)=min(r₁,m(r₂,…,rₖ)). Induction proves that m is a member of the original word and m≤rⱼ for every j. The output is the complete ordered position list L={j:rⱼ=m}, with positions generated from One. The membership theorem proves both directions:
  j∈L  ⇔  rⱼ≤rᵢ for every participating input i.
Thus every limiting tie is retained, no nonleast input is selected, L is nonempty and each returned position is positive. V3's nonempty-input and equal-length guards remain unchanged.

Write an extent as t=u/v with u,v>0. Its admissibility at input j is exactly
  u dⱼ cⱼ ≤ nⱼ v.
At the maximal admitted extent t=m, equality holds at every limiting carrier, so its remaining amount is empty. For every nonlimiting carrier strict inequality gives the retained positive remainder numerator nⱼv−u dⱼcⱼ over the positive denominator dⱼv. Exceeding the least ratio reverses the bound for a limiting input and would require unavailable matter; the native rejection proof makes that boundary explicit.

Appending a new ratio r preserves an old least row precisely when it also satisfies the new comparison. Formally,
  (x≤y for every y∈R++[r]) ⇔ ((x≤y for every y∈R) and x≤r).
Together with the complete-position theorem, this yields the source successor rule: old minima survive a larger appended ratio, a tied appended ratio joins the full tied support, and a smaller appended ratio replaces the earlier limiting set. Original row positions remain the output order, rather than a preference that resolves ties.

536. Covalent sharing: one retained channel, two nuclear access records

  access(c,left) = e(c) = access(c,right).

The channel collection retains an exchange trace for every pair i<j; this is not a selected subset of pairs. The singleton base has no distinct pair to check. The check therefore implements the source's exclusion of cycles between distinguishable classes. Equal observed classes already supply both tie edges, so under this check

  a.atom E* b.atom and b.atom E* a.atom ⇔ ℓa=ℓb
    ⇔ distinguishable(O,a.symbol,b.symbol)=false.

cyclesExactlySourceClasses and sourceTieExactly prove these equivalences.

Define the induced relation between held class labels by

  x ≼ y ⇔ ∃a,b∈C, ℓa=x, ℓb=y and a.atom E* b.atom.

Reflexivity follows by choosing the same endpoint representative twice and using the identity path. For transitivity, suppose a→*b witnesses x≼y and c→*d witnesses y≼z. Since ℓb=ℓc=y, the generated tie edge b→c joins the two paths, yielding a→*d and hence x≼z. For antisymmetry, take witnesses a→*b for x≼y and c→*d for y≼x. The ties b→c and d→a give b→*a. The cycle check then forces ℓa=ℓb and therefore x=y. These proofs derive the class-order laws from E, rather than taking an independently chosen class order as a premise.

Changing representatives does not change this relation. If ℓa=ℓa′ and ℓb=ℓb′, tie edges connect a with a′ and b with b′ in both directions. Prepending and appending these paths gives

  a.atom E* b.atom ⇔ a′.atom E* b′.atom.

representativeIndependent proves this equivalence directly.

The executable direction first tests class equality, then forward reachability, then reverse reachability, retaining an incomparable outcome if neither path exists. forwardForcesSecond and backwardForcesFirst prove the two strict cases. The latter uses the cycle condition to exclude a simultaneous forward path for unequal classes. tiedDirectionExactly proves that the tie outcome occurs exactly when the observed labels agree.

For an original comparison record c∈B whose first and second endpoint names match a and b, its edge e(c) occurs in E. Consequently the pair cannot be incomparable. recordDirection proves the exact result:

  direction(a,b) = tied,                         if ℓa=ℓb;
                 first,                        if ℓa≠ℓb and c.preference=c.first;
                 second,                       otherwise.

The base source comparison supplies its retained orientation. This result proves its propagation through the complete relation and exact tie class; it does not introduce a separate predictor for the source witness's atom names.

591. Organic reaction families: minimal directed changes and complete equivalence classes

A complete generated reaction retains all carrier placements and all changed relations. For a local relation row r=(ℓ,s_in,s_out), define its change predicate and the minimal transition trace by
\[

\[
A\sim B\iff
(\forall r\in P(A),r\in P(B))\land

\]
The relation is reflexive, symmetric and transitive. \]

602. Mass-spectral composition correspondence

For each generated ion carrier, retain its complete atomic composition and isotope records, its charge orientation and positive charge magnitude q, and its source-bound positive mass m. The isotope-to-atom map equals the carrier's entire constituent list; consequently every constituent has its retained isotope record and every isotope record belongs to that carrier. The ion state supplies the charge: charge(state) = charged(orientation,q), so its non-neutrality follows from the existing charge construction.

Write m = a/b and the normalized charge magnitude as q = c/d, with all four counts positive. Its mass-to-charge position is the normalized positive quotient
    x = m/q = (a d)/(b c).
Normalization preserves the exact equality
    (a d) denominator(x) = numerator(x) (b c).
For two response rows i and j, equality of their response classes is decided by
    numerator(x_i) denominator(x_j)
      = numerator(x_j) denominator(x_i).
Thus the decision retains exact rational class identity. Each row also retains its positive counted abundance n_i and source record. The complete response trace is the ordered map [(x_i,n_i)] of all carrier rows. Forward and reverse membership proofs establish both retention of every input row's response and provenance of every resulting response.

For a represented class anchored at row a, its total count is
    N_a(R) = sum over i in R of [x_a = x_i] n_i.
The empty sum is zero. Appending row j gives the derived recurrence
    N_a(R ++ [j]) = N_a(R) + [x_a = x_j] n_j.
Hence a matching class increases by its recorded abundance, while every nonmatching class remains unchanged. Since an anchor row belongs to its own class and has positive abundance, N_a(R) is positive whenever a is represented. For any two represented classes, their relative abundance is therefore the exact positive ratio N_a(R)/N_b(R); normalization preserves this ratio by cross multiplication.

A spectrum retains the complete carrier rows, precursor-fragment origin records, ionization method, conditions and instrument record. Each origin record binds both complete endpoint records to the carrier support. The one-carrier base has exactly one response pair. Carrier extension preserves the entire earlier trace and appends the new pair. Fragment extension additionally appends its origin record, with the precursor already retained. In both cases
    trace(R ++ [j]) = trace(R) ++ [(x_j,n_j)].
Every earlier origin remains present after fragment extension. A decomposition path is either one retained precursor-fragment link or a retained path followed by a link whose precursor equals the preceding endpoint. Induction on these constructors proves that every path step belongs to the origin ledger and that extending the ledger preserves the exact earlier path record. Fragment extension preserves the method, conditions and instrument record unchanged.

The original eight binary grammar axes generate 2^8 = 256 alternatives. Their original elimination decisions, operational witnesses, controls, registration and closure accompany this derivation. The source's empirical correspondence retains mass/charge separation, relative abundance, composition-fragment correspondence and the ionization-method boundary.

603. Infrared recurrence and molecular distinction

The retained molecule consists of its admitted bonded carrier and complete relative-orientation record. Each internal state retains its recurrence, displacement record, interaction trace and source record. A transition retains both molecular states, the incident recurrence, counted response and provenance. Its endpoints belong to the declared molecular-state support. This preserves the original source's paired-transition domain and observation boundary.

Let R be the complete ordered list of registered transitions. For a transition t, write d_-(t) and d_+(t) for its predecessor and successor interaction traces. The coupling decision is exact:
    c(t) = true if and only if d_-(t) ≠ d_+(t).
The visible support and retained non-coupled support are
    V(R) = [t in R | d_-(t) ≠ d_+(t)],
    U(R) = [t in R | d_-(t) = d_+(t)].
Equality decidability gives the two exhaustive cases for every registered transition. Their supports are disjoint: membership in both would assert equality and its negation. No isolated line substitutes for the complete pattern: the comparison evaluates equality of the full ordered list of normalized frequency numerators, denominators and counted responses. Its Boolean result is proved equivalent to equality of those complete signatures; it does not assert that one shared line determines molecular identity.

604. Electronic absorption and molecular-state distinction

    G(r) = r · r.

    (a d) denominator(f) = numerator(f) (b c).
Multiplication by the generated boundary growth reconstructs the original source. In cross-product form,
    numerator(f) c b = a denominator(f) d,
which is the preceding quotient identity with its finite products reassociated. Uniqueness of normalized positive ratios therefore establishes

The proof applies to every positive source and generated exact positive growth value. 613. Complete three-direction composition derivation of the oscillator closure

Let n=r-1 be the retained excitation multiplicity through positive shell rank r. Natural coordinates encode occurrence multiplicities along the three labelled directions; an empty coordinate is an empty direction, not a supplied scientific scalar. The exact-shell and filled supports are
    T_n = {(a,b,c) : a+b+c=n},
    F_n = {(a,b,c) : a+b+c<=n}.
The complete two-direction partitions separate the empty first direction from the positive first direction:
    P_0=[(0,0)],
    P_(n+1)=[(0,n+1)] followed by [(a+1,b) : (a,b) in P_n].
The same disjoint construction gives
    T_0=[(0,0,0)],
    T_(n+1)=[(0,b,c) : (b,c) in P_(n+1)]
             followed by [(a+1,b,c) : (a,b,c) in T_n],
    F_0=T_0,    F_(n+1)=F_n followed by T_(n+1).
Soundness and completeness prove both displayed support equalities for every n. The successor branches cannot overlap because their first coordinates are respectively empty and positive; distinctness is preserved within each branch. Successive shells are disjoint because their excitation totals differ. Each admissible spatial composition therefore occurs exactly once.

Writing p_n=|P_n| and t_n=|T_n|, induction gives
    p_n=n+1,    t_0=1,    t_(n+1)=t_n+n+2,
    2t_n=(n+1)(n+2).
Both exclusion-distinct Fold labels occur once on every spatial composition. The complete labelled filled-support count C_n obeys
    C_0=2,    C_(n+1)=C_n+2t_(n+1)
                       =C_n+(n+2)(n+3).
The base identity 3C_0=1*2*3 and successor calculation
    3C_(n+1)=(n+1)(n+2)(n+3)+3(n+2)(n+3)
             =(n+2)(n+3)(n+4)
prove 3C_n=(n+1)(n+2)(n+3) at every depth. Consequently
    C_(r-1)=r(r+1)(r+2)/3.
The native proof establishes exact divisibility: the original oscillator operation's divisibility guard passes for every positive rank and its quotient equals the complete labelled support. The complete-state membership theorem is
    ((a,b,c),label) in labelled(F_n) iff a+b+c<=n

615. Exact atomic coordinate boundary from the derived fine-structure ratio

The atomic-boundary operation uses the already derived terminal ratio A=N/D=503846395469/3676744786. The source's One binding ceiling admits a positive whole coordinate k precisely when k/A<=1, equivalently kD<=N. No measured element endpoint enters A or the quotient construction.
For any positive exact ratio n/d at least One, Euclidean division gives
    n=dq+t,    q=n div d,    0<=t<d.
Here the host remainder t records either empty remainder or a positive retained part. Therefore
    qd<=n<(q+1)d.
Since n>=d, the quotient is positive: division removes the first denominator and gives q=(n-d) div d+1. Thus all original post-division checks succeed on the admitted domain. The operation rejects non-Fraction inputs and fractions below One before division. For each later coordinate k>q,
    n<(q+1)d<=kd.
If another whole coordinate j satisfied both jd<=n and n<(j+1)d, j<q would contradict the lower quotient bound, and j>q would contradict its own lower bound. Hence j=q. This is a successor-general greatest-whole certificate, with no upper search bound.
Applied to the existing terminal AlphaRatio operation, the quotient returns 137. The exact bounding products are
    137*3676744786=503714035682<=503846395469,
    138*3676744786=507390780468>503846395469.
The remainder is 132359787. Every k>=138 is excluded by the preceding arbitrary-coordinate inequality, not by a finite scan.

618. Material identity and retained extension records

The material-system obligation requires the constituent carrier, composition and bonding organization, and declared observation boundary to remain distinguishable. The retained-record argument makes explicit why erasing one required distinction cannot provide the same identity. Write R=(C,B,d,O), where C is the retained sequence of chemical constitution/isotope/context records, B the named bonding records, d the declared boundary, and O the observation/reference pairs. For this record,
    R=R' iff C=C' and B=B' and d=d' and O=O'.
Consequently any identification relation preserving all four coordinates implies record equality. Conversely, equality of the four coordinates suffices: the record introduces no additional identity test. If an encoding e collapses two unequal records and a recovery map q reconstructs both, then
    R=q(e(R))=q(e(R'))=R',
contradicting their retained distinction.

A constituent, relation or observation extension appends its record to the corresponding sequence and holds the other coordinates fixed. With E_x the extension and P_x removal of its final appended coordinate,
    P_x(E_x(R))=R.
Thus E_x(R)=E_x(R') implies R=R'. For a finite extension history h=[x_1,...,x_n], define E_h by successive extension and P_h by removing those extensions in reverse order. The induction is
    P_[](E_[](R))=R,
    P_(x::h)(E_(x::h)(R))=P_x(P_h(E_h(E_x(R))))=P_x(E_x(R))=R.
It follows that arbitrary finite histories retain every earlier constituent, bonding and observation record, keep d fixed, preserve nonempty constituent support, and cannot merge initially distinct records. Each retained constituent carries its complete chemical constitution, isotope and context; the proof does not impose uniform composition across different constituents.

The separate original candidate grammar has eight binary preservation coordinates: carrier, relation, organization, observation, record, provenance, generality and extension. Its literal Cartesian product contains 2^8=256 alternatives. Acceptance requires the admitted value on every coordinate; therefore the all-admitted tuple is the unique survivor. Exhaustion and each rejected-coordinate elimination are proved for the original product. The native program reproduces every pinned candidate, decision, control, closure, registration field and hash, and the original independent validator accepts the result and rejects the three adverse cases.

Original sources: pinned sft/materials/obligations.py, MATERIALS_OBLIGATIONS[0]; sft/materials/derivation.py, _dimensions, _blueprint and blueprint_candidate_ids; sft/materials/generated_law.py, GeneratedEmpiricalMaterialsProgram. Native verification: SFT/Materials/MaterialIdentity.lean, identityExactly, leastRequiredIdentity, priorExact, finiteExtensionInjective and erasedIdentityCannotRecover; MaterialRetention.lean, historyRecovery, finiteConstituentRetention, finiteBondRetention, finiteObservationRetention and completeConstituentIdentity; MaterialGrammar.lean, candidatesComplete, uniqueSurvivor and acceptanceIffExactCriteria; MaterialEvidence.lean, original program records. 619. Material composition, finite closure and sealed authority correspondence

The constituent record retains both chemical identity and exact composition. Write c_i=(I_i,q_i), where I_i holds constitution, isotope and required chemical context, and q_i is the exact composition record supplied by the chemical dependency. A material carrier is
    M=([c_1,...,c_n],B,d,O), n>0,
with complete constituent support, bonding records B, declared boundary d and observation/reference records O. No condition q_i=q_j is imposed across different constituents. The source-bound conversion from a Substance constituent preserves its identity and composition separately. Equality of two constituent records is equivalent to equality of both I and q. Equality of carriers requires equality of the four retained coordinates. Thus any relation preserving those coordinates implies the same identity, while the coordinates themselves suffice without another identity rule.

Appending a constituent preserves all earlier pairs (I_i,q_i); appending a bonding record preserves the full earlier bonding sequence; appending an observation preserves its earlier reference pairs. For each extension E_x, removing its last appended coordinate gives P_x(E_x(M))=M. Reversing a finite extension history gives P_h(E_h(M))=M by induction. Every earlier constituent, composition, bonding relation and observation consequently remains available, the declared boundary remains fixed, and nonempty support remains nonempty. A supposed equality E_h(M)=E_h(N) would imply M=N after applying P_h, so extension cannot erase an earlier distinction.

621. Generated subshell support and first occupation

For joint-cover bound B, the generated support is C_B = [(p,o): 1≤p, 1≤o≤p, p+o≤B], traversed by increasing joint cover and then principal rank, as specified by the original nested loops. At a fixed cover c, the loop retains exactly the principal indices p with 0<p<c and c−p≤p and emits (p,c−p). Thus every emitted cell satisfies p+o=c. Conversely, any positive pair with o≤p and p+o=c appears at its principal index p. Induction on B, using C_(B+1)=C_B concatenated with the cells of cover B+1, proves completeness over the entire stated support.

Every principal index occurs once within its cover. Different covers cannot share a cell: an earlier cell has p+o≤B, whereas a new cell has p+o=B+1. Therefore the generated support contains no repeated cell. These arguments apply to every natural bound B, not just the atomic endpoint used by the source operation.

The capacity of orbit rank o=n+1 is the upstream generated value q(o)=2(1+2n). For a remaining occupation R, filling emits min(R,q(o)) and passes R−min(R,q(o)) to the next cell, stopping when this remainder is zero. The implementation uses the admitted endpoint to generate C_(2·137); it does not add an atomic-number guard at 137. The source comparison includes every atom1–137, larger inputs, closure prefixes and rejection cases. All 266 compared cases agree with pinned V3.

For the first-occupation scan, successful return of n yields an exact decomposition S=P concatenated with [n] concatenated with T. Occupation at n is nonempty, and occupation at every member of P is empty. This follows by induction over the scan: an empty occupation passes to the suffix; a nonempty occupation returns the head. 622. G-block derivation: ordered support, conserved filling and closed predictions

The ordering is explicit. For cells a=(p,o) and b=(p',o'), write a≺b when p+o<p'+o', or when p+o=p'+o' and p<p'. 625. Specimen: source-bound sampling and retained preparation

The base specimen has one source-bound row: R₁=(M,[s],[],B). Its sampled length is One, and σ(R₁)=[c]. A nonempty sample also forces M to be nonempty, since its first row supplies a constituent of M. The empty sample is excluded by the same positive-carrier condition.

627. Material phase: connected recurrence and symmetry classes

At declared conditions, let G be the retained support graph and R(x) the existing ordered-region record associated with a support cell x. The established stable-observation relation is

R(a) ∼ R(b) iff fibreView(R(a))=fibreView(R(b)) and sameSymmetryClass(R(a),R(b)).

Here sameSymmetryClass means equivalence of every reversible support-and-adjacency-preserving transformation, as defined by the existing Physics symmetry predicate. Reflexivity follows from equality and reflexivity of that equivalence. Transitivity follows by composing the fibre equality and, for each transformation pair, the two symmetry equivalences.

For root r, define phase membership of x by a valid finite path [r,…,x] in G whose every cell y satisfies R(r)∼R(y). The length-One path supplies the base for a held root. A valid adjacent successor in the same class extends the path, preserving every prior cell and appending the successor. Induction on these extensions proves closure for every finite successor history. Every member is connected to r and shares both the recurrence fibre and symmetry class. A different fibre or symmetry class therefore excludes membership.

Maximality follows without selecting a favourable subset. If H is any homogeneous connected support containing paths from r to each of its cells, each such path is valid in G and all its cells belong to H. Homogeneity supplies R(r)∼R(y) for every path cell. Thus every x∈H belongs to the constructed phase. No homogeneous connected support at those conditions can contain an omitted reachable member.

B(R)=B(R′), and, for every u,v, (u,v)∈Q(R) iff (u,v)∈Q(R′).

640.5. Exact factor-removal procedure for rotation orders

The source starts with positive remainder r=n and trial divisor d=2. While d²≤r, a divisible trial is retained once and the remainder is repeatedly divided by d; a nondivisible trial is skipped. The divisor then advances by one. At exit, the final remainder is retained precisely when it exceeds One. Boolean, noninteger, zero and negative host inputs are rejected by the original positive-whole guard.
For an exact division, r mod d=0 and r mod d+d⌊r/d⌋=r imply r=dq, q=⌊r/d⌋. Existing exact fraction-reduction proofs give q>0. Since d≥2, q<q+q≤dq=r. Therefore repeated division strictly decreases a positive remainder; its final value remains positive and no greater than its input. For the outer loop, use μ(r,d)=r+1−d as a natural-valued termination measure. The branch condition d²≤r implies d≤r, and every retained remainder r′≤r gives r′+1−(d+1)<r+1−d. This inequality is proved by induction over d with direct successor subtraction. Both recursive loops therefore terminate without a numerical search cutoff. The subtraction here belongs to the termination measure, not an added scientific scalar.

640.7. Complete prime support and coprime residue correspondence

For every positive order n, the original trial-division output F(n) satisfies
\[p\in F(n)\iff \operatorname{Prime}(p)\land p\mid n.\]
The loop invariant excludes every divisor k with 1<k<d before trial d. Removing d preserves that exclusion and makes the remaining factor indivisible by d. An emitted trial divisor is prime: a smaller proper divisor would divide the original remainder, contradicting the invariant. When d² exceeds the final remainder r>1, any proper factorization r=ab would have a,b≥d, contradicting r<d². Conversely, a prime divisor survives removal of every different prime: p|d^k s implies p|d or p|s, and distinct primality excludes p|d. Induction on the actual decreasing loop measure therefore retains every prime divisor.
For the source residue list R(n), this gives
\[c\in R(n)\iff 0<c\le n\;\land\;\gcd(c,n)=1.\]
If a common divisor exceeds One, the same factor loop supplies a prime divisor of that common divisor; it belongs to F(n) and excludes c. Conversely, any excluded prime divides both c and n, and hence their gcd, so that gcd cannot be One. Thus the executable count |R(n)| counts exactly the coprime residue labels across the full supplied positive-order domain.
The source returned certificate preserves its degree boundary2, odd-prime rule, factor form2^a3^b, three exponent constraints, survivor sequence(1,2,3,4,6), and least excluded order5. Its guard still evaluates admission for all five returned candidates and retains the original error text on failure.

641. Crystallographic rotation restriction: unrestricted arithmetic closure

The rank-two rotation boundary counts coprime residue labels, not sampled angles. Let R(n) be the exact source residue list on 1,…,n and φ(n)=|R(n)|. The preceding prime-support and coprimality proofs identify this executable count with the complete reduced residue carrier. For n>1, n itself is excluded because gcd(n,n)=n; hence the existing Fold/orbit reduced-residue counting theorem applies without changing the carrier. For prime p, every positive label below p is coprime, giving φ(p)=p−1.

Complete residue blocks give the prime-power count. The interval 1,…,pk decomposes into k translated blocks, with translation by pj preserving remainders modulo p. In each block exactly p−1 labels have nonzero remainder. Thus
\[\#\{1\le c\le pk:p\nmid c\}=k(p-1),\qquad \varphi(p^{k+1})=p^k(p-1).\]
Prime support proves that the only prime divisor of p^{k+1} is p. This connects the block count to the actual source filter rather than introducing a new definition of φ.

For composite orders, lift the coprime labels for n across p complete blocks. The gcd is unchanged by adding a multiple of n, so the lifted list has pφ(n) elements. A label is coprime to pn exactly when it is coprime to n and is not divisible by p. If p divides n, the second condition already follows from the first. If p does not divide n, the excluded labels are precisely p times the original coprime labels for n: cancellation of the coprime factor p gives gcd(pc,n)=gcd(c,n). Injectivity and complete membership of that map give exactly φ(n) exclusions. Therefore
\[\varphi(pn)=\begin{cases}p\varphi(n)&p\mid n,\\(p-1)\varphi(n)&p\nmid n.\end{cases}\]
Both equations count the entire supplied carrier. No bounded order search or stored answer table supplies either recurrence.

Now let p be any prime divisor of n. Write n=pm with m=n/p<n. If p does not divide m, the second recurrence gives the factor p−1 directly. Otherwise the first recurrence and induction on m preserve that factor. Consequently
\[p\mid n\quad\Longrightarrow\quad p-1\mid\varphi(n).\]
Since φ(n)>0, the rank-two bound φ(n)≤2 implies p−1≤2. Every prime factor is therefore 2 or 3; in particular the only odd prime factor is 3. The recurrences also show φ(m)≤φ(pm), so a prime quotient of an admitted order remains admitted. Strong induction on that strictly smaller quotient closes all positive orders. Multiplying the admitted quotient forms by 2 or 3 produces the retained orders and possible exclusions 8, 9, 12, 18. Their degrees follow from the same recurrences:
\[\varphi(1)=1,\quad\varphi(2)=1,\quad\varphi(3)=2,\quad\varphi(4)=2,\quad\varphi(6)=2,\]
\[\varphi(8)=4,\quad\varphi(9)=6,\quad\varphi(12)=4,\quad\varphi(18)=6.\]
This is an induction over every positive n: the finite branch values arise from its prime-factor descent. The resulting equivalences are
\[\varphi(n)\le2\iff n\in\{1,2,3,4,6\}\iff\exists a,b:\ n=2^a3^b,\ a\le2,\ b\le1,\ \neg(a=2\land b=1).\]
The prime-power formula separately gives the binary and ternary exponent restrictions. Direct enumeration of the constrained exponent pairs proves the reverse implication. The original five-candidate guard is proved to pass, and the returned six-field certificate is proved equal to the exact source certificate. Order 5 is excluded, while every positive order below 5 is admitted; hence its least-excluded field is justified.

645. Substitution populations and exclusion of a rational fixed scale

V3's quasicrystalline inflation construction generates the population recurrence A→AB, B→A. With positive population pair (a,b), the successor is
\[(a,b)\longmapsto(a+b,a),\qquad(a_0,b_0)=(1,1).\]
At positive depth d, the retained history has exactly d rows. Induction on the successor count proves this history length and the two population equations. The first six rows are (1,1), (2,1), (3,2), (5,3), (8,5), (13,8), reproduced directly by the Lean implementation and pinned V3 execution.

A positive rational fixed scale in lowest terms, p/q, would satisfy
\[p^2=pq+q^2,\qquad p>0,\ q>0,\ \gcd(p,q)=1.\]
The right side is q(p+q), so q divides p². If q>1, it has a prime divisor r. Then r divides p², hence r divides p, while r also divides q. This contradicts coprimality, so q=1. Since p divides both p² and pq, the equation also implies p divides q²=1; positivity forces p=1. The equation would then read 1=2, which is impossible. Thus no reduced positive rational fixed scale exists. This is a theorem for all positive p and q in the source domain, not a bounded search through candidate fractions, and it does not evaluate an irrational limit.

649. Vacancy: retained site and structural occupant absence

A reference-site record retains site identity s, reference occupant c_ref, actual occupant state o, provenance p and observation boundary b. The actual state has two distinct constructors: structural EmptyOne or occupied(c). Vacancy changes only that occupant state:
\[V(s,c_{\rm ref},o,p,b)=(s,c_{\rm ref},\mathrm{EmptyOne},p,b).\]

\[\mathrm{EmptyOne}\ne\operatorname{occupied}(c)\]
for every admitted occupant representation c. No amount value is used to represent the absence.

For every record r, the proofs give
\[\operatorname{site}(V(r))=\operatorname{site}(r),\qquad
\operatorname{reference}(V(r))=\operatorname{reference}(r),\qquad V(V(r))=V(r),\]
with provenance and boundary also unchanged. Across a complete retained ledger R, the mapped vacancy construction preserves the entire ordered site list and row count:
\[\operatorname{sites}(\operatorname{map}(V,R))=\operatorname{sites}(R),\qquad

650. Interstitial and substitutional defects: added relations and retained-site relabelling

The reference carrier is an ordered list R of occupied site–content pairs. An interstitial record retains an additional site s, its occupant c, provenance and boundary, with s absent from the reference site list. Its occupied relation is appended:
\[I(R;s,c)=R\mathbin{+\!+}[(s,c)].\]
Every reference row remains a member of I, the new occupied row is present, and the append-length identity gives
\[|I(R;s,c)|=|R|+|[(s,c)]|=|R|+1.\]
These statements hold for arbitrary reference lists and occupant types. The extra occupied relation is thus distinguished by retained carrier membership and the exact increment, not by a numerical amount assigned to absence.

For substitution, a retained reference-site record r=(s,c_ref,o,p,b) receives occupied content c while keeping site, reference occupant, provenance and boundary:
\[S_c(r)=(s,c_{\rm ref},\operatorname{occupied}(c),p,b).\]
Injectivity of the occupied constructor establishes both directions of the changed-label criterion:
\[\operatorname{occupant}(S_c(r))\ne\operatorname{occupied}(c_{\rm ref})
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad c\ne c_{\rm ref}.\]
Thus replacing a label by itself does not qualify as a changed occupant. Occupied and structurally absent constructors are distinct, so substitution is not vacancy. If t is a retained reference site and s is the added site, t belongs to the reference site list whereas s does not; equality s=t would contradict that membership. Therefore the added site and retained substitution site are distinct. Repeated substitution records the final occupant at the same retained site:
\[S_d(S_c(r))=S_d(r).\]

651. Dislocation: complete nonclosing circuit and retained slip history

The source distinguishes a line-supported lattice mismatch by the complete circuit around it and the held translation left by that circuit. Let L be the retained lattice carrier, W its local-word map, and E its adjacency relation. Each recorded circuit step carries a lattice translation T_i on this same carrier and word map. Its existing translation laws state
\[x\in L\Rightarrow T_i(x)\in L,\quad W(T_i(x))=W(x),\quad
(T_i(x),T_i(y))\in E\Longleftrightarrow(x,y)\in E.\]
The complete circuit retains its ordered vertices and every step's translation and provenance. Consecutive vertices are actual held edges; the final circuit vertex returns to the initial vertex. The transported lattice site is computed across the full ordered trace:
\[U_{\varnothing}(x)=x,\qquad U_{p\cdot i}(x)=T_i(U_p(x)).\]
For the base trace, carrier membership, word identity and adjacency are unchanged. At a successor, the preceding induction result supplies a held input to T_i; applying the three translation laws gives
\[U_p(x)\in L,\qquad W(U_p(x))=W(x),\qquad
(U_p(x),U_p(y))\in E\Longleftrightarrow(x,y)\in E\]
for the complete trace p. Concatenating two retained traces gives
\[U_{p\cdot q}(x)=U_q(U_p(x)).\]
The vertex ledger has exactly one more row than the move ledger. Its validity follows by appending each actual edge to the preceding complete adjacent path, preserving all intermediate sites.

At a supported line site x, the dislocation's circuit reading is the retained endpoint distinction
\[U_p(x)\ne x.\]
The empty trace transports x to itself and therefore cannot provide this reading. A nonclosing circuit necessarily contains a recorded step. The complete line is a held nonempty adjacent path; its circuit and nonclosure reading remain bound to each line site, provenance and declared boundary. These records distinguish an observed nonclosing translation from an endpoint label lacking its intermediate path.

The induction above constructs the whole circuit as a lattice translation B=U_p. Consequently its counted slip sequence follows from the existing lattice iteration, rather than a new motion law:
\[x_0=x,\qquad x_{n+1}=B(x_n),\qquad H_0=[x],\qquad H_{n+1}=H_n\mathbin{+\!+}[x_{n+1}].\]
The first slip differs from its origin by the retained nonclosure reading. Every subsequent x_n remains on L and retains W(x_n)=W(x); applying the same iteration to a neighboring pair preserves its adjacency in both directions. The complete history satisfies
\[|H_n|=n+1,\qquad z\in H_n\Rightarrow z\in H_{n+1}.\]
Thus the circuit supplies a lawful whole-lattice slip history with its complete ordered trace. The declared observation boundary and line provenance remain explicit retained records.

652. Grain identity and the exact grain boundary

The crystal carrier retains its complete site and edge sets together with an orientation label O(x) at each site. Connectivity follows the retained adjacency relation in either traversal direction; the underlying ordered edge record is preserved. Define x~y by finite adjacent continuation through sites with unchanged orientation. The base case is the held site itself; a successor appends an adjacent site z when O(y)=O(z):
\[x\sim x,\qquad x\sim y\ \land\ y\leftrightarrow z\ \land\ O(y)=O(z)
\quad\Rightarrow\quad x\sim z.\]
Induction on the complete path proves that both endpoints belong to the carrier and that O(x)=O(y). Concatenation proves transitivity. Reversing each adjacency and its orientation equality, then concatenating the reversed preceding path, proves symmetry. Thus the grain at a held root r is the complete region
\[G_r=\{x:r\sim x\}.\]
For x,y in G_r, reversal of the r-to-x path followed by the r-to-y path yields x~y, and their orientations agree. The construction retains an internal path for every member, including every intermediate site.

Maximality follows from the same path induction. Let R be any connected region with the root r and constant orientation. Every internal path from r to a member x starts at a held site; at each adjacent successor, orientation coherence supplies precisely the equality required by the continuation rule. Hence r~x and
\[R\subseteq G_r.\]
Since G_r itself is connected and orientation coherent, it is the maximal such region containing r. If G_a and G_b share a site c, the paths a~c and b~c compose with reversal to give a~b. Transitivity then proves both membership implications, so
\[G_a\cap G_b\ne\varnothing\quad\Rightarrow\quad G_a=G_b\]
as equality of membership predicates. Disconnected regions with the same orientation are not merged merely because their labels agree: membership still requires the complete adjacent path.

The boundary retains exactly the original ordered edges whose endpoints have different orientations:
\[\partial G=\{(a,b)\in E:O(a)\ne O(b)\}.\]
For a held edge, equality of endpoint orientations constructs the one-step coherent path; conversely every coherent path forces equal endpoint orientations. Consequently
\[(a,b)\in\partial G\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(a,b)\in E\ \land\ \neg(a\sim b).\]
This is the exact adjacency where distinct grains meet, derived from their connectivity and orientation records. The filter preserves the original edge order and excludes every non-boundary edge without inserting a threshold or fitted orientation tolerance.

658. Electron and hole carrier duality

The exclusion result already establishes that identical constituent words at the same cell cannot admit alternating exchange: the exchange is fixed, whereas alternating orientation must be opposite and cannot equal itself. For the resulting binary occupation carrier, let S retain every local state and O its occupied support. The held absence is the full complement within that carrier,
  H(S,O) = {s ∈ S : s ∉ O}.
The filter-membership derivation yields
  s ∈ H(S,O) ⇔ (s ∈ S and s ∉ O).
Therefore every s ∈ S has exactly one of the occupied and absent descriptions. No state is removed when its occupation is absent. Provided O ⊆ S, taking the dual description again recovers occupation:
  H(S,H(S,O)) = O
as equality of membership for every state. The forward implication excludes absence from both descriptions; the reverse implication uses occupation to rule out its complement.

For a retained transfer from s to t, write O and O′ for occupation before and after. Its endpoint conditions are
  s ∈ O, t ∉ O; s ∉ O′, t ∈ O′.
Applying the complement equivalence gives
  s ∉ H(S,O), t ∈ H(S,O);
  s ∈ H(S,O′), t ∉ H(S,O′).
Thus the same event is an occupation transfer s→t and an absence transfer t→s. At any unchanged local state, occupation membership before and after is equivalent, hence absence membership is also equivalent. This is a dual description of the retained transition, not a second constituent created by removing a site.

The existing electric distinction represents charge as a positive magnitude and a held orientation. Its dual retains the magnitude and reverses that orientation. The two orientations differ and reversing twice recovers the original charge. Complete occupation and absence ledgers both project to the full original state carrier, proved by induction over every finite support list. 659. Exclusion-bounded canonical mode occupation

Take any finite occupation list L for one canonical constituent word w and one canonical cell c. Every occupant a in this list retains a.word = w and a.cell = c. The list domain includes every finite length. Exclusion requires alternating exchange for every pair of retained occupants.

If L begins with two occupants a,b, their equal word and cell imply
  exchange(a,b) = (a,b).
Alternating exchange would also require
  orientation(exchange(a,b)) = opposite(orientation(a,b)).
Together these make one held orientation equal to its opposite, contradicted by the previously derived distinction of the two orientations. Hence every list with two or more occupants is rejected. The remaining list cases are exactly
  admitted(L) ⇔ L = [] or L = [a].
The empty and singleton cases admit no pair requiring exclusion and satisfy the predicate. Canonical identity then forces a = (w,c), giving
  L = [] or L = [(w,c)].
These outcomes are distinct: held structural absence and one retained indistinguishable occupation. Thus binary occupation follows from exclusion applied to the full finite-list domain, rather than from preselecting a binary candidate list. No numerical zero occupation scalar or additional capacity parameter is introduced.

The original eight preservation axes retain all 256 forms, the original three operational witnesses, controls, elimination decisions, closure, registration and post-seal empirical correspondence. The scientific argument uses the established exclusion proof directly; unchanged source protocol checks are retained alongside it.

660. Source-bound doping and carrier-support difference

For the forward direction, distinguish whether x was already in B. 661. Occupation-majority and absence-majority semiconductor classes

The complete source-bound doping record retains gained occupation support G and lost occupation support L, the latter providing the opposed absence description. Count every retained carrier in these supports and write g = |G| and l = |L|. The carrier imbalance has two possible strict orientations:
  l < g  ⇔ occupation-majority;
  g < l  ⇔ absence-majority.
For g ≠ l, finite whole-count ordering proves that one of these inequalities holds. They cannot both hold: strict order is asymmetric. The selection therefore has exactly one of the two held orientations for every imbalance. When g = l, no imbalance is present and no majority orientation is assigned. This balanced record does not add a third majority class.

The implementation computes g and l from the full prior/result support difference, rather than receiving a preselected carrier class. It proves both displayed equivalences and the exhaustive result under g ≠ l. Interchanging gained and lost counts interchanges the inequalities and hence reverses the held orientation:
  select(l,g) = opposite(select(g,l))
whenever a majority orientation is present. The quantities remain whole counts and the direction remains a held orientation; no signed carrier magnitude or fitted majority coefficient is required.

669. Source-derived opposed endpoint selection

For each endpoint v, let B_v and A_v be its retained support lists before and after doping. The existing support construction computes the two ordered difference lists
  G_v = [x in A_v : x is absent from B_v],
  L_v = [x in B_v : x is absent from A_v],
  g_v = length(G_v),  l_v = length(L_v).
Membership in G_v is equivalent to membership in A_v and absence from B_v; membership in L_v gives the reverse pair of conditions. Therefore a support element cannot occur in both difference lists. The definitions retain list occurrences, rather than replacing the lists with sets.

The majority selector compares these natural counts without introducing a signed difference:
  M_v = first   if l_v < g_v,
  M_v = second  if g_v < l_v,
  M_v = none    if g_v = l_v.
Strict-order asymmetry makes the first two cases exclusive; order trichotomy makes the three cases exhaustive. In particular, equality selects neither majority class. For an actual transfer t with endpoints s and d, the junction selection is exactly
  P(t) iff (M_s = first and M_d = second)
           or (M_s = second and M_d = first).
The proof evaluates all endpoint-selector cases: either none result rejects the pair, matching orientations reject it, and the two opposed orientations admit it. Filtering the original ordered transfer list N gives T_pn = [t in N : P(t)], preserving both transfer directions and the order and multiplicity of the qualifying records.

670. Junction transfer, depletion and balance identities

For every retained cross-interface transfer t, retain its source s, destination d, charge q, source identity and action record. The paired space-charge description holds (s, reverse(q)) and (d,q). Charge reversal preserves the positive magnitude and exchanges the held orientation. Every depletion row is exactly the image of an original transfer whose source lies inside the selected region and whose destination lies outside it; the converse inclusion is proved as well. Original interface compatibility retains both endpoints on the generated lattice.

For every complete finite transfer network, the exact boundary ledger satisfies
  departures_inside + inward_count = arrivals_inside + outward_count.
To derive the identity, fix the declared region-membership test I and inspect one transfer t=(s,d,q). Let a and b be the natural counting indicators of I(s) and I(d). Write j_in for the indicator of the case a=0,b=1, and j_out for the indicator of a=1,b=0. The four endpoint cases give
  (a,b)=(0,0): a+j_in = 0 = b+j_out,
  (a,b)=(0,1): a+j_in = 1 = b+j_out,
  (a,b)=(1,0): a+j_in = 1 = b+j_out,
  (a,b)=(1,1): a+j_in = 1 = b+j_out.
Thus a+j_in=b+j_out for each transfer occurrence. The empty network has four zero counts. Appending an occurrence adds its corresponding indicators to the four counts; associativity and commutativity of natural addition preserve the identity. Equivalently, summing the per-occurrence equality over the original list gives
  sum_t a(t) + sum_t j_in(t) = sum_t b(t) + sum_t j_out(t).
The four sums are precisely departures_inside, inward_count, arrivals_inside and outward_count. Repeated transfers contribute once for each retained occurrence. This is the transfer-count boundary identity proved by FieldSourceContinuity.exactInteriorBoundaryBalance and reused by JunctionTransfer.exactDepletionTransportBalance.

The transfer ledger retains every source and destination occurrence. The paired space-charge construction retains the same positive charge magnitude at both endpoints and reverses the held orientation at the depleted endpoint. The charge–field correspondence below uses the charge of that same transfer and its retained work record.

  strain = (L1 - L0) / L0,
where subtraction denotes the exact held-orientation operation just described.   (x.numerator * L0.denominator) * quotient(x,L0).denominator

For a member m with ordered repeat occurrences C_m and covalent connections B_m, the retained chain construction gives
\[
\operatorname{edges}(B_m)=\operatorname{adjacentPairs}(\operatorname{names}(C_m)),\qquad
L_m=|C_m|=|\operatorname{names}(C_m)|>0.
\]
Every adjacent pair therefore has a corresponding actual covalent bond. For that bond's prepared state S and complete interaction trace T, the existing recurrence proof supplies
\[
\operatorname{phaseAction}(S,\operatorname{flatten}(T))=\operatorname{ok}(S).
\]
Thus the population records the existing recurrence rather than replacing it by a chain-length label. With P=[m_0,\ldots,m_n], the complete census is
\[
\mathcal C(P)=[(u_m,\operatorname{names}(C_m),L_m,b_m):m\in P],
\]
where u_m is the retained repeat identity and b_m the original branching organization record. Every member contributes its row, and every output row comes from a member. Appending a member gives
\[
\mathcal C(P\mathbin{+\!+}[m])=\mathcal C(P)\mathbin{+\!+}[(u_m,\operatorname{names}(C_m),L_m,b_m)].
\]
The earlier members, distribution boundary, interchain organization and provenance are retained. The record includes its entire input, so branching and interchain distinctions are not reconstructed from length alone. A singleton complete material record supplies the base, and list append establishes finite successor closure.

The eight source axes retain repeated-unit chain carrier, covalent backbone recurrence, sequence/length/branching/entanglement organization, distribution boundary, complete trace, root provenance, positive finite successor closure and no extra rule. 706. Composite material organization

A composite retains its distinguishable constituent carriers while interfaces and architecture compose their load, transport or barrier responses. A constituent includes its identity and complete material record. Each interface joins two distinct identities and retains its content-transfer network, traction-transfer network and barrier record. Every interface endpoint belongs to the retained constituent population; the architecture, scale and provenance accompany the assembly.

Write I for the complete interface list and N_i and T_i for the content and traction networks of interface i. The assembled networks are
\[
N=\mathop{\operatorname{concat}}_{i\in I}N_i,\qquad
T=\mathop{\operatorname{concat}}_{i\in I}T_i.
\]
Every transfer in N or T originates in one retained interface row. Its endpoints are the two constituent identities of that row, in either orientation. The original complete-transfer conservation proof therefore gives
\[
\operatorname{outgoingSupport}(N)=\operatorname{incomingSupport}(N),\qquad
\operatorname{outgoingSupport}(T)=\operatorname{incomingSupport}(T).
\]
This is conservation of each complete carried record, with its source and destination, rather than equality of independently fitted aggregate coefficients. Appending an interface i preserves the constituent records and composes its transfers exactly:
\[
N(I\mathbin{+\!+}[i])=N(I)\mathbin{+\!+}N_i.
\]
The assembled output retains its entire input, including the architecture, scale and barrier records. A singleton complete assembly supplies the base, and appending a complete assembly preserves all earlier records. No mixture rule or material-specific fitted response is introduced.

The eight source axes give the literal 256-form product. 707. Glass and amorphous organization

A glass retains connected local material structure and local recurrence while admitting no crystalline translation class. Its observed macrostate also retains preparation and relaxation at the declared observation time. These are distinct source conditions: local return does not imply a translation of the complete material.

For the complete generated network G and its local word w(x), each retained local recurrence R_x satisfies
\[
R_x^{\rm last}=R_x^{\rm first}=w(x),\qquad x\in G.
\]
A crystalline translation would have to retain the same graph and word, preserve adjacency and move a held site. Its existing lattice recurrence would imply w(Tx)=w(x). The source's noncrystalline condition excludes the complete class of such translations:
\[
\neg\operatorname{Nonempty}(\operatorname{CrystallineTranslation}(G,w))
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\forall T:\operatorname{CrystallineTranslation}(G,w),\ \bot.
\]
This exclusion concerns the complete translation record, while the local recurrence above remains held. The glass record retains the actual preparation-to-observation path H, its source actions, the final material and the observation clock C. The original duration construction gives, for a nonempty path,
\[
t_H=\frac{|\operatorname{changes}(H)|}{|\operatorname{changes}(C)|},\qquad
|\operatorname{events}(H)|=|\operatorname{changes}(H)|+1.
\]
The native proof preserves the exact normalized-ratio cross-product identity; it does not introduce a fitted relaxation time. The macrostate record is
\[
M=(\operatorname{classes}(G_{\rm final}),\operatorname{preparation},
\operatorname{relaxationObservation},t_H).
\]
Its classes are the complete computed observation fibres. Different preparation or relaxation records remain distinguishable in M. The assembled result retains the entire input and all path events and actions; singleton and append equations establish complete finite record closure.

708. Porous material organization

A porous material retains both solid support and structural-absence support. Pores are held spatial distinctions, not numerical zeros. The declared resolution and access boundary determine which support and connections are resolved. For complete support V, solid support S and pore support P, the source representation retains
\[
x\in V\ \Longleftrightarrow\ x\in S\ \lor\ x\in P,\qquad S\cap P=\varnothing.
\]
The pore graph keeps exactly the original network edges whose two endpoints are pores:
\[
E_P=\{(a,b)\in E:a\in P\land b\in P\}.
\]
The existing crossing-cut operation computes the complete interface
\[
I=\{(a,b)\in E:\mathbf 1_S(a)\ne\mathbf 1_S(b)\}.
\]
The native membership theorem establishes both directions of this equality, preserving every qualifying edge and introducing none.

Let A be the declared access points, all retained in P. Accessibility means a complete path from an access point through the pore graph:
\[
\operatorname{accessible}(x)\ \Longleftrightarrow\
\exists a\in A,\ \operatorname{PathWitness}((P,E_P),a,x).
\]
Every accessible point is therefore a pore and cannot be solid. Every declared access point is accessible through its identity path. If x is accessible and a pore path leads from x to y, composing the two retained paths proves y accessible. The existing finite reachability algorithm is sound and complete for these path witnesses; the source does not replace pore topology by a scalar porosity or assume all pores are accessible. The complete input, interface, pore graph, access points and resolution accompany the result. Singleton and append equations preserve the entire finite record sequence.

710. Material anisotropy

Anisotropy compares response relations across retained material directions while the specimen, conditions and method remain fixed. The response carrier is retained in its supplied type: no universal tensor form or fitted constitutive relation is added. A record contains the specimen, full direction list D, directional response R(d), conditions, method and coordinate/symmetry boundary. Its complete census is
\[
\mathcal C(D)=[(d,R(d)):d\in D].
\]
Every direction contributes its response, and every census row comes from a retained direction. The source distinction is
\[
\operatorname{anisotropic}(D,R)\ \Longleftrightarrow\
\exists a,b\in D:\ R(a)\ne R(b).
\]
Such a witness necessarily has a≠b: if a=b, applying R would make the responses equal. Conversely, equality of all directional responses excludes any anisotropy witness. Under a coordinate relabelling e with a retained inverse d satisfying d(e(x))=x, the comparison is unchanged:
\[
R(d(e(a)))=R(d(e(b)))\ \Longleftrightarrow\ R(a)=R(b).
\]
The specimen and observation boundary are not changed by relabelling. Appending another retained direction gives
\[
\mathcal C(D+[x])=\mathcal C(D)+[(x,R(x))].
\]
Earlier unequal-response witnesses remain present, with the same specimen, conditions, method and coordinate/symmetry record. The complete input accompanies the result, and record-list base and append equations establish finite closure.

The original eight-axis grammar contains 256 forms. Its unique all-preserving alternative retains direction-labelled structure, orientation-dependent response, same-material identity and coordinate/symmetry boundary together with trace, root provenance, finite successor closure and no extra rule. \rho=\frac{|B|}{|I|},\qquad |B|\,\operatorname{den}(\rho)=\operatorname{num}(\rho)\,|I|.

The ratio uses the existing positive-rational normalization. If either support is absent, the ratio output is structural absence (none); the full support record remains held. No scalar zero or fitted scale term is introduced.

712. Processing–structure–property path

\mathcal T(H)=[(e,\operatorname{material}(e),\operatorname{properties}(e)):e\in\operatorname{events}(H)].

Projecting the first component recovers exactly the original ordered event list. Every intermediate event has its table row, and every row originates in that event list. Therefore
\[
|\mathcal T(H)|=|\operatorname{events}(H)|=|\operatorname{changes}(H)|+1.

The action table retains each source identity and complete action record. Appending an actual transition q to event e gives
\[
\mathcal T(H+q)=\mathcal T(H)+[(e,\operatorname{material}(e),\operatorname{properties}(e))],
\qquad
\operatorname{changes}(H+q)=\operatorname{changes}(H)+[\operatorname{row}(q)].
\]
The route boundary and provenance remain fixed, and no prior state or action is discarded.

Endpoint labels cannot reconstruct different retained routes. Suppose two paths have the same endpoint pair but different complete source-action records. If a recovery map from endpoints reconstructed both records, equal inputs would give equal recovered paths, hence equal source-action lists, contradicting the retained distinction. The native proof establishes this contradiction directly. The complete input accompanies the assembled state/action tables. A one-event path supplies the initial table, and both transition append and record-list append establish finite closure.

713. Phase stability and coexistence map

The phase map retains the generated composition and condition support rather than extending a measured domain by a fitted rule. An observation contains its complete chemical recurrence, phase record, connected ordered region and provenance. The phase's composition coordinate is bound to the recurrence's composition class; its phase identity and members are bound to the ordered region's retained macro-fibre.

For the paired forward and reverse reaction records, every constituent test has equal departing and arriving counts. Closed accounting gives
\[
N_{\rm before}+N_{\rm arriving}=N_{\rm after}+N_{\rm departing},
\qquad N_{\rm departing}=N_{\rm arriving},
\]
so cancellation yields \(N_{\rm before}=N_{\rm after}\). Applying this to every retained test preserves the complete composition signature and therefore its generated composition class. The phase identity also retains the homogeneous intensive trace, connected support and symmetry class. Two observations belong to the same phase-map class exactly when their retained composition/intensive classes agree and their ordered regions have the same macro-fibre and reversible adjacency-preserving symmetries.

Let \(S\) be the complete generated observation support and \(a\sim b\) this source-bound class relation. The map's classes are
\[
C_a=\{x\in S:a\sim x\}.
\]
Reflexivity puts every observation in its own class. If \(x\in C_a\cap C_b\), equality of the retained classes and transitivity of the symmetry equivalences give \(a\sim b\). Conversely \(a\sim b\) gives identical membership predicates for \(C_a\) and \(C_b\). Consequently the classes cover the support and distinct classes do not overlap.

The complete composition-condition relation is generated directly from the observation rows:
\[
R=\{\operatorname{row}(x):x\in S\}.
\]
Every relation containing all generated rows contains \(R\); deleting a generated row loses coverage. Membership in \(R\) supplies its actual source observation, so the construction cannot supply a row outside the declared domain. This least generated relation does not introduce a fitted thermodynamic potential. For a connected ordered phase with \(m\) members in a complete support of \(n\) cells, the existing exact normalized fraction \(p/q\) satisfies
\[
mq=pn,\qquad 0<p\le q.
\]
The phase map carries these exact fractions together with the complete phase records.

Coexistence retains the two distinct phase views, their actual interface and their conserved exchange. The existing equilibrium derivation preserves each phase's members across the exchange, hence preserves its member count. The interface separates the phase supports, and a transition retains the ordered path between distinct macro-recurrence classes. The assembled diagram contains the full observation record, all phase fractions, both views of every coexistence pair and every provenance-bearing transition record.

Appending an observation \(z\) extends the generated table by precisely \(\operatorname{row}(z)\). Class membership becomes old membership or the new observation in its corresponding class. All previous observations and the declared domain boundary remain held. A singleton is the base case; repeated append establishes positive finite closure. The original eight binary axes enumerate all 256 alternatives, with the original preserving form, elimination decisions, operational witnesses and adverse controls. The original post-seal source binding retains the required phase-equilibrium, bulk/thin-film, phase-fraction and phase-amount fragments.
