714. Solidification as an ordered nucleation and growth path

Solidification retains the complete path from mobile material organization to position-retaining organization. The original candidate cluster family includes every generated boundary recurrence. A cluster persists when every retained boundary exchange preserves its phase label and members. The nuclei are precisely all persistent clusters of least size:
\[
\mathcal N(F)=\{c\in F:P(c)\ \land\ \forall d\in F,\ P(d)\Rightarrow |c|\le |d|\}.
\]
The construction retains all equal-sized least clusters; the internal witness search does not discard competing minima from the scientific output. The solidification path begins at a member of this complete nucleus set.

A growth step appends one fresh compatible cell, its actual transfer and its source identity. If the path begins at \(c_0\) and ends at \(c_k\), induction over the retained steps gives
\[
|c_k|=|c_0|+k,\qquad
|\operatorname{clusters}(H)|=k+1.
\]
Every initial cell remains held. Each compatible step retains the phase and declared conditions, so the final cluster preserves the initial phase and the complete boundary recurrence. Every edge in the final boundary has its corresponding retained recurrence row; the final phase label is preserved across each such exchange.

The mobile record retains its support-relative displacements and their positive separation. The position-retaining record is a recurrence of the complete location list. Its first location support is bound to the grown cluster. Since the final location list returns to the initial carrier,
\[
\operatorname{support}(L_{\rm final})
=\operatorname{support}(L_{\rm initial})
=\operatorname{cells}(c_k).
\]
Thus the retained position record and grown organization describe the same final support.

Latent energy transfers and rejected constituents have separate complete ledgers. For each ledger, projection from every departure and corresponding arrival recovers the same ordered carrier support:
\[
\pi_{\rm carrier}(\operatorname{departures})
=\pi_{\rm carrier}(\operatorname{arrivals}).
\]
Every rejection transfer begins within the grown support and ends outside it. Rejected content is therefore retained as an explicit cross-boundary transfer, not deleted from the composition accounting. The complete record contains the candidate family, nucleus, every intermediate cluster, growth transfers and their provenance, latent and rejection ledgers, final interface and all boundary recurrence rows. Rate and gradient observations remain in their declared boundary record.

A complete record is the base carrier. Appending a source-bound record appends exactly its assembled path and ledgers while preserving all earlier records. Within each path, the existing growth induction supplies the one-cell successor and recurrence-preservation derivation. The original eight binary axes exhaust 256 alternatives and retain the source's precise carrier, nucleation/growth/rejection relation, latent/composition ledger and rate-gradient boundary, together with its common preservation axes, operational witnesses and controls.

715. Sintering and densification

Sintering retains the particle interfaces, complete material transport and the reorganization of pore support along the processing path. The original particle carrier and transport observation share the same lattice. Each transport step lies on a generated interface between distinct material labels. The initial and final material locations are bound to the solid portions of their complete solid/pore partitions.

A single constituent move replaces the location of one retained occurrence without changing its content:
\[
B=A+[(u,c)]+Z,\qquad B'=A+[(v,c)]+Z.
\]
Projection onto constituent content gives
\[
\pi_c(B)=\pi_c(A)+[c]+\pi_c(Z)=\pi_c(B').
\]
Induction over the actual joined sequence of moves therefore yields
\[
\pi_c(S_{\rm initial})=\pi_c(S_{\rm final}).
\]
Every reading computed from this complete content list is preserved. The destination of each move remains in the generated lattice, so the induction also preserves support membership.

For each actual joining pair \((u,v)\), the complete interface test establishes that the pair is a generated adjacency and that the two original material labels differ. Both endpoints belong to the held network. The path records every move with its before state, after state, constituent and provenance; its row count is exactly the number of moves. No retained move is replaced by an endpoint-only summary.

The pore records retain structural absence explicitly. At both endpoints the complete support obeys
\[
x\in V\iff x\in S\ \lor\ x\in P,\qquad S\cap P=\varnothing.
\]
Binding \(S\) to the actual material locations shows that a final pore is not a final material location. The pore-interface set is exactly the generated crossing cut
\[
\partial S=\{(u,v)\in E:[u\in S]\ne[v\in S]\}.
\]
Both complete pore networks and their interfaces accompany the transport history. Distinct final pore organizations remain distinct records even when content is conserved. Temperature, time, load and provenance remain explicitly held. A singleton complete record provides the base; appending one record appends its exact transport and pore assembly, while the reused transport induction covers every finite move sequence.

The original eight binary axes enumerate 256 alternatives. The unique preserving form retains particle/pore support, interface-driven transfer, conserved content with reorganized pores and the declared processing boundary, together with complete trace, provenance, finite closure and no extra rule. Original program methods, elimination decisions, operational witnesses and controls are preserved.

716. Heat treatment and path-bound material response

Heat treatment retains the declared thermal/time history together with every corresponding phase, defect, grain, interface and property record. Each process event carries a complete material identity and a thermal state consisting of its time, temperature, microstructure and property relation. Cooling and specimen conditions accompany the complete process rather than selecting an alternative law.

For the complete ordered event path \(H\), form the thermal table
\[
T(H)=[(e,t(e),\theta(e),\mu(e),p(e)):e\in\operatorname{events}(H)],
\]
where \(\mu\) is the entire microstructure record, including its phase and defect arrangements. Projection onto the event coordinate recovers the exact original event list. Every original event therefore has its row and every row has an original event. Since a path with \(k\) transitions has \(k+1\) events,
\[
|T(H)|=k+1.
\]

For each source transition \(q\), retain the complete original action row and both thermal states:
\[
Q(q)=(q,\operatorname{thermal}(q_{\rm before}),\operatorname{thermal}(q_{\rm after})).
\]
Projection onto \(q\) recovers the entire ordered action list. Thus phase, defect and other microstructure changes remain associated with their actual temperatures, times, material states and property observations. Projecting source identities and action records recovers the original provenance sequence exactly.

Appending a real transition \(q\) to a new event \(e\) gives
\[
T(H+q)=T(H)+[T(e)],\qquad
Q(H+q)=Q(H)+[Q(q)].
\]
All prior states and transitions remain in order, and cooling and specimen boundaries are unchanged. The complete input accompanies the assembled thermal and transition tables. A single complete record supplies the base; record append and actual transition append give finite closure.

Path-bound response cannot be replaced by reconstruction of the route from endpoint labels alone. Suppose two retained paths have the same endpoints but different source-action lists. If one function of the endpoint pair reconstructed both complete records, equal inputs would imply equal records, hence equal action lists, a contradiction. The full thermal history is therefore retained alongside its property consequence. This argument concerns the exact supplied records and does not add a fitted thermal-response equation.

The original eight binary axes exhaust 256 forms. The preserving form retains the history-labelled phase network, thermal-path/microstructure relation, time-temperature transition record and cooling/specimen boundary together with the common trace, provenance, finite-closure and no-extra-rule axes. The original candidate decisions, controls and source-bound validation behavior are preserved.

717. Corrosion: the joint material–environment ledger

Corrosion retains the material and environment as one complete interfacial reaction/transport record. The generated interface consists exactly of adjacency edges whose two material labels differ. Every such edge has its reaction record, electron-transfer records and constituent transport ledger. Mapping the assembled rows back to their edges recovers the entire original interface, so no generated interface is omitted and no ungenerated row is inserted.

Each reaction places every retained constituent from a registered reactant into a registered product. Let \(P\) be the complete concatenated placement sequence. Projection from its input and output flows preserves the constituent sequence, and for every retained constituent test \(\chi\),
\[
\sum_{c\in\operatorname{inputs}(P)}\chi(c)
=\sum_{c\in\operatorname{outputs}(P)}\chi(c).
\]
The products therefore retain the original complete constituent carrier list. Each actual reaction also contains a retained relation change; it is not replaced by an identity operation.

Electron transfer retains the same electron in its donor-loss and acceptor-gain halves. With the complete electron sequence \(E\),
\[
\pi_e(\operatorname{inputs}(E))=\pi_e(\operatorname{destinations}(E)),
\qquad N_{\rm loss}(\chi,E)=N_{\rm gain}(\chi,E).
\]
Both endpoints of every accepted electron transfer remain in the generated material/environment support. The actual edge orientation is retained, allowing either direction across the interface. Source history projection recovers every original electron record, including its donor and acceptor.

The separate constituent-transport ledger similarly satisfies
\[
\operatorname{outgoingSupport}(T)=\operatorname{incomingSupport}(T).
\]
Every transfer is bound to its actual interface edge and both endpoints remain held. Thus chemical products, charge transfer and transported material are accounted for together while their distinct roles remain explicit. The assembled result retains its entire input, all interface rows, complete reaction flows, redox history, transport ledger, environment/time boundary and provenance.

One complete record is the base carrier. Appending a new source-bound record appends precisely its assembled reaction, electron and transport records. Existing reaction and redox induction proofs preserve the full carrier ledger across every finite extension. The original eight binary axes exhaust 256 alternatives: material/environment carrier, interfacial redox/transport, mass-charge-product accounting, environment/time boundary, complete trace, root provenance, finite closure and no extra rule. 718. Wear, friction and retained surface transfer

Wear retains the complete contact/load/motion history of both surface carriers. At every event the record contains both material identities, their organization, the applied load/motion observation and the friction response. Material transfer is retained separately from that friction response, including explicit debris destinations.

S(H)=[(e,A(e),B(e),L(e)):e\in\operatorname{events}(H)],
\qquad F(H)=[(e,f(e)):e\in\operatorname{events}(H)].

\operatorname{outgoingSupport}(T(H))=\operatorname{incomingSupport}(T(H)).
\]
Let \(D\) be the declared debris-site support. The debris ledger is exactly
\[
T_D(H)=\{t\in T(H):\operatorname{destination}(t)\in D\}.
\]
Membership is proved in both directions. A material occurrence transferred to debris remains in the carrier accounting; it is not deleted. The departure/arrival identity also holds for this complete debris subledger.

Friction and material loss remain distinct observables. Two records with the same friction history but different transfer ledgers cannot have the same complete result: projecting the result back to its transfer ledger would contradict the retained difference. A changed final surface adjacency similarly distinguishes the complete records. Thus a friction label does not erase transferred content or surface reorganization.

S(H+q)=S(H)+[(e,A(e),B(e),L(e))],\qquad
F(H+q)=F(H)+[(e,f(e))].

719. Radiation damage and the retained probe-to-defect path

\[
w'(x)=\begin{cases}w_s'&x=s,\\w(x)&x\ne s,\end{cases}

\]
It proves the exact localization equivalence
\[
w'(x)\ne w(x)\iff x=s.
\]
The source site belongs to the generated lattice. The first state of the subsequent path is bound to \(w'\), so that path begins with the actual changed word while all other initial sites retain their reference words.

with the original held orientations and exact positive-support arithmetic. No interaction row or displacement record is discarded when the defect is assembled.

\]
A retained final departure fails that equality; the construction does not erase it or label it recovered. Every supplied migration history retains its constituent words and generated destination support by the existing finite transport induction.

720. Piezoelectric coupling: retained cross-response and orientation closure

V3's piezoelectric entry retains the mechanical–electric cross-response, its orientation and charge ledger, the field/stress observation conditions and the complete state-transition record. Its dynamics dependency defines reversibility with a retained record separately from inversion of an output without that record. Both definitions are preserved here.

Let S be the complete source support, q:S→M its retained material observation and f:M→E the cross-response, where M=q(S). The admitted transformation guards require nonempty duplicate-free source labels and exactly one image per source label. The composed response is

    (f∘q)(s)=f(q(s)).

Write T={(m,f(m)):m∈M} for the complete ordered transition rows and R for the retained rows. V3's original dynamics check is

    reversible_with_record(T,R) ⇔ (∀t∈T, t∈R) ∧ distinct(R).

The complete record retains R=T. Total single-valued admission gives distinct source keys; repeated whole pairs would repeat their source key, so T has no duplicate pair. Therefore the original retained-record reversibility check returns true. For every (m,e)∈T,

    m∈predecessor_records(T,e).

All merged predecessors remain individually recorded. None is selected from an unrecorded inverse. If the electric output alone is to determine the predecessor, the separate original conservation test supplies exactly

725. Nanoscale boundary and failure of the bulk quotient

The finite material record retains the complete network, boundary and interior partition, accessible states, transfer/mechanical census, surface and curvature records, and size/shape conditions. Let C be its cell support, B its boundary, I its interior, A its accessible-state support and p its retained property observation. For each cell c, the required census is

    F(c)=(c∈B, c∈I, c∈A, p(c)).

The bulk observation q has its own exact partition over the same C. Its ability to close this census is checked over every ordered pair:

    bulkCloses ⇔ ∀a,b∈C, q(a)=q(b) ⇒ F(a)=F(b).

The native finite all-pairs check is proved equivalent to that statement in both directions. Its negation is the retained nanoscale-boundary criterion. Thus a pair with the same bulk image but different retained census rejects closure and activates that criterion.

Boundary/interior disjointness supplies a concrete class of such distinctions. If a∈B and b∈I, the first coordinate of F(a) is true. If F(a)=F(b), that coordinate would put b in B as well, contradicting B∩I=∅. Hence F(a)≠F(b). If the bulk image merges this pair, it cannot preserve the boundary distinction. A difference in p(a) and p(b) likewise implies a difference in F.

This failure also rules out reconstruction from the bulk image alone. For any proposed reconstruction g, the three equalities

    q(a)=q(b),    g(q(a))=F(a),    g(q(b))=F(b)

would imply F(a)=F(b), contradicting the retained distinction. The obstruction identifies the exact distinction lost by that quotient.

The existing finite-support comparison remains explicit. For positive boundary and interior counts b and i, its exact ratio r satisfies

    r=b/i,    b·denominator(r)=numerator(r)·i.

Absent supports retain the original structural-absence result. This ratio is calculated from the recorded supports; the closure test uses the actual state/property distinctions and introduces no numerical nanoscale cutoff. Every material transfer remains paired in the complete conservation ledger.

The full output retains the original material and bulk partitions, complete cell/census table, size/support record, closure result and its negation, together with the size/shape/resolution boundary. Projecting the cell table recovers exactly C. A singleton record gives the base and finite extension appends the complete new record without erasing prior records.

The original eight binary axes exhaust 256 forms: finite constituent/boundary carrier, retained boundary/interior support relation, discrete-state/interface census, size/shape/resolution boundary, complete trace, root provenance, finite closure and no extra rule. 726. Biomaterial interface: identity, transfer, response and observation

The material–biological interface is a joint relation. Its carrier retains both sides, their structures and every cross-interface row. For the complete registered adjacency graph G=(V,E), with material/biological identities m(v), the interface is the existing exact boundary operation

\[ I=\{(u,v)\in E\mid m(u)\ne m(v)\}. \]

The assembly visits every member of I in its original order. Its row is

\[ J(u,v)=(u,v,m(u),m(v),w(u),w(v),T_{uv},R_{uv},k_{uv}), \]

where w retains structure, T is the full transfer ledger, R is the full response ledger, and k is the compatibility record. Therefore projecting the assembled rows onto their edges returns I exactly. Membership in the assembly is equivalent to being the row of an edge in I. In particular every assembled row retains unequal side identities; internal same-identity edges cannot appear as an interface row. This construction reuses the complete interface derivation rather than selecting a subset using a biological outcome.

Both directed orientations are retained. For each registered transfer or response occurrence t on edge (u,v),

\[ (\operatorname{src}(t),\operatorname{dst}(t))=(u,v)
\quad\text{or}\quad
(\operatorname{src}(t),\operatorname{dst}(t))=(v,u). \]

The accepted graph retains both endpoints in V, so this relation also places every transfer source and destination in the actual joint carrier. The source's bidirectional boundary permits these two orientations; it does not require a nonzero occurrence in both directions at every observation. Each occurrence keeps its carrier, source identity and action record. Flattening all interface ledgers preserves their original order and multiplicities. The complete conservation derivation then gives

\[ \operatorname{out}(\mathop{\mathrm{concat}}_{e\in I}T_e)
 =\operatorname{in}(\mathop{\mathrm{concat}}_{e\in I}T_e),
\qquad
\operatorname{out}(\mathop{\mathrm{concat}}_{e\in I}R_e)
 =\operatorname{in}(\mathop{\mathrm{concat}}_{e\in I}R_e). \]

These equalities follow occurrence by occurrence: departure and arrival projections carry the same original transfer object. No transfer, response or provenance row is discarded.

Exposure e and function boundary f accompany the relation J. A biological outcome o is a separate retained observation. If U_o changes only that observation, the construction proves

\[ J(U_{o_1}(r))=J(U_{o_2}(r))=J(r). \]

The material law is thus constructed from its carrier and interface records independently of the outcome used to test it. The full output is (r,J(r),e,f,o); projecting it recovers the complete input and both observation boundaries. This does not assert that biological outcomes are identical: they remain distinct records at their declared exposure and function boundaries.

For a finite list of these complete records, the base is [record(r)] and the successor satisfies

\[ \mathrm{records}(L\mathbin{+\!+}[r])
=\mathrm{records}(L)\mathbin{+\!+}[\mathrm{record}(r)]. \]

All prior interfaces, transfers, responses, exposures and outcomes remain held. 727. Material lifecycle, complete flow records and recovery identity

The lifecycle follows the actual material from its source through processing and use, with an explicit recovery path whenever recovery is claimed. The endpoints are complete material observations, including the constituent composition and identity, bonding, material boundary and recorded distinctions. Processing and use are typed paths

\[ p:s\longrightarrow p_*,\qquad u:p_*\longrightarrow u_*. \]

An optional recovery record contains both a recovered observation r_* and its actual path q:u_*→r_*. A recovery label without this path is not the source's recovery construction. Each path is built from a one-event base and finite append operations. For any such path t,

\[ |\mathrm{events}(t)|=|\mathrm{changes}(t)|+1. \]

The proof follows the same induction as its construction: the base has one event and zero transitions; appending a transition adds its endpoint and its complete change row. Every change retains before/after observations, source identity and action record. Processing, use and recovery therefore retain intermediate states as well as endpoints.

The ordered lifecycle transitions are

\[ C=\mathrm{changes}(p)\mathbin{+\!+}\mathrm{changes}(u)
\mathbin{+\!+}\begin{cases}\mathrm{changes}(q),&\text{recovery is present},\\ [],&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases} \]

For each c∈C, the ledger records

\[ (c,F(c),L(c),Q(c_{\mathrm{before}}),Q(c_{\mathrm{after}})), \]

where F is the complete material flow, L records losses, and Q retains the declared quality observations. Projection onto the first coordinate returns C exactly; every transition contributes its original row. Flattening the flow lists and loss lists preserves all their occurrences. By the existing source/destination pairing proof,

\[ \operatorname{out}(\mathrm{concat}_{c\in C}F(c))
=\operatorname{in}(\mathrm{concat}_{c\in C}F(c)),\qquad
\operatorname{out}(\mathrm{concat}_{c\in C}L(c))
=\operatorname{in}(\mathrm{concat}_{c\in C}L(c)). \]

A loss leaves the useful material stream but remains in the complete ledger with its destination and provenance. These equalities do not erase the loss or assert unchanged quality.

Recyclability retains the source's explicit recovery requirement:

\[ \mathrm{recyclable}(R)\iff
\exists q,\ R.\mathrm{recovery}=\mathrm{some}(q)
\ \land\ \mathrm{sameIdentity}(s.\mathrm{material},q.\mathrm{recovered}.\mathrm{material}). \]

The previously derived material identity relation is exact equality of its complete constituent/composition, bonding, boundary and observation records. With a recorded q, the recovery condition is therefore equivalent to equality of those four original material fields. Their equivalence follows directly from the material identity reconstruction theorem in both directions. When recovery is absent, the existential condition is false: an absent recovery path cannot establish recyclability. The definition tests the retained recovery; it does not assume that every material has one. Event observations and before/after quality records remain alongside this identity test, with the declared system boundary and provenance.

The complete output retains the entire lifecycle input, the transition ledger, all flows and all losses. The finite-record base contains one complete lifecycle, and its extension obeys

\[ \mathrm{records}(A\mathbin{+\!+}[R])
=\mathrm{records}(A)\mathbin{+\!+}[\mathrm{record}(R)]. \]

Earlier source, process, use, recovery, transformation, loss and quality distinctions are preserved. The source's eight binary axes enumerate all 256 candidates and retain the source/process/use/recovery carrier, complete flow path, loss/transformation/quality ledger, explicit system boundary, complete trace, root provenance, finite closure and no extra rule. Original witnesses, elimination decisions, controls, source comparison and independent validator are preserved.

728. Post-seal Koide comparison with complete rational uncertainty propagation

The charged-lepton cubic fixes its root sum and pair sum before any measured mass ratio is opened. Write its three normalized roots as x₁,x₂,x₃. The established invariants give

\[ s_1=x_1+x_2+x_3=1,\qquad s_2=x_1x_2+x_1x_3+x_2x_3=\frac16. \]

Expanding the square of the sum yields s₁²=x₁²+x₂²+x₃²+2s₂. Consequently the sealed Koide reading is

\[ Q=\frac{x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2}{(x_1+x_2+x_3)^2}
=\frac{s_1^2-2s_2}{s_1^2}
=1-2\left(\frac16\right)=\frac23. \]

KoideComparison.sealedInvariant obtains s₁ and s₂ from the existing chargedInvariants construction and performs those exact rational operations; exactTwoThirds proves its result. Neither measured masses nor their uncertainties occur in this computation.

The measurement side retains both complete fixed-width CODATA 2022 rows: the muon/electron ratio A and muon/tau ratio B. Each quantity must occur exactly once. Its complete central value c and uncertainty u are parsed as exact decimals, and the original guard requires 0<u<c. The row therefore supplies [c−u,c+u], not a central-value surrogate. Let the two intervals be [a₋,a₊] and [b₋,b₊]. Positivity gives the outward tau/electron interval

\[ T=[t_-,t_+]=\left[\frac{a_-}{b_+},\frac{a_+}{b_-}\right]. \]

Every square root is enclosed using the original exact dyadic procedure. For a positive rational v=p/d and positive binary depth h, put S=2ʰ and N=pS². The original integer-square-root seed is followed by upward corrections while (k+1)²d≤N and downward corrections while N<k²d. The resulting integer satisfies

\[ k^2d\le N<(k+1)^2d. \]

KoideEnclosure.floorBounds establishes both inequalities for every numerator N and positive denominator d. The upward correction terminates because each accepted successor satisfies k+1≤(k+1)²d≤N. Its finite recursion bound is derived from N; upSourceRun proves that it follows the original guard and stops only when that guard fails. The downward correction decreases k. At its stopping point k²d≤N, while every decrement preserves the strict upper bound because the old square exceeded N. The two square bounds also determine k uniquely: if a<b, then (a+1)²d≤b²d≤N contradicts N<(a+1)²d, and the reverse ordering gives the symmetric contradiction. Thus the corrected result is the original integer floor independently of the seed implementation. These proofs use no square-root theorem as an additional axiom.

Dividing the squared inequalities by dS² yields the rational enclosure

\[ \sqrt v\in\left[\frac{k}{S},\frac{k+1}{S}\right]. \]

If k²d=N, both returned endpoints are k/S. Otherwise the upper endpoint is (k+1)/S. All fractions are normalized exactly. Nonpositive v or h is rejected by the original guard. The source's depth 160 determines arithmetic enclosure precision; it does not change the sealed scientific invariant. The proof applies to every positive depth.

Apply this enclosure separately to a₋,a₊,t₋,t₊, keeping the lower endpoint at the lower argument and upper endpoint at the upper argument. Denote them α₋,α₊ and τ₋,τ₊. Then

\[ N_-=1+a_-+t_-,\quad N_+=1+a_++t_+,\qquad
D_-=(1+\alpha_-+\tau_-)^2,\quad D_+=(1+\alpha_++\tau_+)^2. \]

The sum is monotone on these positive intervals; squaring preserves their order. Positive division reverses the denominator order, giving the complete outward reading

\[ Q_{\mathrm{source}}\in\left[\frac{N_-}{D_+},\frac{N_+}{D_-}\right]. \]

KoideComparison.fromIntervals implements these endpoints in the original operation order. The source-row assembly theorem connects it to both exact parsed rows. The full CODATA calculation reproduces V3's rational endpoints exactly and places the independently sealed 2/3 inside the resulting interval. Both uncertainties and all four input endpoints remain present.

The external validator first performs this numerical interval test. An excluded 2/3 returns the original error; an accepted interval proceeds to the existing blind source validator using the same complete source bytes. The retained source hash, prediction seal, custody and isolation records, both target rows and adverse comparison controls match V3's complete validator output. This preserves the distinction between deriving 2/3 and subsequently testing it against measured ratios.

The original eight binary axes enumerate all 256 comparison forms. The grammar retains the sealed invariant, exact rational enclosure, both source rows, declared uncertainty, custody and the remaining original preservation coordinates; its original elimination procedure has one survivor. The base retains the complete muon/electron interval, and the successor composes the complete muon/tau interval without removing either endpoint. 730. Positive polynomial-balance certificates for algebraic magnitudes

An algebraic magnitude is retained by its defining balance and a replayable rational enclosure. The construction begins with two positive-coefficient polynomial sides. A side retains its first term and every further supplied term; the exponent is a finite operation count. For positive rational x,

\[ P(x)=a_0x^{e_0}+\cdots+a_rx^{e_r},\qquad
Q(x)=b_0x^{f_0}+\cdots+b_sx^{f_s},\qquad a_i,b_j>0. \]

The certificate identifies P(x)=Q(x); it does not replace that identity by an approximate scalar. Held orientation assigns each term to its side. Separation partitions the oriented term list while retaining every coefficient, exponent and evaluated value. If E evaluates the oriented list and S separates it, the structural induction proves

\[ E(S(T),x)=S(E(T,x)). \]

The empty bookkeeping list records no term. The successor sends the newly held term to exactly its declared side and invokes the induction hypothesis for the retained remainder. Summing each resulting side therefore gives the same pair of positive totals before and after separation. This is the preservation of the defining balance; no negative magnitude or extra coefficient is introduced. The polynomial evaluation trace retains each supplied term and its exact rational value, for every finite list length.

For a rational bracket l<u whose endpoint side orders are opposite, calculate the exact midpoint m=(l+u)/2. If l=A/B, u=C/D and the normalized midpoint is M/N, the implementation proves

\[ (AD+CB)N=M(2BD). \]

The endpoint order AD<CB gives

\[ 2AD<AD+CB<2CB,\qquad l<m<u. \]

All products have positive denominators, so the cross-multiplied inequalities preserve their directions. At m there are three exact outcomes. Equality P(m)=Q(m) retains m as an exact balance. Otherwise the midpoint order equals precisely one endpoint order; exactly one of [l,m] and [m,u] retains the order swap. The selected endpoints are ordered and form the original half-bracket. Hence

\[ m-l=u-m=\frac{u-l}{2}. \]

The base certificate is the supplied order-swapping bracket. Each successor retains either the exact balance or the unique order-swapping half. The recorded trace has n+1 states after n refinements; every state retains the balance-or-order-swap property and ordered endpoints. The midpoint identity and half selection establish strict narrowing at every nonterminal refinement, rather than an appeal to a completed infinite process.

The original square-balance witness starts with

\[ \left(\frac75\right)^2=\frac{49}{25}<2<\frac94=\left(\frac32\right)^2. \]

The exact source iteration calculates m=(l+u)/2 and replaces l by m when m²<2, otherwise u by m. Its twenty-refinement witness retains l²<2<u² and

\[ u-l=\frac{1}{10\cdot2^{20}}. \]

Every recorded transition replays this operation exactly. The original supplied-round behavior is retained, including no iterations for a negative host iteration count. This host control count is not a new scientific parameter or an admitted negative magnitude.

The implementation-distinct coefficient check uses the source family 1/2, 1/3 and 1/6. Its elementary combinations are calculated from those roots:

\[ e_1=\frac12+\frac13+\frac16=1,\]
\[ e_2=\frac12\frac13+\frac12\frac16+\frac13\frac16
=\frac{6+3+2}{36}=\frac{11}{36},\qquad
 e_3=\frac12\frac13\frac16=\frac1{36}. \]

Holding the two orientations separately gives the positive-sided cubic identity

\[ x^3+e_2x=e_1x^2+e_3,
\quad\text{thus}\quad x^3+\frac{11}{36}x=x^2+\frac1{36}. \]

The coefficients in the Lean polynomial are assembled from these root combinations. Each of the three source roots is then independently evaluated against both polynomial sides and gives exact equality. The original rational sum and pair-sum witnesses and the positive-side coefficient assembly agree.

731. Exact recurrence of every finite componentwise Fold configuration

A supplied component is a reduced positive rational part p/q, with 0<p≤q and gcd(p,q)=1. Its exact rank transition is F_q(p)=2p mod q when that remainder is positive, and q when the remainder is zero. The latter case represents the One. Applying this operation componentwise introduces no additional dynamics.

Each positive denominator has an exact decomposition

\[ q=2^a m,\qquad m>0,\quad m\text{ odd}. \]

The construction repeatedly divides an even denominator by two; each division strictly decreases the positive denominator. An odd denominator terminates the construction at depth zero. The retained denominator theorem then gives, after a+k Fold steps,

\[ \operatorname{den}\bigl(\operatorname{reduce}(F_q^{a+k}(p)/q)\bigr)=m. \]

For a finite tuple, take the maximum of these derived transient depths. The list base has no component restriction; adjoining a component replaces the retained depth by the maximum of the old depth and that component's derived depth. At this common depth A every component has its conserved odd denominator core. Neither A nor the cores are fitted inputs.

The original rank carrier is finite. For denominators q_1,…,q_n its Cartesian construction is

\[ S(q_1,\ldots,q_n)=\{1,\ldots,q_1\}\times\cdots\times\{1,\ldots,q_n\},
\qquad |S|=\prod_{i=1}^n q_i. \]

Fold preserves 0<F_q^t(p)≤q, so every generated tuple remains in this carrier. The support proof is structural: the empty product contains the empty tuple; adjoining a component enumerates every rank with every retained suffix and multiplies the cardinality by its denominator.

For the normalized component at depth A, the existing exact orbit theorem derives its first positive period ℓ_i. For an odd core m_i>1 this is the first positive exponent with 2^{ℓ_i}≡1 modulo m_i; the One component has period one. The recurrent Cartesian carrier uses the complete component orbit lists

\[ C_i=(p_i,F_{m_i}(p_i),\ldots,F_{m_i}^{\ell_i-1}(p_i)),
\qquad C=C_1\times\cdots\times C_n,\quad |C|=\prod_i\ell_i. \]

Every component state at step t equals its state at t mod ℓ_i, so the generated tuple belongs to C. The synchronized orbit need not visit every independently phased member of C; its first joint return is determined by the periods below.

To connect normalized components to the original trajectory, let g be the greatest common divisor of its rank at depth A and its original denominator. Exact normalization gives p_raw=g p and q_raw=g m. The source Fold operation satisfies

\[ F_{gm}(gp)=gF_m(p),\qquad F_{gm}^t(gp)=gF_m^t(p). \]

Induction establishes the second identity from the first. Cancellation of the positive g proves that the original component returns precisely when its normalized component returns. List induction lifts this equivalence to the entire original tuple; the recurrence certificate therefore concerns the supplied states themselves.

Write t=sℓ_i+r with 0≤r<ℓ_i. Iteration composition and the period return remove sℓ_i. If t returns, r returns; minimality of the first period forces r=0. Conversely a multiple of ℓ_i returns by induction. Thus

\[ F_{m_i}^{t}(p_i)=p_i\iff\ell_i\mid t. \]

The tuple returns exactly when every component period divides t. The existing exact least-common-return construction consequently yields

\[ L_1=\ell_1,\qquad L_{j+1}=\operatorname{lcm}(L_j,\ell_{j+1}),
\qquad L_n=\operatorname{lcm}(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_n). \]

All periods are positive. L_n returns every component, and any positive joint return t is a common multiple, hence L_n≤t. Combining this result with the normalization equivalence proves for every supplied nonempty finite tuple X

\[ F^{A+L_n}(X)=F^A(X),\qquad
0<t\ \land\ F^{A+t}(X)=F^A(X)\ \Longrightarrow\ L_n\le t. \]

The single-component case is the denominator-to-orbit construction. Adjoining a component extends the Cartesian support and replaces the joint period by its least common return with the new component. This proves the source successor statement for every finite tuple length.

The original witnesses replay the rotation (1,2,4)↦(2,4,1) over denominator seven, the four-rank orbit over denominator five, and the mixed odd-core periods

\[ \operatorname{ord}_3(2)=2,\quad\operatorname{ord}_5(2)=4,\quad
\operatorname{ord}_7(2)=3,\qquad\operatorname{lcm}(2,4,3)=12. \]

The eight original binary grammar axes retain state domain, component rule, denominator custody, support, recurrence, period, generality and addition. Their complete product contains 2⁸=256 alternatives. The source decision is equivalent to all eight admitted coordinates: finite rational tuple, componentwise Fold, conserved odd core, finite product support, exact return, least common period, tuple successor and no extra rule. Exhaustion and this equivalence establish the unique survivor. The source's exact control predicates, registration, census, decisions, closure and canonical identities are preserved and checked against the pinned original program. The independent original validator checks the complete product and adverse records. This entry retains its original formal evidence mode.

732. Derived finite-depth bound for floored Fold fluids

The generated binary Fold ladder supplies the exact positive spacing h_k=1/2^k. Its construction is the existing lower-preimage recursion, not an inserted minimum length: the lower preimage of the previous rung folds back to that rung, and k iterations return the kth rung to the One. Exact normalization establishes

\[ h_k=\frac{1}{2^k}>0,\qquad h_{k+1}=\frac{h_k}{2}. \]

At a supplied finite depth, retain each generated edge's source, destination, positive spacing s and positive velocity separation u≤1. The spacing requirement is s≥h_k. The discrete gradient magnitude is the exact quotient G=u/s. Writing u=a/b and s=c/d, the original restrictions are

\[ 0<a\le b,\quad c,d>0,\quad d\le c\,2^k. \]

The quotient is normalized from ad/(bc). Before normalization the bound follows by three explicit steps:

\[ ad\le bd\le bc\,2^k,\qquad \frac{ad}{bc}\le2^k. \]

If its normalized numerator and denominator are N and D, exact normalization preserves

\[ adD=Nbc. \]

Multiplying the preceding inequality by positive D and cancelling positive bc proves

\[ N\le2^kD,\qquad G\le2^k. \]

This proves the bound for every supplied edge, hence for every finite generated edge list. The original discrete vorticity-magnitude bound uses this same One-bounded separation over positive edge spacing. No limiting derivative or additional continuum field is introduced.

The bound is attained by the original maximal-gap/minimal-edge construction u=1 and s=h_k. Substituting into the exact quotient yields

\[ G=\frac{1}{1/2^k}=2^k. \]

Thus the cap is forced by the existing velocity ceiling and generated floor. At the first Fold depth it is two; a successor refinement divides the floor by two and multiplies the reciprocal bound by two:

\[ B_1=2,\qquad B_{k+1}=2B_k,\qquad B_k=2^k. \]

Every finite k gives a positive spacing and a finite bound. At depth five the value is 32. The original witness table checks every depth from one through fourteen using exact normalized quotients. These evaluations accompany the general depth and edge proofs; they do not replace their induction and inequalities.

Transport retains the source endpoint, destination endpoint and exact positive amount of every transfer. Mapping a finite transfer list to its ledger preserves each of these triples. The source's independent mass witness splits the same whole into two retained amounts:

734. Unique half-One reflection axis

The reflection is the original exact complement within the One, implemented by the existing guarded Take operation. For a reduced positive part p=n/d, it succeeds precisely when n<d. This condition is derived from the operation's existing guard: a successful complement has a positive remainder; conversely n<d gives that remainder. The whole One retains the original rejection because its remainder would be numerical zero. No replacement domain or new numerical value is introduced.

Let R(p)=q=a/b be the returned normalized complement. Exact normalization preserves

\[ (d-n)b=ad. \]

Adding nb to both sides gives

\[ nb+ad=db,\qquad p+q=1. \]

Both parts are positive. Consequently q<1 as well: the positive term nb makes ad<db, and cancellation of positive d gives a<b. Complement can therefore be applied again.

For the second application, the desired numerator-denominator identity is

\[ (b-a)d=nb. \]

Indeed, (b-a)d+ad=bd, while the first junction identity gives nb+ad=db. Cancelling the common positive-count summand ad yields the desired equality. The established exact normalization identity then proves

\[ R(R(p))=p. \]

Thus every admitted reflection is an involution on its original positive-part domain. Existence of each partner comes from the original Take admission theorem, not an assumed pairing table.

If p is self-complementary, set q=p in the preserved value equation:

\[ (d-n)d=nd. \]

Cancel positive d to obtain d−n=n, hence

\[ d=2n,\qquad p+p=1. \]

The existing Foundation self-junction theorem forces p to equal half-One. Conversely the existing half-One complement certificate gives R(1/2)=1/2. Combining both directions establishes the unique fixed axis:

\[ R(p)=p\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p=\frac12. \]

For every non-half part p, let q=R(p). If q=p, the fixed-axis theorem would force p=1/2. If q=1/2, involution and the half-One fixed certificate again force p=1/2. Therefore p and q are distinct and neither becomes a second fixed point. This is the original successor statement for each newly generated non-half part.

The source witnesses calculate

\[ R\!\left(\frac14\right)=\frac34,\quad
R\!\left(\frac34\right)=\frac14,\quad
R\!\left(\frac13\right)=\frac23,\quad
R\!\left(\frac23\right)=\frac13. \]

Its adverse logical control uses the two-point set S={1/4,3/4}. The explicit partner equations prove R(S)=S. Both members have reduced denominator four, so neither equals the half-One with reduced denominator two. The fixed-axis theorem then proves neither member is a fixed point. Hence

\[ R(S)=S,\qquad S\cap\{1/2\}=\varnothing. \]

This establishes the exact original distinction between an invariant set and a set consisting of fixed points. The Riemann correspondence in this entry is the derived reflection axis together with the separately derived Fold-order prime structure. Its original complex-zero boundary is enforced by this explicit symmetry control; no complex analytic continuation object enters the derivation.

The eight original binary grammar axes retain domain, involution, fixed point, off-axis pairing, prime tie, zero location, generality and addition. 737. Equality of native Fold evaluation and certificate verification

The original native domain consists of every positive finite word over the two generated fibre labels. Its deterministic evaluation is the complete suffix-closing trace E(w)=C(w) derived above. A supplied certificate is a finite sequence of states. The original verifier first checks that this sequence is nonempty, starts at w and ends at structural empty One; it then compares the complete sequence with the exact closing trace. The Lean operation preserves these checks and the original invalid-word failure.

For w in W_k with k>0, the generated-domain theorem proves that the closing evaluator accepts w. Its exact trace starts at w, terminates at empty One, and contains each forced suffix successor. Therefore the verifier accepts the evaluation itself:

\[ V(w,E(w))=\mathrm{true}. \]

Conversely, acceptance requires exact equality with that complete evaluation. The source and terminal tests alone are insufficient; the final comparison retains every intermediate state. Native proof decomposition follows the original guard branches and yields

\[ V(w,c)=\mathrm{true}\ \Longrightarrow\ c=E(w). \]

Combining completeness and soundness gives the exact certificate characterization

\[ V(w,c)=\mathrm{true}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad c=E(w),
   \qquad w\in W_k,\ k>0. \]

This is the source's two-containment argument. Every deterministic evaluation emits its accepted certificate, giving P_F within NP_F. Every accepted certificate is the unique deterministic evaluation, giving NP_F within P_F. Thus

\[ P_F=NP_F. \]

The source resource is the number of lawful closing edges retained in the trace. Since |E(w)|=|w|+1, and acceptance forces c=E(w), the evaluator and verifier use the same edge count:

The proof applies at every positive finite depth, not only at the witness depths.

738. Arbitrary native Fold circuit lower bound and attainment

Let W_r be the complete generated binary word population at positive depth r. The lawful edge from a word removes its leading label; at depth one its target is structural empty One. The original construction retains every such edge in increasing layer order:

\[ E_k=\bigcup_{r=1}^{k}\{(w,F(w)):w\in W_r\},\qquad
F(w)=\begin{cases}\operatorname{tail}(w),&|w|>1,\\\mathrm{empty\ One},&|w|=1.\end{cases} \]

The generated words at different layers have different lengths, and the binary-word construction has no duplicate word within a layer. Each edge retains its source as its first component, so distinct source words give distinct edges. The width and complete layered size therefore follow from the original binary generation:

\[ |W_k|=2^k,\qquad L_0=0,\qquad L_{k+1}=L_k+2^{k+1},\qquad
|E_k|=L_k=\sum_{r=1}^{k}2^r. \]

Assign rank zero to structural empty One and rank |w| to each generated word. Every lawful edge has source rank exactly one greater than its target rank. For an arbitrary path of n edges assembled from E_k, induction over its actual edge sequence gives

\[ \rho(w_0)=\rho(w_n)+n. \]

Consequently a closing path starting at depth k and ending at empty One has n=k. This argument applies to every lawful path, independently of the chosen circuit's other edges. The complete edge circuit attains that depth: the first forced edge removes the leading label and the remaining suffix follows its own forced path. Induction on the word constructs the entire closing path, including the depth-one edge to empty One.

For any circuit retaining the required source edge of every generated word through k, projecting its edges to their source words covers the distinct complete population. The source-cardinality bound yields

\[ |\mathrm{circuit}|\geq\sum_{r=1}^{k}2^r. \]

Likewise every circuit retaining the depth-k input population requires at least 2^k input source positions. Since E_k has exactly these inputs and edges and provides the closing paths above, all three bounds are attained together:

\[ (\mathrm{depth},\mathrm{input\ width},\mathrm{layered\ edges})
=\left(k,2^k,\sum_{r=1}^{k}2^r\right). \]

At depth three the original construction has fourteen distinct forced edges. The source enumerates every subset by its fourteen-bit mask. 739. Unbounded positive-finite fault tolerance and exact circuit composition

The original fault order is supplied as a nonempty trace with distinct position labels. Its length t counts the allowed changed positions. The trace identifies an input fault allowance; it is not a fitted scientific parameter or an additional selection of the code law. V3 derives the first correcting repetition width from strict-majority preservation. With at most t changed positions, the retained source labels must outnumber those changes. The least such total is

\[ w_t=t+(t+1)=2t+1. \]

For a generated source label a in {held, returned}, encode w_t copies. A mask selects positions to replace by the opposite generated label. The original subset generator lists all masks of cardinality 0 through t. Its existing soundness and completeness proof gives exactly

\[ M\in\mathcal M(w_t, t)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
M\text{ is a positional subset of }\{0,\ldots, w_t-1\},\quad |M|\leq t. \]

Let e be the number of changed labels and c the retained source count. The actual changed-word count proof establishes e≤|M| and c+e=w_t. Therefore

\[ e\leq t,\qquad c=2t+1-e\geq t+1>e. \]

The original decoder counts the two labels. Equal counts return the explicit no-strict-majority result; unequal counts return the majority label. Empty words or external labels raise the original domain error. Reusing the verified general correction results with these exact output distinctions proves recovery for both source labels and every allowed mask. No stochastic error distribution or sampled mask selection enters this argument.

Minimality is constructive. For each positive predecessor width 1≤w≤2t, the source changes the first q=⌈w/2⌉ positions:

\[ q=\left\lfloor\frac{w+1}{2}\right\rfloor,\qquad
x_w=(\underbrace{\mathrm{returned},\ldots,\mathrm{returned}}_{q},
     \underbrace{\mathrm{held},\ldots,\mathrm{held}}_{w-q}). \]

The native translation builds this word from the original ordered position range. Its count proofs derive the two counts from that construction. Quotient/remainder arithmetic establishes

\[ q\leq t,\qquad w-q\leq q. \]

Thus the counterexample uses an allowed number of changes and either ties or reverses the original held majority. Every predecessor width fails; width 2t+1 corrects every allowed mask. \[ (2t+1)-1=2t,\qquad
w_{t+1}=2(t+1)+1=w_t+2. \]

The first positive order yields width three: widths one and two admit the counterexamples above, while width three retains at least two original labels against one change. The same arithmetic applies to every supplied positive finite order, and t+1 defeats any proposed terminal finite fault-order ceiling.

For the source's canonical worst mask, the first t positions change and the remaining t+1 retain the original label. Native count proofs establish exact decoding at arbitrary t for each label. Induction over the complete source word then yields

\[ R_t(a_1,\ldots, a_n)=(a_1,\ldots, a_n). \]

The recovered word is the identical input to the existing reversible circuit semantics. Replacing that word in an arbitrary retained branch position preserves the complete input state, including all surrounding branches and the phase cycle. 755. Free-particle Fold phase and exact dispersion

An admitted phase is an exact rational φ with 0<φ≤1. Its momentum carrier p satisfies 0<p≤1/2. For any positive exact rational x, write C(x) for the original operation that repeatedly subtracts a complete One while x>1. The endpoint One is retained: C(1)=1 and C(k)=1 for every positive integer k. The existing complete-One removal proof establishes positivity, termination, uniqueness and the upper bound C(x)≤1.

The source cyclic advance is A(φ,a)=C(φ+a), with a>0. On a common positive denominator d, its subtraction recurrence is

C_d(n)=n when n≤d,
C_d(n)=C_d(n−d) when n>d,
C(n/d)=C_d(n)/d,

with the last fraction reduced exactly. Scaling numerator and denominator together preserves this value. Normalization therefore changes its representation without changing the cyclic phase.

To compare successive advances, apply induction to the complete-One removal trace. If n≤d, C_d(C_d(n)+m)=C_d(n+m) immediately. At a removal step, n=(n−d)+d. Adding m preserves this one-complete-turn difference, so the induction hypothesis and C_d(k+d)=C_d(k), for k>0, give

C_d(C_d(n)+m)=C_d(n+m).

Cross multiplication and exact reduction carry this identity between arbitrary positive rational denominators. Consequently

A(A(φ,a),b)=C(C(φ+a)+b)=C(φ+a+b)=A(φ,a+b).

For the source momentum domain, 2p≤1. Thus its Fold dispersion is F(p)=C(2p)=2p, including the endpoint p=1/2. Substituting a=b=p gives the full free-phase relation

A(φ,F(p))=A(φ,2p)=A(A(φ,p),p).

This is established for every admitted phase and momentum. FreePhase.sourceAdvance and sourcePartAdvance connect the count-pair proof to the actual cyclicAdvance executable, including its exact fraction and positive-carrier guards. originalFoldTwoStepIdentity proves equality of the two original executable routes. No conventional dispersion equation is supplied as a premise.

The original witness uses φ=1/3 and p=1/4. Its dispersion and both phase routes are

A(1/3,1/2)=C(5/6)=5/6,
A(1/3,1/4)=C(7/12)=7/12,
A(7/12,1/4)=C(10/12)=5/6.

For subsequent ticks, let X₀=Y₀=φ, Xₙ₊₁=A(Xₙ,F(p)) and Yₙ₊₁=A(A(Yₙ,p),p). The base equality is immediate. If Xₙ=Yₙ, the proved single-tick identity gives Xₙ₊₁=Yₙ₊₁. 761. Magnetic correction as an exact Fold-covariant partition

t=v²,

t+C(v)=1.

For v=n/d with positive integers n<d, exact multiplication and positive subtraction give

t=n²/d²,
C(v)=(d²−n²)/d²>0.

The strict inequality follows from n²<nd<d². All fractions are normalized by the same exact carrier operations. The partition therefore survives normalization: its numerator sum is n²+(d²−n²)=d², and division by d² returns One. MagneticSourceProofs.exactPartition and positiveRemainder establish these identities for every admitted speed.

The Fold acts on a positive part x by doubling its support and retaining the complete-One convention:

F(x)=2x when 2x≤1,
F(x)=2x−1 when 2x>1.

For the square t, the two complementary branches are explicit. If t<1/2,

F(t)=2t,
F(1−t)=2(1−t)−1=1−2t=1−F(t).

If t>1/2,

F(t)=2t−1,
F(1−t)=2(1−t)=2−2t=1−F(t).

The equality t=1/2 cannot occur for a positive rational speed. It would require d²=2n². An odd integer has an odd square, so d must be even: d=2k. Substitution and exact cancellation yield n²=2k². The original equality also forces n<d, since n≥d would give d²≤n²<2n²=d². Thus the same positive-square equation would recur with the strictly smaller denominator n. Induction on the positive denominator excludes such an equation. MagneticSquare.noHalfSquare proves that descent constructively; no numerical approximation to a square root or additional axiom is used.

The normalized count proof retains both branches rather than sampling them. At a common denominator D, let N be the square numerator and D−N its positive complement. The two doubled-and-cast counts satisfy

cast(2N,D)+cast(2(D−N),D)=D,

with both retained counts positive. Hence the second count is exactly D minus the first. MagneticCovariance.complementaryCounts and foldComplement connect this count identity through the existing exact normalization and Fold operations to F(1−t)=1−F(t).

The complete source operation returns

(speed_square,electric_remainder,folded_remainder)
=(v²,1−v²,F(1−v²)).

766. Complete finite-loop sums and their positive remainder

The source starts at the generated half-One carrier and appends one exactly halved positive term at every further finite depth. For depth N≥1, write t₁=S₁=1/2 and

tₙ₊₁=tₙ/2,
Sₙ₊₁=Sₙ+tₙ₊₁.

No input determines the binary factor: it is the previously generated binary count. Depth records how many generated terms are retained. The original operation rejects Boolean inputs, zero and negative depths, then checks that its exact result is positive and strictly below One.

The complete denominator at depth n is Dₙ=2ⁿ. At that common denominator the source-ordered term weights are

W₀=[],
Wₙ₊₁=double(Wₙ) followed by [1].

Doubling every earlier weight preserves every earlier term when the denominator doubles; appending the final weight 1 retains the new half-sized term. If Aₙ is the sum of all weights, the already proved DyadicClosure.weightSuccessor and completeLedger give

A₀=0,
Aₙ₊₁=2Aₙ+1,
Aₙ+1=2ⁿ.

The empty initial list is bookkeeping for this induction; every source-admitted depth is positive. The base source state is (S₁,t₁)=(1/2,1/2). At the successor, the prior exact state is (Aₙ/Dₙ,1/Dₙ). Halving its last term yields 1/(2Dₙ), while the total becomes

Aₙ/Dₙ+1/(2Dₙ)
=2Aₙ/(2Dₙ)+1/(2Dₙ)
=(2Aₙ+1)/(2Dₙ)
=Aₙ₊₁/Dₙ₊₁.

FiniteLoopProofs.halveRatio and appendHalfTerm prove these exact normalized arithmetic steps. completeLoopState connects them by induction to the actual source-order accumulator, retaining both the running total and its latest term. Hence, at every positive finite depth,

Sₙ=Aₙ/2ⁿ=(2ⁿ−1)/2ⁿ,
tₙ=1/2ⁿ,
Sₙ+tₙ=1.

The identity Aₙ+1=2ⁿ leaves a strictly positive remainder. For n≥1, Aₙ>0 and Aₙ<2ⁿ, so 0<Sₙ<1. sourcePositiveDepth proves that the original operation's boundary test succeeds and returns this exact total for every positive depth. This establishes the source's finite-depth closure through the operation itself, in addition to its concrete witnesses.

The first six complete sums are

S₁=1/2,
S₂=1/2+1/4=3/4,
S₃=3/4+1/8=7/8,
S₄=7/8+1/16=15/16,
S₅=15/16+1/32=31/32,
S₆=31/32+1/64=63/64.

The second original witness checks all sixteen generated depths from 1 through 16. Both original witnesses, all 256 combinations of the eight binary grammar axes, every elimination decision, controls and complete registration are preserved. The source explicitly concerns generated finite supports; it introduces neither a completed infinite support nor a fitted radiative coefficient or subtraction counterterm. Its exact retained remainder is part of the derivation.

771. Weak gravitational potential and conserved source flux

The positive inertial-energy source is distributed over the rank-two boundary already derived in the inverse-square and source entries. For exact source s and radius r, the original operation admits 0<s<r≤1 and computes

F(s,r)=s/(r·r),
Φ(s,r)=(F(s,r)·r)·r=s,
P(s,r)=1−s/r.

The boundary rank fixes the two radius factors; there is no adjustable exponent. To see the cancellation explicitly, write s=a/b and r=c/d, with positive integer carriers and ad<bc. Then

F=(a/b)/(c²/d²)=ad²/(bc²),
F·r=ad/(bc),
(F·r)·r=a/b=s,
s/r=ad/(bc)<1,
P=(bc−ad)/(bc)>0.

The numerator bc−ad is positive by the original source/radius ordering. The operation positive_take first requires exact fractions, an ordered whole/part pair and a positive part. Equality returns the empty structural record (); strict inequality returns the exact difference. Thus the clock potential is a positive retained carrier, while equality of a general take is represented by absence rather than by a numerical zero carrier.

GravitySourceProofs.admittedSourceRecord proves the complete three-field output of the actual guarded weakGravity operation for every positive source and radius satisfying the original inequalities, including r≤1. It uses InverseSquare.exactResponse and CoulombGauss.sequentialFluxReturnsSource for the two successive radius multiplications. sourceProduct and sourceQuotient connect the exact normalized rational operations to those existing carriers; takeBelowOne proves that the original take returns the retained difference. This is the source conservation argument for each generated radius, not an extrapolation from the two shell examples.

The original examples instantiate that derivation:

s=1/8,r=1/4: F=2, Φ=1/8, P=1/2;
s=1/8,r=1/2: F=1/2, Φ=1/8, P=3/4.

GravityFlux.innerSourceRecord and outerSourceRecord establish all returned fields. 772. Exact causal interval and the generated 3–4–5 partition

788. Terminal quark self-coupling dressing

The original dressing operation reuses the sealed inverse fine-structure result and the generated cover depths. Write

R_up=A/(A+u)=1/(1+7/A).

Substituting the already derived rational A gives the exact intermediate arithmetic

A+2=(503846395469+2·3676744786)/3676744786
    =511199885041/3676744786,
D_down=511199885041/503846395469,
A+7=(503846395469+7·3676744786)/3676744786
    =529583608971/3676744786,
R_up=503846395469/529583608971.

828. Complete principal shells, generated filling recurrence and periodic closure

The filling walk is generated from joint cover, not from a table of configurations. For each cover c=2,...,M, visit principal ranks p=1,...,c-1 in order, set r=c-p, and emit (p,r) exactly when r<=p. 829. Exact transition rates, complete-channel lifetimes and electric multipole succession

The admitted elementary transition retains one orbital unit. For an exact generated level gap x with 0<x<1, held positive line strength S and positive whole upper-state weight g, the complete spatial volume supplies the E1 power x^3. Electric rank L appends a held boundary pair at each successor. Its exponent is
  e(1)=3, e(L)=2L+1,
  e(L+1)=2(L+1)+1=(2L+1)+2.
The first four exponents are 3,5,7,9. The normalized source rate is
  A_L(x,S,g)=x^(2L+1) S/g.
The input guards retain the original exact-Fraction gap and strength domains, the strict-part gap boundary, and the positive-integer weight/rank domains excluding Booleans. The default electric rank remains One.

The source power operation is formalised by exact rational multiplication:
  P(x,0)=1, P(x,k+1)=P(x,k)x.
For every positive rational gap x=n/d, induction gives
  P(n/d,k)=n^k/d^k.
For every positive strength S=s/t and weight g=w+1, direct multiplication and division consequently give the source-specific universal rate formula
  A_L=(n^(2L+1)s)/(d^(2L+1)t(w+1)).
This formula is proved for arbitrary admitted numerators, denominators, weights and positive ranks, rather than inferred from selected numerical outputs.

  A_(L+1)=x^(2L+3)S/g
         =(x^(2L+1)S/g)x^2
         =A_L x^2.
The Lean theorem relates the actual normalizedElectricRate operations at successive ranks. For n,d>0 and n<d, n^2<d^2, hence
  0<x^2=n^2/d^2<1.

The empty list and any non-Fraction or nonpositive channel retain the original rejection. The original exact witness is

Every channel is retained in the sum; no independent lifetime value enters the formal operation.

All 1,024 candidates are generated and decided with the original controls, induction and closure. 830. Terminal atomic field splitting: held angular support, Zeeman spacing and typed Stark response

Let q be the positive whole doubled-angular count. The complete held support has q positions and its retained successor class, hence
\[
 N(q)=q+1,\qquad N(q+1)=N(q)+1.
\]
The conventional name q=2J therefore gives 2J+1 sublevels. The first six admitted inputs produce 2,3,4,5,6,7. One magnetic field act for each held orientation gives Z(g,m,B)=gmB for positive exact rational g,B. For g=a/d and B=b/e, the translated operation returns precisely
\[
 Z(a/d,m,b/e)=\frac{amb}{de}.
\]
Appending one orientation preserves the same field act:
\[
 Z(g,m+1,B)=g(m+1)B=gmB+gB=Z(g,m,B)+gB.
\]
Thus the adjacent spacing is the common carrier gB, rather than a separately selected spacing. \[

 Q(a/d,b/e)=\frac{ab^2}{2de^2}.
\]
Consequently L(p,2E)=2L(p,E) and Q(p,2E)=4Q(p,E); likewise Z(g,m,2B)=2Z(g,m,B). The original witnesses use g=3/2,m=2 and fields 1/5,2/5, giving Zeeman magnitudes 3/5,6/5. 844. Exact scattering support, Rutherford transfer and Compton conservation

A nonforward direction-transfer part is an exact positive rational u with 0<u≤1. The unchanged direction is the structural empty transfer, not a numerical zero substituted into a reciprocal. The established phase-compatible transition carrier supplies one overlap leg L(u)=1/u. Pairing preparation-to-transfer and transfer-to-record legs gives
W(u)=L(u)L(u)=1/u².
This is exact self-composition of the admitted overlap carrier. The source does not insert a complex amplitude or a measured angular weight. The native pairedDensityForEveryAdmittedPart and pairedDensityIsReciprocalSquare proofs derive the reciprocal-square result from overlapLeg and pairedOverlapDensity for every admitted rational part; everyPositivePartAdmitted proves the executable guards for positive fractions a/b with a≤b.

The Coulomb direction partition retains a complementary hand 1−u for u<1. Its cumulative incident-area support is C(u)=(1−u)/u=1/u−1. Complete backscatter u=1 leaves the complementary hand structurally empty. For 0<a<b<1, the exact area removed across a transfer interval is
C(a)−C(b)=(1/a−1)−(1/b−1)=(b−a)/(ab).
Dividing by the positive interval b−a gives
[C(a) take C(b)]/[b take a]=1/(ab).
At b=1 the removed area is C(a) itself and the interval is 1−a, so C(a)/(1−a)=1/a=1/(a·1). Thus the endpoint uses the same reciprocal-product identity while retaining the structural empty upper area. No signed formal area or limiting numerical approximation is required.

The proof works directly with the source operations on exact fractions. Writing a=A/D and b=B/D gives 0<A<B≤D. In the interior,
(D−A)B=(D−B)A+D(B−A),
so the positive area difference is D(B−A)/(AB), the positive interval is (B−A)/D, and their quotient is D²/(AB)=1/(ab). The backscatter case B=D is proved separately with the empty upper area; everyOrderedAnnularDensity combines the two cases and everyAnnularReciprocalProduct identifies their common formula. Any two positive rational parts admit a common positive denominator by multiplying their denominators. The numerator cross-products preserve their original order and both fractions exactly. The proofs use the original source guards, which everyOrderedIntervalAdmitted establishes from 0<A<B≤D.

For a positive conserved charge-product carrier Q and incident-energy carrier E, the backscatter approach support is Q/(4E). Pairing it gives
S(Q,E)=[Q/(4E)]²=Q²/(16E²),
and the differential support is
D(Q,E,u)=S(Q,E)W(u)=Q²/(16E²u²).
For Q=N/D and E=P/R, the native general formula is (NR)²/[D(4P)]². Therefore doubling Q multiplies the support by four, while doubling E divides it by four. At the external angular correspondence u=sin²(θ/2), the angular factor becomes sin⁻⁴(θ/2), the Rutherford relation. The formal positive transfer-part derivation is complete before that dimensional and angular reading is opened. Its registered comparison retains the nonrelativistic point-boundary conditions.

Closed photon–electron transfer uses the positive incident/rest-energy ratio x and the same direction part u. The wavelength increase in Compton carriers is Δ(u)=2u. The outgoing/incident energy ratio is
r(x,u)=1/(1+2xu),
and outgoing energy in electron-rest units is
F(x,u)=xr(x,u)=x/(1+2xu).
These formulas are implemented by photonShiftInComptonCarriers, scatteredPhotonEnergyRatio and scatteredPhotonInRestUnits. The native general normalized forms for x=P/Q and u=A/B are

They preserve arbitrary positive incident carriers and every admitted direction part; the source's comparisons at four transfer parts are not used in place of these general proofs.

The actual conservation operation takes the inverse incident support from the inverse outgoing support:

Equating this positive wavelength-transfer support to 2u gives
1−r=2xur,       1=r(1+2xu),       r=1/(1+2xu).
The native proof first calculates the source operation for x=P/Q and r=T/V, with 0<T<V:

H(u)−F(n,u)
 =1/(2u)−n/(1+2un)
 =[(1+2un)−2un]/[2u(1+2un)]
 =1/[2u(1+2un)]>0.
The successor difference is
F(n+1,u)−F(n,u)

Thus every generated successor increases outgoing rest-energy support while remaining below its ceiling. 845. Terminal decay widths, complete branching partitions and lifetimes

An open decay channel retains a positive overlap leg l, generated available-output support E and action carrier A. Pairing the transition leg with its return gives l². Composition with output support and division by action therefore yield
γ=l²E/A.
For l=L/K, E=P/Q and A=U/V, the exact generated carrier is
γ=[(L²/K²)(P/Q)]/(U/V)=L²PV/(K²QU).
All six numerator and denominator counts are positive. The original operation rejects nonpositive carriers. A closed channel is the empty form (), and is not inserted into an open-channel family as a numerical null. partialWidthForEveryPositiveCarrier verifies this formula for every admitted positive rational triple; closedChannelIsEmpty verifies the distinct empty representation.

For a nonempty ordered family (γ₁,…,γₙ), the total starts with γ₁ and folds positive addition over the remaining channels:
Γ₁=γ₁,             Γₙ₊₁=Γₙ+γₙ₊₁.
No numerical-null seed is used. totalForEveryAdmittedFamily identifies the original total operation with this fold. appendedSourceFamily and totalAfterEveryAdmittedSuccessor connect the original guarded append operation to the displayed successor equality. The appended channel is validated as positive before it enters the family.

On a common denominator D, adjoining numerator m changes the total from N/D to (N+m)/D. The exact increment is [(N+m)−N]/D=m/D, the appended width itself. successorIncrementForEveryCommonDenominatorFamily verifies this equality through the original successorTotalIncrement operation.

Every such rational family admits a constructed common denominator D. If the retained tail is represented by numerators nᵢ over D and the next carrier is p/q, extend the denominator to Dq, the tail numerators to nᵢq and the new numerator to pD. The equalities
nᵢ/D=(nᵢq)/(Dq),             p/q=(pD)/(Dq)
preserve every carrier and its order. All new numerators and the new denominator remain positive. Starting from the empty denominator bookkeeping value One, this construction covers every finite list; the physical total still starts with its first positive channel. everyPositiveFamilyHasCommonDenominator proves this representation from the actual positive-numerator guards. The common denominator is determined from existing inputs and is neither a scientific fit nor an additional physical parameter.

Writing γᵢ=nᵢ/D and N=n₁+⋯+nₙ gives Γ=N/D. Each branch is its own width divided by the complete total:
bᵢ=γᵢ/Γ=(nᵢ/D)/(N/D)=nᵢ/N.
Complete exclusive composition then gives
b₁+⋯+bₙ=(n₁+⋯+nₙ)/N=N/N=One.
For the first channel alone, N=n₁ and b₁=One. For a successor channel γₙ₊₁, every branch uses the enlarged common total Γₙ+γₙ₊₁, so
Σᵢ₌₁ⁿ⁺¹ γᵢ/(Γₙ+γₙ₊₁)
 =(Γₙ+γₙ₊₁)/(Γₙ+γₙ₊₁)=One.
branchingForEveryCommonDenominatorFamily establishes the normalized vector. completePartitionForEveryAdmittedFamily combines the constructive representation and finite-sum induction to prove the actual completeBranchingPartition operation equals One for every admitted nonempty source family. enlargedFamilyStillPartitionsOne proves the same result after the actual append operation. These are arbitrary-family proofs, independent of the finite witness vector.

Duration is fixed by action-width reciprocity:
τ=A/Γ.
For A=a/b and Γ=n/d, τ=ad/(bn); lifetimeForEveryPositiveCarrier verifies that exact operation and its guards. If Γₐ=n/d and Γᵦ=m/e with ne<md, then
τₐ=ad/(bn),             τᵦ=ae/(bm),
(ae)(bn)<(ad)(bm).
The final inequality is the original width inequality multiplied by positive ab and reordered, so τᵦ<τₐ. everyPositiveWidthOrder proves that the original widerStateLifetimeTake operation accepts this reversed duration ordering and returns the exact positive take of the shorter duration from the longer. Thus increased open-channel width strictly shortens duration while retaining the same action carrier.

858. Finite accumulated separation: complete tail bound and constructive tolerance

Each positive support level retains the exact ordered gap sum from Section 857. Write D_j=(2+2^j)(3+2^j), so g_(j+1)=1/D_j. To express an arbitrary finite sum without an infinite-series premise, retain its numerator and denominator ledger. Starting at depth a, put p_(a,0)=0 and q_(a,0)=1 as the empty accumulator, and append the next positive gap by
p_(a,m+1)=p_(a,m) D_(a+m)+q_(a,m),
q_(a,m+1)=q_(a,m) D_(a+m).
Thus p_(a,m+1)/q_(a,m+1)=p_(a,m)/q_(a,m)+1/D_(a+m). The positive source sum starts with its first gap; the empty accumulator is only the ledger's base representation. The theorem originalAccumulateLedger identifies this recurrence with the actual ordered addition operation, and originalEveryPartialSum identifies S_N=p_(0,N)/q_(0,N) for every N>=1.

For a>=1, the strict successor contraction gives 2D_j<D_(j+1) and hence D_a 2^m<=D_(a+m). Induction through the displayed ledger recurrence gives the finite budget
p_(a,m) D_a 2^m+2q_(a,m)<=2^(m+1)q_(a,m).
The strictly positive second term implies p_(a,m)D_a<2q_(a,m), after cancellation of the positive factor 2^m. Therefore every finite tail from level a+1 through level a+m satisfies
sum_(j=0)^(m-1) g_(a+j+1)<2/D_a.
The actual finiteTailEnvelope operation uses m>=1; originalEveryFiniteTail proves its returned comparison for every admitted pair of endpoints, not only the witness range.

Separate the first gap from N-1 remaining gaps. The head-tail ledger identity is
p_(0,N)=12p_(1,N-1)+q_(1,N-1),
q_(0,N)=12q_(1,N-1).
Consequently S_N=1/12+p_(1,N-1)/q_(1,N-1). Nonnegativity supplies the lower bound; the finite-tail bound with D_1=20 supplies the strict upper bound:
1/12<=S_N<1/12+2/20=11/60.
For N=1, equality holds at the lower endpoint; for N>=2 the appended positive tail makes the lower inequality strict. originalEveryBracketCheck proves that the original accumulation_is_bounded operation returns true for every positive input level.

For any supplied positive tolerance denominator d, the original search starts at level 2 and advances while 2g_level>=1/d. At offset j from that start, the tested strict stopping condition is exactly 2/D_(j+1)<1/d. Cross multiplication with positive denominators gives 2d<D_(j+1). Positive-count induction establishes k+1<=2^k; taking j=2d+2 therefore gives 2d<D_(2d+3), a finite termination witness. The implementation tests every source comparison in order and returns at its first success. SourceSearchRun records those actual unsuccessful comparisons followed by the successful comparison. originalToleranceTrace proves this trace for every positive d, and originalEveryTolerance proves that tolerance_is_witnessed returns true at the returned level. The recursion bound is calculated from d solely to implement the terminating original loop; it neither selects the returned level nor introduces a scientific parameter.

Their ordered names, questions, elimination reasons and conjunction of original preservation conditions are retained. The admitted envelope is assembled as 1/12+2(1/20)=11/60. m-1-j=j,   m-1=2j,   q=j/(2j)=1/2.

Conversely 1-1/2=1/2. Thus half-One is precisely the self-antipodal mode. The source does not select an index from an incomplete list: originalModeCoverage proves that the generated range contains exactly every integer index 0<j<m-1, and originalModeIndexUnique proves that distinct indices cannot become the same normalized rational mode. The complete lists in section 872 therefore establish membership in each of the forced odd sectors and absence from the two-sector interior. originalTableMassClosure checks the actual four returned table records: c_m+mu_m=1 and mu_m>0 for every sector in the forced ladder.

Write the positive common support R=k+1. The actual running operation returns

c_m(R)=(m+k)/(m+k+1),
1-c_m(R)=[(m+k+1)-(m+k)]/(m+k+1)=1/(m+k+1).

For a=m+k and b=n+k with m<n, comparison of these positive fractions is exact cross multiplication:

a(b+1)=ab+a < ab+b=b(a+1).

Consequently c_m(R)<c_n(R), so they cannot coincide. Subtraction over the common denominator gives

b/(b+1)-a/(a+1)
 =[b(a+1)-a(b+1)]/[(a+1)(b+1)]
 =(b-a)/[(a+1)(b+1)]
 =(n-m)/[(m+R)(n+R)] >0.

originalRunningFormula, originalShortfall, originalRunningOrder and originalRunningGap bind these identities to the source operations, preserving the source's forced-sector admission and ordered-pair guard. originalPositiveGap proves positivity. Every three distinct sectors contain an ordered pair, so exact finite triple coincidence is excluded by the same strict inequality; no numerical tolerance substitutes for noncoincidence.

At a binary support successor R -> 2R, R>0 implies m+2R>m+R and n+2R>n+R. Both factors are positive, hence

(m+2R)(n+2R)>(m+R)(n+R),
0<(n-m)/[(m+2R)(n+2R)]<(n-m)/[(m+R)(n+R)].

originalGapShrinks uses the retained RunningConvergence.doubledGapDenominatorIncreases result and exact normalized-rational comparison to prove this strict decrease. For every source depth d>=1, R=2^(d-1) is positive, so the same identities apply at every depth, without a finite-depth cutoff.

891. Generated composite-sector orbits and positive complements

The partition starts at the least remaining label, appends its orbit, removes precisely its members, and repeats. Thus the implementation preserves both the order within each original orbit and the least-label order of the orbit rows. The native recursion uses the finite support cardinality as its iteration budget. The first-return derivation and the exported orbit-operation completion proof below establish that this budget does not truncate an admitted orbit.

For every 0<k<d, the original complement is c=d−k. Positivity follows from k<d; c<d follows from k>0. Exact subtraction gives c+k=d, hence k+c=d. If another positive label h satisfies k+h=d, subtracting k gives h=d−k=c. Applying the operation twice gives d−(d−k)=k. Finally c=k would imply d=2k and therefore d mod 2=0, contradicting the odd-denominator identity d mod 2=1. These four general complement statements are kernel-checked with empty axiom dependencies, using the existing exact-subtraction and modular arithmetic results.
