903. Native reconstruction of the exact velocity operation

The forward/held representation is connected directly to the source operations, including their guards and typed limiting branches. Let u=n/(n+a) and v=m/(m+b) be admitted positive sublimit inputs, with n>0, a>0, b>0 and positive denominators d=n+a and e=m+b. The acceptance equations speed(u)=ok(u) and speed(v)=ok(v) are the existing source guards. They do not introduce a coefficient or a new scientific premise. The exact normalized subtraction theorem already used in the earlier hadron derivation gives (n+a)/d−n/d=a/d. Consequently the original held_pair operation returns

    held_pair(u)=((n+a+n)/d, a/d),
    held_pair(v)=((m+b+m)/e, b/e).

The native theorem originalComposedHeldSublimit then evaluates the actual compose_held_pairs operation, rather than a replacement representation:

    compose_held_pairs(u,v)=(F/(de), H/(de)),
    F=(n+a+n)(m+b+m),  H=ab.

Set N=n(m+b)+m(n+a) and D=(n+a)(m+b)+nm. The exact expansions from section 902 give F=H+2N and F+H=2D. Since n>0 and e>0, N>0. Therefore H/(de)<(H+2N)/(de), so the original recover_speed guard succeeds. The existing normalized division and subtraction operations yield

    recover_speed((F/(de),H/(de)))
      = ((F−H)/(de))/((F+H)/(de))
      = 2N/(2D)
      = N/D
      = (u+v)/(1+uv).

originalRecoverNormalized establishes the corresponding operation for every positive increment δ and positive denominator q: a pair ((h+δ)/q,h/q) recovers δ/(h+δ+h). originalProductRecovery substitutes h=H, δ=2N and q=de; originalReconstructionSublimit binds this result to the original composition of the two held pairs. The proof uses the earlier exact subtraction, multiplication, division and normalization results. No external kinematic transformation is a premise.

At u=One the held component is the original EMPTY constructor. originalHeldPairLimit gives (2,EMPTY). The source product makes EMPTY absorbing in either argument, and recover_speed returns One immediately for that constructor. originalReconstructionLeftLimit and originalReconstructionRightLimit prove both branches directly, including the original order of source guards. The pre-existing typed-rest branches retain their exact identity behavior.

922. Complete paired-population multiplicity and forced half-One equilibrium

For a positive generated pair count n, the original population is 2n. Its full census contains every upper-label count k=0,…,2n and its exact multiplicity

    B(2n,k)=(2n)!/[k!·(2n−k)!].

The central maximum follows from these source multiplicities. To show the integer quotient and its ordering explicitly, write M(a,b)=B(a+b,a). The counting recurrence has boundary values M(0,b)=M(a,0)=1 and successor

    M(a+1,b+1)=M(a,b+1)+M(a+1,b).

The two summands partition the complete count by the next held label. Its connection to the original factorial quotient is exact:

    M(a,b)·a!·b!=(a+b)!.

At the boundary this is 1·1·b!=b!. For the successor, multiply the recurrence by (a+1)!·(b+1)!. The first summand becomes (a+1)·(a+b+1)! and the second becomes (b+1)·(a+b+1)!, using the two preceding identities. Their sum is

    [(a+1)+(b+1)]·(a+b+1)!=(a+b+2)!.

Thus the quotient in the original operation is the same positive integer M(a,b); it is not rounded or replaced by a different census. ThermalEquilibriumPaired.originalSplitMultiplicity proves this connection for every a,b. The factorial identity also gives the exact adjacent relation

    (a+1)·M(a+1,b)=(b+1)·M(a,b+1).

When a<b, the right coefficient is strictly larger and M(a,b+1)>0. Therefore

    M(a,b+1)<M(a+1,b).

This is the source count's strict increase toward balance, established by originalAdjacentMultiplicity. Iterating it toward the midpoint gives

    M(a,a+2(d+1))<M(a+d+1,a+d+1),    d≥0.

For k<n, write n=k+d+1; the last inequality is B(2n,k)<B(2n,n). For k>n, the exact factorial identity is symmetric in the two label counts: B(2n,k)=B(2n,2n−k). Since 2n−k<n, the preceding inequality applies. Consequently

    0≤k≤2n and k≠n  ⇒  B(2n,k)<B(2n,n).

923. Exact factorial comparison for the fixed-population multinomial census

The original multinomial operation divides the factorial of the complete population by each component factorial. Its denominator comparison can be expressed entirely in positive integer arithmetic. For a positive target count t and any competing nonnegative count c,

    t!·t^c ≤ c!·t^t,

with strict inequality when c>t. For c≤t, write t=c+d. Every factor of (c+1)(c+2)…(c+d) is at most t, so

    t!≤c!·t^d,
    t!·t^c≤c!·t^(d+c)=c!·t^t.

For c=t+d, begin at equality for d=0. Advancing to c+1 multiplies the left comparison by t while the right factorial grows by c+1>t. Since the factorial and power factors are positive, each such successor makes the comparison strict. ThermalEquilibriumMultinomial.originalFactorialWeightBound and originalExcessCountStrictBound prove these statements for the exact factorial operation used by the source.

For aligned target and competing vectors t=(t₀,…,t_(L−1)) and c=(c₀,…,c_(L−1)), define the products of these same factors:

    F(t)=∏ᵢtᵢ!,    P(t,c)=∏ᵢtᵢ^cᵢ.

Multiplying every coordinate inequality, with each tᵢ>0, gives

    F(t)·P(t,c) ≤ F(c)·P(t,t).

If at least one cᵢ>tᵢ, its coordinate inequality is strict and all remaining factors are positive; hence the product inequality is strict. originalProductBound and originalExcessProductStrict prove both results over the complete aligned vectors.

The original fixed-population condition is the exact equality Σᵢtᵢ=Σᵢcᵢ. Under equal lengths, either the vectors coincide or some competing coordinate exceeds its target. This alternative is constructive: compare the first counts; an excess supplies the witness immediately. Otherwise the tail cannot have a smaller total if the complete competing total is at least the target total. Continue through the finite tail. If no excess occurs, the tail vectors coincide and total equality forces the first counts to coincide as well. originalEqualPopulationAlternative proves this alternative using the original fold-left population sums.

Combining the preceding results yields the exact conditional denominator comparison

    t≠c,    Σᵢtᵢ=Σᵢcᵢ,    P(t,c)=P(t,t)
       ⇒ F(t)<F(c).

Indeed, unequal equal-population vectors supply an excess coordinate, giving F(t)P(t,c)<F(c)P(t,t); equality of the two power products then permits the same positive integer factor to be cancelled. originalFixedPopulationDenominatorStrict proves this implication. Its power-product equality is an explicit hypothesis of this intermediate theorem. The factorial and power products are arithmetic expressions over the existing candidate counts; they add no input fields or selection choices to the source operation. 924. Fixed count and throw force the multinomial maximum

Let L=n+2 and let the original dyadic target be dᵢ=2^(L−1−i), for 0≤i<L. Write N(c)=Σᵢcᵢ and E(c)=Σᵢi cᵢ for the original population and indexed throw. For every length-L nonnegative count vector c,

    P(d,c)·2^E(c)
      = ∏ᵢ 2^((L−1−i)cᵢ) · ∏ᵢ 2^(i cᵢ)
      = ∏ᵢ 2^((L−1)cᵢ)
      = 2^((L−1)N(c)).

The complementary exponents are ordinary natural numbers because every enumerated index satisfies i<L. If N(c)=N(d) and E(c)=E(d), the right sides coincide. Cancelling the positive common factor 2^E(d) gives P(d,c)=P(d,d). Thus the power-product equality in Section 923 follows from the original two conserved counts; it is not an additional selection premise. Every dᵢ is positive. For c≠d, Section 923 therefore gives F(d)<F(c).

The source computes multiplicity by sequential integer division. This operation has the exact identity

    M(c)·F(c)=N(c)! ,    M(c)>0.

To establish exact division, split the list as a::s, with b=N(s). The source binomial count B(a+b,a) obeys B(a+b,a)·a!·b!=(a+b)!, and the tail multiplicity obeys M(s)·F(s)=b!. Multiplication gives

    [B(a+b,a)·M(s)]·[a!·F(s)]=(a+b)!.

Induction begins with the empty list, whose factorial product and multiplicity are both one. At each sequential division the remaining factorial product is an exact factor, so the implemented quotients agree with this positive integer multiplicity. No real-valued approximation or alternative division rule is used. Equal populations now give

    M(c)F(c)=N! =M(d)F(d).

Since F(d)<F(c) and both multiplicities are positive, M(c)≥M(d) would imply M(c)F(c)>M(d)F(d), a contradiction. Hence every distinct admissible competitor satisfies M(c)<M(d).

929. Complete finite occupation words and the cold occupation measure

For N positive occupants and L positive generated levels, the original occupation walk holds a prefix and a remaining population. At each nonterminal cell it enumerates every integer c from zero through min(cap, remaining), in that order, and recurses on remaining−c. At the last cell it emits the remaining population exactly when it is at most cap. The preserving class uses cap=N; the alternating class uses cap=1. Zero is the source's empty-cell record.

The walk invariant and its converse are

    emitted word = prefix ++ suffix,
    length(suffix) = remaining levels,
    sum(suffix) = remaining population,
    every suffix coordinate ≤ cap.

The base case has one remaining cell. In the successor case, choosing c subtracts c from the remaining population and adds one coordinate. Conversely, the first coordinate of every admissible suffix lies in the enumerated interval, and its tail satisfies the recursive conditions. Different first coordinates belong to disjoint branches; induction gives no duplicates within a branch. This proves exhaustive, duplicate-free enumeration at every finite positive N and L.

For preserving words, sum(n_i)=N already implies n_i≤N, so the implementation cap adds no restriction. Its exact carrier is

    {(n_0,…,n_(L−1)) : n_i≥0 and Σ_i n_i=N}.

For alternating words the exact carrier adds n_i≤1. Summing these bounds gives N≤L. Consequently the complete alternating enumeration is empty when N>L. These statements are proved for the original walk, including the input-operation bindings, rather than inferred from a sample census.

The source raw weights and complete canonical measure are

    a_i=2^(L−i−1),
    s_d(n)=∏_i a_i^(d n_i),
    Z_d=Σ_(n in the complete occupation carrier) s_d(n),
    p_d(n)=s_d(n)/Z_d.

Here d is the positive cold-depth input of the original operation. The canonical mean throw uses the same entire distribution:

    T_d=Σ_n p_d(n) [Σ_i(i+1)n_i]/N.

The ground word is g=(N,0,…,0). The source searches successive positive depths for p_d(g)≥(m−1)/m, retaining every tested triple (d,p_d(g),T_d). Its finite search bound uses K, the number of preserving competitors: it finds the first positive b with 2^b≥max(1,K(m−1)), then tests depths 1 through b+1. 930. General occupation counts, normalization and the unique ground minimum

The preceding exhaustive walk permits an exact count for every finite positive population and level count. Let B(N,L) be its preserving count. Holding the first occupation c leaves N−c occupants and L−1 levels, so

    B(N,1)=1,
    B(N,L+1)=Σ_(c=0)^N B(N−c,L).

The existing factorial-quotient derivation supplies Pascal's identity

    C(a+b+2,a+1)=C(a+b+1,a)+C(a+b+1,a+1).

Induction on the population telescopes the complete branch sum; induction on the levels therefore gives

    B(N,L)=C(N+L−1,N).

For alternating occupation the first cell is either empty or holds one occupant. Its corresponding recurrence is

    F(N,L+1)=F(N,L)+F(N−1,L).

The empty-population continuation has one all-empty word; a positive population exceeding the number of cells has no word. These are boundary cases of the original recursive enumeration. Induction on the occupied and empty level counts, using the same Pascal identity, gives F(N,L)=C(L,N) for N≤L and F(N,L)=0 otherwise. originalEveryOccupationCensus connects both formulas to the native source census: its complete field is true for every positive N and L, including overfull alternating input.

For the canonical measure, every raw dyadic weight is positive. Each score

    s_d(n)=∏_i [2^(L−i−1)]^(d n_i)

is consequently a positive integer, and the sum Z_d over any nonempty generated support is positive. The implementation retains each original occupation word beside its normalized rational weight. Its complete rational sum is

    Σ_n p_d(n)=Σ_n s_d(n)/Z_d
              =(Σ_n s_d(n))/Z_d
              =Z_d/Z_d=1.

originalWeightAssembly proves this exact pairing and normalization for the native operation; originalEveryAdmittedMeasureNormalizes proves its resulting sum. The nonempty-support condition distinguishes the original empty alternating support when N>L; no positive measure is assigned to an absent word.

To derive the ground minimum, expose the starting level index in the source's indexed throw:

    M_a(n)=Σ_(i=0)^(L−1)(a+i)n_i,
    M_a(c::r)=a c+M_(a+1)(r),
    M_(a+1)(n)=Σ_i n_i+M_a(n).

The original totalThrow is M_1. Hence M_1(n)=N+M_0(n)≥N for every word with population N. If M_1(c::r)=N, the same recurrence gives

    M_1(c::r)=c+Σ r+M_1(r)=N+M_1(r).

Equality forces M_1(r)=0. Since M_1(r)≥Σ r, every nonnegative tail coordinate is zero. Thus c=N and the only possible minimum word is g=(N,0,…,0). The full preserving enumeration contains g, and direct evaluation gives M_1(g)=N. Every different generated word therefore has strictly greater total throw. This proves the ground minimum and its uniqueness for every positive population and level count; it does not rely on the finite certificate's sample range.

931. Exact cold-depth disadvantage of every excited occupation word

For every excited word e(n)≥1, and hence 2^(e(n))≥2. Each successive cold step therefore multiplies that word's relative score by at most one half. These are identities and inequalities for the actual generated occupation words and source score operation.

939. Depth-independent phase-count orthogonality

Let b(x,k) record whether the original held/returned coincidence count has odd parity. This Boolean records an orientation, not a signed amplitude. The native definition is b(x,k)=(#{i:x_i=returned and k_i=returned} mod 2 = 1). On adjoining one original binary label, the four cases are
b(held·x,held·k)=b(x,k),
b(held·x,returned·k)=b(x,k),
b(returned·x,held·k)=b(x,k),
b(returned·x,returned·k)=not b(x,k).
The last equality follows from exact count succession: the new coincidence count is the old count plus one, so its remainder modulo two switches between the two possible remainders. The proof reuses the existing exact remainder/quotient decomposition and removal of complete multiples. QuantumSupportParity.originalPhaseOperation proves that this orientation is exactly the value of the original walsh_phase operation on its equal-length, nonempty domain.

For two generated points x,y, let A_d(x,y) be the complete ordered list of Boolean agreements b(x,k)=b(y,k) over k in W(d). Let H(A) count true entries and R(A) count false entries. The two successor mode blocks are retained in the original held-first, returned-second order. If a,b are the newly adjoined point labels, then
A_(d+1)(a·x,b·y)=A_d(x,y) concatenated with T_(a,b)(A_d(x,y)),
where T is the identity when a=b and Boolean complementation when a differs from b. This equality is a theorem about the actual generated lists, not just their cardinalities.

Diagonal point pairs have agreement at every mode, so H(A_d(x,x))=2^d and R(A_d(x,x))=0. For distinct successor points there are two exhaustive cases. If their leading labels agree, their tails differ, and the inductive equality H=R is preserved by duplicating the old list. If their leading labels differ, the second mode block complements the first, giving H(new)=H(old)+R(old)=R(old)+H(old)=R(new), whether or not the tails agree. At the first binary depth this is the original diagonal pair and cancelling off-diagonal pair. Together with H(A)+R(A)=length(A)=2^d, the induction establishes every original diagonal and off-diagonal phase-count relation at every generated depth.

The generated-word length theorem establishes the native equal-length guard for every point and mode. QuantumSupportOrthogonalityNative.originalGeneratedProductRow then identifies each original inner product-row operation, including both native phase calls and their held/returned comparison, with the agreement label used in the induction. Thus the induction applies to the source table's actual rows. The 340 pair rows through the source's four census depths also agree exactly with the original Python output. This is supplementary output correspondence; the all-depth conclusion follows from the induction itself.

940. Parseval counting and the forced support-product bound

For a selected support S and mode k, retain the original positive count pair (h_k,r_k), where h_k counts held phase labels and r_k counts returned phase labels. Write m(h,r)=magnitude(imbalance(h,r)), using exactly the original empty-One result when h=r and the positive count difference otherwise. The mode energy is E_k(S)=m(h_k,r_k)^2. No signed amplitude is introduced.

The count recurrence has the exact identity
m(h+1,r)^2+2r=m(h,r)^2+2h+1.
To derive it, remove one held and one returned occurrence together: m(h+1,r+1)=m(h,r). The two empty-side cases reduce to m(h,0)=h and m(0,r)=r. At the remaining boundary, (n+1)^2=n^2+2n+1 supplies the successor identity. Interchanging h and r gives the returned-phase counterpart.

Adjoin a fresh generated point x to S. At each mode, let a_k count existing points whose phase agrees with x and let o_k count those whose phase differs. In either orientation the same successor relation is
E_k(S∪{x})+2o_k=E_k(S)+2a_k+1.
For every y in S, x differs from y. The all-depth off-diagonal theorem therefore gives equal agreement and disagreement counts over the complete mode carrier. Summing over the retained points preserves that equality: sum_k a_k=sum_k o_k. Summing the mode successor relation and cancelling these equal count terms yields
E(S∪{x})=E(S)+N, where E(S)=sum_k E_k(S) and N=2^d.
The empty accumulator has E(empty)=0. Induction over the original unique selected support gives the exact Parseval count
sum_k m(h_k,r_k)^2=N·|S|.
Uniqueness is precisely the original no-duplicate support requirement; membership is in the original complete binary carrier. The empty accumulator is the proof's list-induction base and does not change the source operation's nonempty input guard.

Let s_t=|S| and let s_f count the original occupied modes, namely those whose imbalance is not empty-One. Every mode retains h_k+r_k=s_t. Hence m(h_k,r_k)≤s_t and E_k(S)≤s_t². Unoccupied modes contribute zero to the host count sum. Keeping every occupied mode gives
N·s_t=E(S)≤s_f·s_t²=(s_t·s_f)·s_t.
For the source's nonempty support, s_t>0, so cancellation forces N≤s_t·s_f. This derives the source support-product inequality from its phase-count table and exact count recurrence.

The energy, frequency-support count and every held/returned mode-count pair agree with all 273 retained original nonempty supports through depth three. 941. Exact normalization, squared spread and spacing cancellation

The phase-count derivation establishes N≤s_t s_f for N=2^d and every original nonempty unique selected support. The complete generated carrier has N>0. Put P=s_t s_f. Dividing the support inequality by the positive N gives P/N≥1, the exact unit-free support product. The native rational comparison is proved false for P/N<1; this binds the mathematical inequality to the original Boolean test.

The source squares each normalized support separately and multiplies:
(s_t/N)^2(s_f/N)^2 = (s_t²s_f²)/N⁴ = P²/N⁴.
Since P≥N>0, multiplication gives P²≥N². Division by N⁴ gives
P²/N⁴ ≥ N²/N⁴ = 1/N².
The Lean equality retains the actual normalized rational multiplication, and the bound retains the actual rational less-than operation. Cross-multiplication uses positive denominators throughout. At the already established depth-two saturation N=4, P=4, the result is P²/N⁴=16/256=1/16.

Let a be any positive exact rational spacing accepted by the source. Its reduced numerator p and denominator q satisfy p>0 and q>0, with a=p/q. The original positional extent is s_t a. Its reciprocal-grid frequency extent is (s_f/N)/a. Therefore
(s_t a)((s_f/N)/a)
= (s_t p/q)((s_f/N)(q/p))
= (s_t p s_f q)/(q N p)
= s_t s_f/N.
The proof first establishes the identity for positive p,q and then derives that representation from every native rational satisfying the original positive-spacing guard. Thus it covers the complete accepted spacing domain, including the four original certificate spacings 1/8, 2/9, 3/7 and 5/11, without selecting a spacing to determine the result.

942. The support-uncertainty entry's complete grammar and executable record

947. General m-Fold fibres and interior fixed modes

Write the admitted image as y=p/q with positive whole p,q and p≤q. For a positive whole multiplicity m≥2, the original complete offset range is j=0,…,m−1. Its j-th preimage is
x_j=(y+j)/m=(p+jq)/(qm).
Multiplication returns the original image with its exact offset:
m x_j=(m(p+jq))/(qm)=(p+jq)/q=y+j.
The numerator is positive. Since j+1≤m and p≤q,
p+jq≤q+jq=(j+1)q≤mq,
so 0<x_j≤1. If x_i=x_j, cancellation of the common positive denominator gives p+iq=p+jq and then i=j. The complete range therefore yields exactly m distinct positive preimages, including the positive wrapped endpoint when y=1. The native division-and-addition operation is proved equal to this normalized fraction for every admitted multiplicity, image representation and offset. Its entire ordered enumeration is proved equal to the mapped complete offset list.

For interior fixed modes put m=k+2. The original indices are i=1,…,m−2, and
u_i=i/(m−1).
Their fixed-return equation is
m u_i=mi/(m−1)=i/(m−1)+i=u_i+i.
For each listed index, 0<i<m−1, hence 0<u_i<1. Distinct indices give distinct normalized fractions. The index list has exactly m−2 members; at m=2 it is the source's empty One form. The successor identity range(n+1)=range(n) concatenated with [n] proves the original index extension. The native fixed-mode division list is bound to this same complete index construction. Increasing multiplicity reconstructs the fractions using the successor denominator while adding the next index.

The original executable certificate also retains every m from 2 through 12 and all three images 1/m, 1/2 and 1 for each m. For each E²_i≥1 the source starts with consecutive whole-number bounds [k_i,k_i+1], where k_i²≤E²_i<(k_i+1)². At each refinement m_i=(l_i+u_i)/2. Given p_i^−=H₀l_i and p_i^+=H₀u_i, the distance bounds are
• H_i<p_i^−: d_i^−=p_i^−−H_i, d_i^+=p_i^+−H_i;
• H_i>p_i^+: d_i^−=H_i−p_i^+, d_i^+=H_i−p_i^−;
• otherwise: d_i^−=0, d_i^+=max(H_i−p_i^−,p_i^+−H_i).
The exact variance unit is V_i=σ_i²+E²_iσ₀². Each row contributes once:

992. Molecular electron census and held-spin decomposition

For the retained nuclear populations, let Zᵢ be the positive atomic number and nᵢ the positive occurrence count. The neutral census is N₀=Σᵢ Zᵢnᵢ. The original charge carrier separates direction from magnitude: structural empty-One retains N=N₀; an adjoin action with positive count t gives N=N₀+t; a remove action gives N=N₀−t with the original guard t<N₀. Empty nuclear support and a removal erasing or exceeding the positive support are rejected. Nuclear element symbols, molecular carrier, electron occurrences and spin fibres remain held labels with their original families.

At a declared positive spin width w, the source construction sets d=w−1. Compatibility is exactly d≤N and (N−d) mod 2=0. It then defines P=(N−d)/2. The existing constructive quotient/remainder identity gives (N−d) mod 2+2⌊(N−d)/2⌋=N−d. Substituting the accepted zero remainder and adding d yields 2P+d=N. If another count Q has 2Q+d=N, subtracting the same retained d from both equalities gives 2P=2Q; cancellation of the positive factor two yields P=Q. Thus the pair count is unique at that declared width. The width identity is w=d+1, with (d+1)−1=d.

Reducing the decomposition modulo two gives N mod 2=d mod 2, and (N+1) mod 2=(d+1) mod 2=w mod 2. The source parity operation therefore returns odd-positive-width for even electron support and even-positive-width for odd support. This is the original parity consequence; no measured ground-state term is inserted into the census or candidate selection.

The generated organization enumerates electron-1 through electron-N, followed by the prescribed cell construction: pair-1 through pair-P contain the ordered complementary fibres (fibre-a,fibre-b), and held-1 through held-d each contain fibre-a. The organization checks the complete occurrence count, occurrence uniqueness and family, total occupied support, pair-plus-held decomposition, width, and the actual ordered complementary-pair/single-cell counts. It does not add a cell-identifier uniqueness guard absent from the source.

The two successor equations are 2(P+1)+d=(2P+d)+2 and 2P+(d+1)=(2P+d)+1. Adding a complementary pair preserves d and hence width; adding one unmatched fibre increases both support and width by one. 1013. Quasicrystal substitution: retained recurrence and rational-scale exclusion

The source substitution A→AB, B→A starts with positive population pair (a₁,b₁)=(1,1). Counting the two substitutions gives aₙ₊₁=aₙ+bₙ and bₙ₊₁=aₙ. Appending the next pair preserves the complete previous history, so a positive requested depth d contains exactly d pairs. The first six source pairs are (1,1),(2,1),(3,2),(5,3),(8,5),(13,8). The native successorEquation, historyCount and originalDepthCount establish the recurrence and history length for every admitted depth; originalSixSuccessors evaluates the declared witness.

Suppose a positive reduced rational fixed scale is p/q with gcd(p,q)=1. The source recurrence requires p²=pq+q². Consequently q divides p². Any prime divisor of q would then divide p and q, contradicting coprimality; hence q=1. Also p divides p² and pq, so p divides their difference q². With q=1, positivity forces p=1. Substitution then requires 1=1+1, which is false. Thus no positive reduced rational fixed scale satisfies the recurrence. The existing native theorem rationalFixedScaleExcluded proves this argument for arbitrary positive p and q, without evaluating an irrational limit.

The native six-field rational-inflation certificate retains the original recurrence, fixed-scale equation, divisibility statement, least positive candidate, its rejection and the held structural-absence label. Its operational witness evaluates the original six-pair history and least-candidate rejection. 1041. Molecular exchange source reconstruction and exact measured separation

The source energy inscription is parsed as an exact decimal rational. If the integral digits represent I and the fractional digits after removing underscore separators represent F with length k, the unreduced value is N/Q=(I·10^k+F)/10^k. With g=gcd(N,Q), its exact Fraction representation is (N/g)/(Q/g). The original lexical guard accepts the stated opening brackets, whitespace and optional approximation marker, and rejects inscriptions containing eV. These are source-record parsing operations, not fitted energy values.

For a singlet energy E_s=a/b and triplet energy E_t=c/d, the measured separation is

    Δ = |E_s−E_t| = |ad−cb|/(bd).

Writing h=gcd(|ad−cb|,bd), the retained positive separation has numerator |ad−cb|/h and denominator bd/h; zero separation is rejected by the original guard. The held order is singlet-below-triplet when ad<cb and triplet-below-singlet otherwise. All 14 source pairs are retained: 13 have triplet-below-singlet and one has singlet-below-triplet. The exchange law preserves this measured ordering boundary. The PositiveRatio constructor retains the supplied positive numerator and denominator exactly; reduction here comes from the source Fraction computation, not an additional constructor rule.

1062. Multicentre delocalized support: retained graph and topology

A volume satisfies |V|≥4, |E|>|V| and at least one d(v)≥3. Every changing scan increases its cardinality, so the finite registered centre count bounds these changes; it is not a fitted cutoff. 1069. Multicentre edge-scan preservation and the connected attachment step

Let C be the retained list of molecular centres, E the ordered list of support edges, and S_E(R) the source edge scan starting from reached centres R. Each incident edge inserts its endpoints only when absent. Therefore there is a suffix T such that
  S_E(R) = R ++ T,     |S_E(R)| = |R| + |T| >= |R|.
The source stopping condition is not merely a comparison of unrelated counts. If |S_E(R)| <= |R|, the displayed identity forces |T| = 0, hence T = [] and S_E(R) = R. Every remaining recursive scan then retains R unchanged.
If both endpoints of every edge in E occur in C, processing each edge inserts neither endpoint, so induction over E gives
  S_E(C) = C.
For a retained anchor a in C and a fresh centre f not in C, concatenation of scans and the insertion guards give the original attachment step:
  S_(E ++ [(a,f)])(C)
    = S_[(a,f)](S_E(C))
    = S_[(a,f)](C)
    = addReached(addReached(C,a),f)
    = C ++ [f].
Thus the scan retains the existing complete reached list and adds the connected centre without a separate interaction rule. These equations concern the actual source edge-scan and endpoint-custody operations. The existing retained-word derivation supplies the corresponding complete support-word and non-pair statements.

1071. Multicentre finite traversal and complete-word successor

The reached-set bound follows from the registered molecular-centre domain, rather than from a chosen iteration limit. Let C be the registered centre list, E its endpoint-custodied edges, R_0=[c_0], and S_E the original ordered edge scan. Identity comparison uses exactly the retained family and label byte lists. Insertion tests this same identity before appending. Induction over edges therefore preserves both invariants
  keys(R_i) are distinct,       keys(R_i) subseteq keys(C).
Finite deletion of a held key proves the cardinal inequality
  |R_i| <= |C|.
If a scan changes R_i, its retained-prefix property gives |S_E(R_i)| >= |R_i|+1. Starting with one retained centre, strict growth cannot continue through |C| scans. The implemented centre-count recursion therefore reaches a fixed point. More explicitly, for any intermediate reached list R and remaining scan count n satisfying |C| < |R|+n, a growing scan preserves that inequality for n-1; the zero-count branch contradicts the cardinal bound. A non-growing scan leaves R unchanged. The inductive OriginalScanRun trace records precisely these growing and stopping branches of V3's while-loop. registeredInitialScanRunsOriginal and acceptedInitialScanRunsOriginal bind the trace to the actual initial singleton and accepted constructor guards.
The source count test also establishes coverage, not merely matching cardinalities. If a registered key k were absent from a duplicate-free reached list R with |R|=|C|, R would fit inside C with k removed. That removal strictly reduces the available cardinality, contradicting |R|=|C|. Thus every registered centre is reached.
For the connected successor, let a be retained in C and f a fresh centre. Set
  C' = C ++ [f],       E' = E ++ [(a,f)].
Let Q be the terminal reached list for C', E'. Its fixed-point property closes every incident edge, and its retained prefix contains c_0. The complete old traversal therefore remains inside Q. The old coverage result puts a in Q, and the new edge puts f in Q. Freshness makes R ++ [f] duplicate-free, so
  |C|+1 = |R ++ [f]| <= |Q| <= |C'| = |C|+1.
Consequently |Q|=|C'| and connected(C',E')=true. Additional endpoint-custodied edges preserve this result: the enlarged terminal closed set contains the old traversal, while the same registered-centre upper bound applies. This proves the source's at-least-one-edge extension, including further retained incidences.
The electron support word extends in the same order. Structural induction on the original byte-equal words gives
  sameWord(W,C)=true  implies  sameWord(W ++ [f],C ++ [f])=true.
acceptedConnectedWordSuccessor combines these two conclusions directly from an accepted DelocalizedMolecularSupport translation. The original path, cycle and branched-volume incidence guards, all five operational witnesses, all 256 candidate decisions, all 20 IUPAC/NIST comparison rows and all 15 adverse controls remain bound to this same entry.

1074. Molecular state transitions: retained endpoints, structural absence and composition

A transition retains the ordered record T=(M,I,E,o,R): molecular carrier M, initial state I, terminal state or structural absence E, orientation o and observation record R. The four observed orientations are forward,reverse,bidirectional and coupled; the fifth is structurally absent. The constructor checks the carrier,initial-state and record families before the orientation and endpoint requirements. An accepted observed record satisfies E=state(J), I≠J and o∈{forward,reverse,bidirectional,coupled}. An accepted absent record has E=EMPTY_ONE, the original singleton structural absence. A separate object with the same absence inscription does not satisfy the singleton-identity guard. 1092. Molecular configuration order: complete neighbours and retained paths

\[

\]

\[
 B(L,C,R)=(cb<ad)\land(cf<ed).
\]
The positive-height barrier decision reverses the comparisons:
\[
 T(L,C,R)=(ad<cb)\land(ed<cf).
\]

A positive centre with an EmptyOne neighbour is not a basin. The source's singleton identity tests and its accepted EmptyOne objects are preserved separately in the translation.

so every earlier comparison and its complete node records remain, and exactly one new complete-neighbour comparison becomes available. For every transformed branch, observation uses the shared singleton-word decoder and retains the whole predecessor record ((wordᵢ,phaseᵢ,labelᵢ))ᵢ₌₁ⁿ. Existing observation proofs establish |record|=|branches|, retaining phase labels rather than identifying the quantum and classical traces. The source certificate checks decoded-map equality, inverse restoration and completeness of every record. 1128.1. From the accepted chemical table to complete reversible execution

Let R=((s₁,t₁),…,(sₙ,tₙ)) be the table accepted by MolecularProcess. Its constructor supplies n>0, pairwise distinct sᵢ and pairwise distinct tᵢ, together with the original carrier and law families. Write ι(s)=[s] for the singleton-word encoding. The identity ι(a)=ι(b)⇒a=b transfers distinctness from the original columns to the generated words. Hence

  S₀=((ι(sᵢ),phase-held))ᵢ₌₁ⁿ,
  G=((ι(sᵢ),ι(tᵢ)))ᵢ₌₁ⁿ,
  P=(phase-held,phase-returned),   Δ=(phase-successor)

satisfy the original state and gate guards. Every initial phase belongs to P, |P|=2, Δ is nonempty, and the two generated gate columns remain distinct. The domain identity follows directly, with its row order retained:

  sources(G)=map(ι,sources(R))=support(S₀).

These are constructor consequences, not additional assumptions supplied to the molecular operation. Applying the existing reversible-application theorem to these generated objects yields S₁=applyGate(S₀,G), an admitted S₁ with |S₁.branches|=n, and

  applyGate(S₁,inverse(G),inverse_phase=true)=S₀.

Every image word is ι(tᵢ): a successful transformed branch has an actual gate lookup, that lookup retains an original table row, and the target of that generated row is exactly [tᵢ]. Thus the shared observation map O=((ι(tᵢ),tᵢ))ᵢ₌₁ⁿ classifies precisely support(S₁), with no extra or missing word. For each branch bᵢ=(ι(tᵢ),phaseᵢ), lookup(O,ι(tᵢ))=tᵢ. The complete record contains (bᵢ,tᵢ), so the selected class for that observation is nonempty and the observation operation succeeds. Its retained complete predecessor record Cᵢ has |Cᵢ|=n. Executing that operation once per transformed branch yields n records, each of length n; the source resource ledger counts the n observation records, while each record retains all n predecessor rows.

The list construction exposes both induction steps. The empty traversal returns an empty list of records. For a head branch followed by a retained tail, the original observation succeeds at the head, the tail traversal succeeds by induction, and the result prepends the head's complete record. Therefore |records|=|S₁.branches|=n, while every record has n rows. In parallel, decode(gateRows([]))=[] and decode(gateRows(r::R))=r::decode(gateRows(R)), so the decoded quantum table is exactly R and equals the classical row projection. 1138. Held dihedral coordinates and cyclic torsional states

With predecessor and successor indices interpreted cyclically, the conformer condition is hᵢ<hᵢ₋₁ and hᵢ<hᵢ₊₁; the barrier condition is hᵢ₋₁<hᵢ and hᵢ₊₁<hᵢ. Both inequalities are strict, so a plateau does not become a strict extremum. EmptyOne is structural absence in this comparison. Starting from each barrier, scan each orientation independently and stop at the first conformer minimum, examining at most n successors. This retains both adjacent paths even when their conformer endpoint coincides.

1147. Molecular formation energy: named reference composition and held state order

A formation record retains a completely identified product state P and a nonempty finite tuple of positive constituent reference states r_1,...,r_m.   R_1 = r_1; R_(j+1) = R_j + r_(j+1); R = R_m.
For positive rational states n/d and a/b, each composition is the exact reduced fraction (n b + a d)/(d b). The reference is therefore constructed from the entire named tuple.

The product and reference force one of three relations. If P=R, the orientation is product-reference-equal and the magnitude is structural EmptyOne. If P>R, the orientation is product-above-reference and the positive separation is Delta=P-R. If P<R, the orientation is product-below-reference and Delta=R-P. To express the same derivation using a common positive denominator D, write P=N/D and R=M/D. Equality is N=M; otherwise the numerator is N-M when N>M, or M-N when M>N. These are positive differences in the selected order, not signed proof values. Reassembly is explicit:
  (N-M)+M=N when M<N;
  (M-N)+N=M when N<M.
The native branches equalStates, productAbove and productBelow follow these exact comparisons. aboveSeparationReassembles and belowSeparationReassembles reuse the existing retained-part reassembly theorem.

For a shared positive state X=Q/D, the two numerators become N+Q and M+Q. Their ordering is unchanged, and their separation satisfies
  (N+Q)-(M+Q)=N-M when M<N,
  (M+Q)-(N+Q)=M-N when N<M.
Equality remains equality. For a positive repetition k, the numerators become kN and kM; the orientation is retained and the positive separation becomes k Delta, since kN-kM=k(N-M) in the above branch and kM-kN=k(M-N) in the below branch. The common denominator is constructed from the supplied denominators; it introduces no scientific choice or fitted parameter.

1148. One carrier and its complete cross-property projection vector

V3 retains one structural molecular carrier C=(identity, constitution, state, charge, geometry/symmetry, condition, F), where F is the nonempty set of applicable held property families. A projection is the complete record p=(f,g,o,v): its property family f, admitted generating relation g, held result orientation o and exact positive result or structural EmptyOne v. The vector V=(p_1,...,p_n) is admissible precisely when each family occurs once and its family support is exactly F:
  f_i != f_j for i != j; {f_1,...,f_n}=F.
The source composition returns that original ordered tuple. It does not sort the results, substitute values or fit a separate carrier for each property.

Named projection is selection from the original tuple:
  M_f(V) = [p in V such that p.family=f].
When M_f(V)=[p], the projection is p itself, preserving all four fields. Empty or nonunique matches produce the original rejection. For an extension e with family h absent from the existing vector, the enlarged carrier has family support F union {h}, and the vector is V'=V ++ [e]. For every prior family f, h != f gives
  M_f(V ++ [e]) = M_f(V) ++ M_f([e])
                    = M_f(V) ++ [] = M_f(V).
Thus selecting any prior named projection returns the identical record, including generating relation, orientation and exact result. The recursive native matchingAppendFresh follows this equation by induction on V; projectionAppendFresh connects it to the actual source selection operation, and namedResultPreserved retains the selected original record. The source operations and the append-selection theorems compile with empty axiom dependencies. The three composition-to-extension declarations compile with empty axiom dependencies. Applying the same argument to the accepted extended tuple V ++ [e] yields M_(f_i)(V ++ [e])=[p_i] for every earlier p_i. 1149. Finite chemical microstate support, multiplicity and exact weight

A chemical microstate retains five held identities: state, composition, phase, observation condition and internal state. Equality compares all five fields. A finite support S=(s_1,...,s_N) is nonempty and contains no duplicated state. Each macro-observation fibre F_j is a nonempty tuple of distinct states with one held macrostate identity. The support constructor requires distinct macrostate identities and tests the flattened tuple F_1 ++ ... ++ F_k: it contains no duplicate state and its set is exactly the support set. Therefore every generated state belongs to exactly one retained fibre:
  S = disjoint union_(j=1)^k F_j; N = sum_(j=1)^k m_j; m_j = |F_j| > 0.
The count m_j is the source's finite multiplicity. Its statistical weight is the exact positive ratio
  w_j = m_j / N.
The ratio constructor reduces the two supplied finite counts by their common divisor. No distribution prior, fitted degeneracy or temperature value selects either count. Named selection must identify exactly one fibre; absent or nonunique identities are rejected.

The finite successor supplies one new microstate s and one new macrostate identity h. The source first rejects s already in S and h already among the fibre identities. It then constructs the singleton fibre (h,(s)) and the enlarged support through the same partition constructor:
  S' = S ++ [s]; P' = P ++ [(h,[s])].
The source preservation check takes both prefixes of length one less than the enlarged tuples, verifies they are S and P, and verifies the final state and singleton fibre. Earlier state-to-fibre assignments remain unchanged; the new state has its own new named fibre.   r_i=(R_i,C_i,T_i,k_i,c_i,t_i,U_i),

Condition ordinals may repeat and different reactions remain separate.

Let pi sort the accepted rows by increasing target ordinal. The source construction returns the fixed temperature-dependence carrier together with
  Q(L)=((R_pi(i),T_pi(i),k_pi(i),C_pi(i),c_pi(i),t_pi(i)))_(i=1,...,n).

  carrier(Q(L+r))=carrier(Q(L)) and take_n(Q(L+r))=Q(L).

1187. Activation barriers from complete ordered paths

A generated path retains species and path identities, an ordered word of state identities and relative supports, a positive source-target ordinal, and source-reference, uncertainty and method provenance. Write
  P=(S,P_id,((q_1,h_1),...,(q_m,h_m)),t,reference,uncertainty,method).
Each h_i is a positive exact ratio or structural EmptyOne. V3's constructors require the registered-species, generated-reaction-path and generated-path-state label families; m>0; distinct state identities; at least one positive support; a positive target ordinal; and held-label or EmptyOne provenance. EmptyOne is retained as absent displacement rather than introduced as a freely chosen absolute energy origin.

From the positive states, forced_activation_barrier selects the boundary with greatest exact support. For h=a/b and h'=c/d with positive denominators, the decision is
  h<h' iff a*d<c*b.
Starting at the first positive state, each subsequent positive state replaces the current boundary only when this strict comparison holds. Equal fractions therefore retain the earlier state, including when their numerator/denominator representations differ. The returned result retains the actual boundary state, its original positive ratio and the path identity, under the held orientation least-state-to-highest-path-boundary:
  B(P)=(P_id,q_j,h_j,orientation),
  j=the first positive-state index attaining max {h_i : h_i is positive}.
All nonboundary states remain in the input path and empirical record. The barrier value is selected by exact order on that path; it is not a fitted number substituted for the path.

For a nonempty collection with distinct positive target ordinals, the source numerically sorts by those ordinals and returns
  C(P_1,...,P_n)=((S_pi(i),P_id,pi(i),h_j(pi(i)),q_j(pi(i)),t_pi(i)))_(i=1,...,n).
The collection's held carrier is complete-source-ordered-path-census. Its append operation compares the carrier and the entire old prefix of the new collection, using the original labels, ratio representation and ordinal. An earlier-ordinal insertion can return false, and a duplicate ordinal rejects, matching the original operation.

The operational witnesses give max(2,5,3)=5 on a path with a retained least-state EmptyOne; convert the inscription 0.00 to EmptyOne; preserve source target order (1,2) even when the barriers are (5,3); and retain the complete earlier collection on the original successor append. The original eight grammar axes are path, source, boundary, reference, minimality, identity, record and prediction. Their literal binary product contains 2^8=256 alternatives. The registered decisions require the preserving choice on every axis. The false-premise control replaces the preserving choice on the first axis, path, with its original rejected choice.

1191. Complete competing-channel support and exact branching

Competing channels retain the whole product record. For a reaction R and held condition C, V3's ProductChannelSupport holds a product identity p_i, its original positive rational support s_i or structural EmptyOne, and positive source ordinal i. CompleteChannelRecord requires at least two channels, distinct product identities, consecutive ordinals 1,...,n, and at least one positive support. The reaction, condition, product and source identities are carried into the result. These constructor conditions are exactly the original accepted domain.

Let I be the indices whose retained supports are positive ratios. The operation forms the exact sum S = sum_{i in I} s_i. Since I is nonempty and every included support is positive, S > 0. It then returns q_i = s_i/S for i in I and structural EmptyOne for each absent-support row. Thus sum_{i in I} q_i = (sum_{i in I} s_i)/S = S/S = 1. The implementation performs the original exact sum-to-One guard after constructing the shares. It returns R, C, S, the full ordered product/ordinal/raw-support/share rows, and the original complete-channel-whole identity. The retained raw fractions preserve the source's stored numerator and denominator; arithmetic totals and shares use reduced exact fractions.

The first original witness uses (s_1,s_2)=(2,3), giving S=5 and shares (2/5,3/5). Their sum is One. The absent-channel witness uses (2,EmptyOne,3), retaining the middle identity, ordinal and absent support rather than deleting its row. A successor must have ordinal n+1. Its addition preserves all previous product identities and raw supports while recomputing the new total S' and shares s_i/S'. The original append predicate compares the preceding identities and raw supports; it does not require the old normalized shares to remain unchanged after the total changes.

The source constructs eight binary grammar axes: support, whole, relation, identity, absence, record, provenance and prediction. Their Cartesian product contains 2^8 = 256 alternatives. 1193. Sequential composition retains every state and elementary boundary

V3 represents each retained state occurrence by its registered state identity, positive occurrence number, held state condition and held observation status. Each elementary transition carries its own registered identity and positive occurrence number, the distinct registered entry and exit state identities, a held transition condition and held transition status. A complete mechanism consists of a registered reaction, a state word (s_1,...,s_n) with n >= 2, and an edge word (e_1,...,e_{n-1}). Occurrence numbers must be exactly 1,...,n and 1,...,n-1. Every edge satisfies entry(e_i)=identity(s_i) and exit(e_i)=identity(s_{i+1}). These equalities are checked on each adjacent pair, with every condition and status retained. Identity labels may recur at different occurrences; the original construction does not impose global uniqueness on them.

The forced composition returns nine fields: reaction, initial state s_1, terminal state s_n, the full state word, the full edge word, the intermediate word (s_2,...,s_{n-1}), positive transition count n-1, intermediate count n-2 when positive or structural EmptyOne otherwise, and the exact-sequential-composition identity. For n=2 the intermediate word is empty and its count is EmptyOne. For the original three-state witness, n=3 gives two transitions and one retained intermediate. The shared-boundary equality exit(e_1)=entry(e_2) follows from their common retained state s_2, which both edges explicitly name.

An appended state has occurrence n+1 and an appended transition occurrence n. Its entry must equal the former terminal identity and its exit must equal the new state identity. The resulting words are S'=S concatenated with [s_{n+1}] and E'=E concatenated with [e_n]. Taking their first n and n-1 entries recovers S and E exactly, including identities, occurrences, conditions and statuses. The new intermediate word is (s_2,...,s_n); taking its first n-2 entries recovers every former intermediate. The source's append predicate checks all three complete prefixes. No differential equation, decay curve or lifetime fit is part of this operation.

The source's eight binary axes are support, adjacency, intermediate, composition, condition, status, provenance and prediction. Their product has 2^8=256 alternatives. 1197. Reversible kinetics and equilibrium support from one closed pair graph

  entry(e₊)=a, exit(e₊)=b, entry(e₋)=b, exit(e₋)=a.

  C(F)=(C(G₁),…,C(Gₙ)),
  C(F∥Gₙ₊₁)=C(F)∥C(Gₙ₊₁).
Consequently taking its first n elements recovers C(F), and its length increases by one. The original append operation constructs the extended family through the same guards before checking these identities. It does not merge repeated observations or remove held status information.

1200. Catalytic turnover from exact return of the held catalyst

Let \(C\) contain \(n\ge2\) distinct registered states \(s_1,\ldots,s_n\) and exactly \(n\) retained directed transitions \(e_1,\ldots,e_n\). The original guards require consecutive positive state positions, one identical held catalyst κ throughout the states, and one identical held condition boundary c throughout the transitions. Define \(s_{n+1}=s_1\). Every edge must satisfy
\[
\operatorname{entry}(e_i)=s_i,\qquad\operatorname{exit}(e_i)=s_{i+1},\qquad1\le i\le n.
\]
Thus the last edge closes at the exact entry state. Each transition also retains its identity, process identity and evidence status; each state retains its observation status. The turnover construction preserves the whole directed word (e₁,…,eₙ), κ and the cycle identity, returns the exact state s₁, and assigns one completed cycle. These six fields are the original ExactCatalyticTurnover result. A product total or an open endpoint path is not substituted for the closed word.

\[
\nu=\frac{N}{T}.
\]
Fraction reduction preserves the relation: 6/4=3/2, and the original operational witness evaluates 3/2. The independent source analysis evaluates the exact count relation 7/5. Neither construction uses a fitted continuum rate or a steady-state assumption.

For a nonempty source-ordered family of n complete occurrences with interval parts t₁,…,tₙ>0, the registered family frequency is
\[
\nu_n=\frac{n}{\sum_{i=1}^{n}t_i},\qquad
\nu_{n+1}=\frac{n+1}{\sum_{i=1}^{n}t_i+t_{n+1}}.
\]
Appending the next complete occurrence preserves the original ordered prefix. If \(\tau(C_i)\) denotes the complete turnover returned for occurrence \(i\), then
\[
[\tau(C_1),\ldots,\tau(C_n),\tau(C_{n+1})]_{1:n}=[\tau(C_1),\ldots,\tau(C_n)],

\] The source's successor assertion preserves the first n complete turnover results and increases the completed-cycle count by one; it does not assert that the frequency stays unchanged. Source positions must be 1,…,n+1. Repeated cycle identities across different family occurrences are retained: the original family constructor does not impose a uniqueness condition on them.

1204. Ordered kinetic isotope-effect relation

Take two distinct held isotope identities H and D on the same retained reaction identity, complete ordered path P=(p₁,…,pₘ), m≥2, and held condition C.     k_H=N_H/T_H,     k_D=N_D/T_D,
    N_H,T_H,N_D,T_D ∈ positive exact counts.

The rate constructor checks both positivity and equality to its complete count relation. The ordered pair then determines

    K=k_H/k_D=(N_H/T_H)/(N_D/T_D)
     =(N_H T_D)/(T_H N_D).

Both products are positive, so K is an exact positive fraction. The orientation is the held label numerator-rate-greater when K>1, denominator-rate-greater when K<1, and rates-exactly-equal when K=1. Thus counts (3,5) and (2,5) give K=3/2; reversing the count rates gives 2/3; equal rates give 1. No numerical isotope mass or mass-frequency equation enters this operation. The six returned fields retain the ordered pair identity, both isotope identities, the complete reaction path, the exact quotient and its orientation.

1206. Joint product states and reaction-scattering shares

    m≥2,    |C|=|P|,    cᵢ≠cⱼ for i≠j.

    W(s)=(outgoing channel, ordered carriers, ordered states, orientation).

    T=Σᵢ₌₁ⁿNᵢ,    T>0,

1208. Exhaustive mechanism paths and retained proof traces

A mechanism search receives a held initial state s, a held terminal state t and the complete ordered list E of registered transitions. A transition records a source state, destination state and its law/trace label. The original operation carries three items at every search position: the current state x, the accumulated label trace τ and the visited-state word V. Initially these are

    (x,τ,V)=(s,(),(s)).

A terminal position x=t contributes its complete trace τ immediately and is not expanded further. Otherwise a registered edge e=(a,b,ℓ) extends the position exactly when

    a=x and b∉V.

Its successor is

    (b, τ++(ℓ), V++(b)).

The visited-state condition excludes repeated states, including a self-loop at the current state and any return to the initial state. It does not discard a distinct parallel transition merely because another transition has the same label. All eligible transitions contribute their continuations. In particular, two registered edge occurrences carrying the same complete label trace produce two retained copies of that trace. The final operation sorts the complete trace list lexicographically; it does not replace it with a set.

For the transition list

    (1,2,"first"), (2,3,"second"), (1,3,"direct"), (2,1,"cycle"),

the search from 1 to 3 produces

    (("direct"),("first","second")).

The edge from 2 back to 1 fails the visited-state condition. Searching from 1 to 1 instead produces the single empty trace (()), because the initial state is already terminal. A search with no route produces the empty trace list (). These two outputs therefore remain distinct.

Termination follows from the original finite transition support and simple-path condition. If an edge occurrence were used twice in one path, its destination state would be revisited, contradicting the admission condition. Consequently a path uses at most |E| edge occurrences. The translation derives its recursion index from |E|; it introduces no externally chosen search cutoff. It visits successors in the reverse transition order corresponding to the original last-in-first-out stack, then applies the original lexicographic ordering. Existing molecular-graph word ordering is reused.

The eight binary grammar axes retain held states, admitted transitions, complete simple-path enumeration, stepwise carrier custody, all parallel routes, the declared cycle/resource boundary, kernel stepwise acceptance and the complete premise/alternative/step/terminal trace. Their literal product contains 2⁸=256 alternatives. The operation consumes the registered transition list; the separate sequential and parallel mechanism entries retain the source-specific transition and carrier conditions on that list.

1217. Electrochemical work and retained reaction direction

The constructor retains the original label families and accepts d in {forward, reverse, equilibrium}. In the directed cases p is an exact positive ratio a/b, with a,b positive counts; equilibrium instead requires equality with EmptyOne. The carrier count remains positive in every case.

For a directed account the derivation composes each carrier with the retained separation:
    p = a/b,    n p = (n a)/b.
Writing g = gcd(n a,b), the normalized stored result is
    W = ((n a)/g)/(b/g).
Both resulting counts are positive. For equilibrium the result is EmptyOne, preserving the source's structural coincidence representation. The six-field result is (d,W,P_c,P_e,n,H): the two paths, reaction direction, transferred carriers and condition are retained together with the work magnitude.

Reversal exchanges forward and reverse, leaves equilibrium fixed, and appends “-reverse” separately to each path label. Cell, condition, carrier count and potential separation are retained. Consequently the same product n p supplies both directed work magnitudes. Applying reversal twice restores the orientation and appends “-reverse-reverse” to each path; it does not erase the recorded path history. The original witness account has n=2 and p=3/2, giving W=3. The other source witnesses preserve chemical and electrical custody, forward direction, positive directed magnitude, EmptyOne equilibrium, reversal magnitude and rejection of a directed EmptyOne account.

1218. Electrochemical-work grammar, source reconstruction and sealed comparison

Thus, for p=a/b, the common-denominator composition gives W(n+1)=(na+a)/b=((n+1)a)/b, agreeing with the positive carrier–potential product in Section 1217. Equilibrium uses the separately retained EmptyOne branch; it is not selected by a measured work or voltage value.

The registered grammar has eight binary axes, in order: custody, carrier, potential, composition, direction, equilibrium, record and reversal. 1219. Electrolysis product amount and complete carrier custody

An electrolysis account retains process, electrode path, product and condition identities together with positive transferred-carrier count n and positive demand d per product. V3 computes the quotient q and remainder r by exact division:
    n = q d + r,    0 <= r < d.
The complete-product field contains the positive count q when q>0 and EmptyOne otherwise. The retained-carrier-remainder field similarly contains r when r>0 and EmptyOne otherwise. The exact-product-amount field preserves the original positive ratio record (n,d), including its unreduced stored counts. Thus n=4,d=2 retains the ratio record (4,2), two complete products and an EmptyOne remainder; n=5,d=2 retains (5,2), two complete products and one remaining carrier. For n=1,d=2, the complete-product field is EmptyOne while the carrier remainder and exact ratio remain present. The five-field result also retains product identity and electrode path.

Two batches compose only when process, electrode path, product, condition and demand d agree. Their transferred counts add:
    n_total = n_1 + n_2,
    amount_total = (n_1+n_2)/d = n_1/d + n_2/d.
Exact division is then applied to the combined count, preserving complete products and remaining carriers without rounding. Starting with one carrier and appending positive like batches therefore retains the same product rule. The eight original witnesses establish the five-halves example, complete products, retained remainder, insufficient-product EmptyOne, exact-division EmptyOne remainder, product identity, like-batch addition and rejection of unlike stoichiometric demands.

1220. Species-resolved ionic conductivity

Each observed ionic species retains its identity, transport direction, electrolyte composition, condition and finite path, together with positive carried-distinction count n_i and positive path-resource count r_i. Its exact response is k_i=n_i/r_i. A conductivity account is nonempty; every contribution shares composition, condition and path, and every species occurs exactly once. The result retains the entire ordered contribution vector and those common identities with
    K = sum_{i=1}^{m} n_i/r_i.
For two fractions, exact composition uses
    a/b + c/d = (ad+bc)/(bd),
followed by positive rational normalization. Iterating this operation over the complete vector produces the original total. Appending a distinct positive contribution gives
    K_new = K + n_new/r_new,
    K_new - K = n_new/r_new > 0.
No prior contribution is refitted or discarded. The original witness uses 3/2+1/2=2; it also retains both species and the common composition and condition, establishes positive extension, and rejects mixed conditions and the empty vector.

1221. Ionic mobility and the complete transference partition

For species i, let t_i, n_i and r_i be its positive traversal, carrier and path-resource counts. Its held direction remains separate from these magnitudes. The original account computes
    mu_i = t_i/(n_i r_i),
    c_i = mu_i n_i = t_i/r_i.
The accounts share composition, condition and path, retain distinct species, and form a nonempty vector. Their complete contribution total is C=sum_i c_i. Each row retains species, direction, mobility and exact transference part
    theta_i = c_i/C.
Positivity gives theta_i>0, and inclusion of c_i in C gives theta_i<=1. The result computes the sum of these parts:
    sum_i theta_i = (sum_i c_i)/C = C/C = One.
The implementation assembles the actual parts and their sum. It does not substitute One for the calculation. With traversals 3 and 1, one carrier each and resource 2, the contributions are 3/2 and 1/2, total 2, and parts 3/4 and 1/4. An absent species is represented separately by EmptyOne. Duplicate-species accounts are rejected; distinct held directions remain attached to their respective rows.

The eight binary axes retain identity, direction, mobility, composition, partition, whole, absence and record. Their 256 alternatives preserve the complete source grammar and its unique accepted combination.   f = r: balanced, EmptyOne;

1227. Observation records and the generated Fold fibres

The Consciousness foundation uses the same exact positive rational part domain and Fold operation already derived at the root. For 0 < x ≤ 1,

  F(x) = 2x if 2x ≤ 1, and F(x) = 2x − 1 otherwise.

Solving the two branches for a given image y gives the complete preimage pair

  F⁻¹(y) = {y/2, (y+1)/2}.

The first lies in (0,1/2] and the second in (1/2,1]; both fold to y. Conversely, the branch selected by any admitted x gives one of these two values. This is the existing general exactTwoPreimages equivalence, not an inference from the examples below.

An observation stores (source,image,held_fibre). Its image is F(source). When retention is requested, the source comparison chooses the lower label if source = y/2 and otherwise the upper label if source = (y+1)/2. Exhaustion of the two fibres ensures that every admitted source receives a label. Reconstruction selects the corresponding predecessor, so the reconstructed source equals the original. Without a retained label the original reversible_from_record operation returns false. For directly supplied observation records, the original operation interprets any held label other than lower as upper; the translation preserves this decision.

At y = 1/2 the two coordinates are 1/4 and 3/4. Thus

  F(1/4) = F(3/4) = 1/2,
  1/4 + 3/4 = 1, and F(1/2) = 1.

The finite self-model trace is (1/4,1/2,1). The complementary recurrent pair follows from F(1/3)=2/3 and F(2/3)=1/3. The three-position support is (1/7,2/7,4/7): its Fold images are (2/7,4/7,1/7), because 2·4/7−1=1/7, and its parts sum to (1+2+4)/7=1. The red_of_red record carries the named qualitative identity with that support and its recurrence. Its external-assignment marker retains V3's explicit separation between this structural derivation and assignment of the label to a stimulus/report class.

For a positive integer count n, orbit returns (x,F(x),…,Fⁿ⁻¹(x)); it rejects Boolean, non-integer and nonpositive counts with the original error. first_return examines F(x),F²(x),…,Fⁿ(x) in order and returns the first matching positive host index, or none. These host counts are declared search and trace lengths.

1300. Retained observation: general native proof and source-validation implementation

The original domain is the exact positive rational parts through One, P={x∈ℚ:0<x≤1}. Its Fold operation is

  F(x)=2x when 0<x≤1/2,
  F(x)=2x−1 when 1/2<x≤1.

For y∈P, put l=y/2 and u=(y+1)/2. Then 0<l≤1/2 and 1/2<u≤1, so the corresponding branches give F(l)=2(y/2)=y and F(u)=2((y+1)/2)−1=y. Also u−l=1/2, hence l≠u. Conversely, if F(x)=y, the lower branch gives 2x=y and therefore x=l; the upper branch gives 2x−1=y and therefore x=u. These two cases exhaust the original domain, including y=1, whose predecessors are 1/2 and 1. Thus

  F(x)=y ⇔ x=y/2 ∨ x=(y+1)/2.

For every exact positive part p, the complete-fibre equivalence applied to F(p)=F(p) gives

  p=F(p)/2  or  p=(F(p)+1)/2.

In the first case the observation stores the lower label; otherwise it stores the upper label. The corresponding stored label reconstructs p. The native statement is

  ∀p, ∃a, observe(p,true)=Ok(a) ∧ reversibleFromRecord(a)=true.

Without that label, the source operation retains its original record and recovery result:

  observe(p,false)=Ok(p,F(p),None),
  reversibleFromRecord(p,F(p),None)=false.

StructuralModel.retainedObservation proves the first statement by the existing exactTwoPreimages equivalence and its two cases. StructuralModel.unretainedObservation proves the second by direct reduction. These general results retain the original observation domain and record fields. The quarter-specific family witnesses reuse these operations; they do not replace the quantified proof with a sample.

The current StructuralModel implementation compiles and its sixteen audited exported declarations have empty axiom dependencies. The current Source implementation likewise compiles with empty dependencies for all six exported declarations, retaining the original seal, source-audit and target-row operations. The complete seven-module observation-act audit covers 137 declarations, all with empty axiom dependencies. Evidence: verification/TURN1355_NATIVE_RESULTS/observation1374_full_entry_audit_report.json. Timeline: TURN1355. The native prediction document matches the original in all four instructions, and the experiment registration matches in all seventeen fields. The twelve-field empirical comparison remains outstanding. Evidence: verification/TURN1358_COMPARISON_RESULTS/observation1374_experiment_report.json. Timeline: TURN1358. 1306.1. Common eight-axis candidate construction

The symbols rᵢ and aᵢ in Sections 1228–1299 denote the fixed rejected and preserving forms returned by generated_law._dimensions. The axes have the source order carrier, distinction, operation, record, evidence, provenance, generality and extension. The preserving tuple a is given separately for each entry. The rejected tuple has these same eight coordinates for all 72 entries:

  r1 (carrier) = carrier-absent-or-description-only.
  r2 (distinction) = distinction-collapsed-or-conflated.
  r3 (operation) = operation-imported-fitted-or-missing.
  r4 (record) = favourable-output-without-complete-trace.
  r5 (evidence) = report-behaviour-correlation-or-confidence-substituted.
  r6 (provenance) = prior-consensus-target-or-application-selected.
  r7 (generality) = one-favourable-instance-with-erased-alternatives.
  r8 (extension) = free-parameter-exception-or-opaque-oracle.

For each axis, Dᵢ={rᵢ,aᵢ}. The original Cartesian product and the native nested flatMap/map enumeration therefore give

  G = D₁ × D₂ × D₃ × D₄ × D₅ × D₆ × D₇ × D₈,
  |G| = 2·2·2·2·2·2·2·2 = 256.

To establish coverage, take any candidate c. Its carrier is one of the two carrier constructors, its distinction is one of the two distinction constructors, and likewise for the remaining six coordinates. Each coordinate occurs in its corresponding two-element list. Combining these eight membership facts through the nested product establishes c∈G. The native candidatesComplete proof performs precisely this construction; generatedCardinality evaluates the full list length.

Let Pᵢ(c) mean that coordinate i has its source-preserving name aᵢ. The original decision_reason examines these predicates in source order and returns the explanation at the first failing coordinate. The original decide_candidate obtains survival by comparing the complete candidate identifier with the preserving identifier. The existing criteriaDecision and sourceDecisionMatchesCriteria connect that coordinate test to the native survivor decision. Coordinatewise equality then yields

  survives(c)=true ⇔ P₁(c)∧P₂(c)∧P₃(c)∧P₄(c)∧P₅(c)∧P₆(c)∧P₇(c)∧P₈(c)
                    ⇔ c=a.

The uniqueCriteriaSurvivor proof considers all constructor combinations, and uniqueSurvivor transfers the result through sourceDecisionMatchesCriteria. These are the intermediate steps behind the abbreviated uniqueness equation in each entry section. Candidate identifiers retain the same eight names, joined in their original order; decisionReason retains the first-failure explanations.

The four operational witnesses are evaluated separately from the candidate product. Writing C for the carrier name, D for the distinction name, O for the operation name and E for the evidence-boundary name, the source predicates are nonblank(C), D≠O, E≠C and E≠D together, and the exact family Fold witness. The last predicate is the specific recurrence, reconstruction or partition construction in the preceding family table. Thus the paper's grammar equation, the claim-specific record checks and the family's Fold calculation each have their corresponding source operation and native declaration.

1322. Consciousness missing-feature control

The original external-consequence validator preserves absent source features explicitly. Let τ denote the source JSON truth value: τ(null)=false; τ(b)=b for a Boolean; τ(n)=(n≠0) for an integer; and τ(x)=(|x|>0) for a string, array or object. In particular canonical integer rendering gives τ(n) ⇔ render(n)≠"0". These are representation cases of the original bool operation, not additional scientific premises. In particular, τ(0)=false, τ(−1)=τ(1)=true, while the empty string, empty array and empty object each have truth value false. A nonempty missing-feature array therefore preserves its affirmative absence record even when no feature is promoted to support.

1386. Astronomy adapter: seal identity and retained target disposition

The Astronomy branch adapts the existing generated empirical physics programme and its blind external measurement validator. Its own source-evidence verification removes the declared identity field k from a decoded record R, computes the canonical SHA-256 identity, and requires

 H(R without k) = R[k].

For the pre-source seal S, all three source-selection/content/outcome flags must be exactly false. Every original sealed-file pair (p,h) must satisfy H_bytes(file(p))=h. These checks occur before the target-set construction.

After the original blueprint validation, the adapter requires eight dimensions and a nonempty target-row sequence. For the verified target row T and blueprint claim c with expected label e, it checks

 T.claim_id=c, T.observed_label=e, T.exact_match=True,
 T.external_evidence_selected_survivor=False.

If the optional numeric comparison is present and non-null, its first_adverse_result_reclassified field must be exactly false. This conditional preserves the first adverse result without imposing a numeric comparison on rows for which the original record has none. The complete adapter also derives each shared-physics target row from the first retained source-evidence row, with its source identity and registered locator; the source snapshot hash, empirical disposition and directness remain explicit.

For dimension d with required property p_d and choice c with property set P_c, adaptation retains the name and explanation and sets its preservation flag to [p_d in P_c]. Dimension validation requires two distinct choice names and exactly one preserving choice:

 |C_d|=2, |{name(c):c in C_d}|=2, sum(c in C_d)[p_d in P_c]=1.

The candidate sequence is the ordered Cartesian product of the eight choice lists. Its preservation predicate retains both the original length check and the paired property tests:

 G=C_1 x ... x C_8, |G|=2^8=256,
 preserves(f)=(|f|=8) and all((d,c) in zip(dimensions,f))[p_d in P_c].

The unique-survivor operation enumerates G and filters it by this predicate; it returns a form only when the filtered sequence has length one. Blueprint validation also requires the SFT-ASTRO- claim prefix, eight dimensions, every operational witness, and equality of the declared exact result to the survivor names joined in order by the original double-underscore separator. During target assembly, the claim-indexed dictionary retains the last row for a repeated key, and the first source-evidence row supplies the source identity and locator. The returned adapter retains its blueprint, adapted dimensions, target rows, snapshot path, snapshot hash, empirical disposition and directness.

1387. Directional modality binding and the complete three-quality orbit

The directional record retains two modality carriers, their common Fold image, their complete sum, a directed route and its repeated use. With the existing positive-part Fold F(x)=2x for 2x≤1 and F(x)=2x−1 for 2x>1, the source construction gives

\[
u=\frac14,\qquad v=\frac34,\qquad
F(u)=2\frac14=\frac12,\qquad F(v)=2\frac34-1=\frac12,
\qquad u+v=\frac14+\frac34=1.
\]

These carriers are the two exact predecessors of half-One from the already proved complete Fold-fibre theorem. The held relation is R={(trigger-channel, concurrent-channel)}. Membership in R preserves direction: the reversed ordered pair is absent. The stable-repeat record is (R,R,R), so repeating the route does not insert its reverse. The original common-image, whole and direction witnesses are evaluated from these retained fields.

For the three-quality record, the start is a=1/7 and successive Fold acts construct b and c:

\[
a=\frac17,\qquad b=F(a)=\frac27,\qquad
c=F(b)=\frac47,\qquad F(c)=\frac87-1=\frac17=a,
\qquad a+b+c=\frac{1+2+4}{7}=1.
\]

The three numerators 1, 2 and 4 are distinct over the common positive denominator 7. Thus no earlier position in this trace returns to a, and the third Fold closes the trace. Its generated support is exactly {a,b,c}; the record preserves the source's false external-information-created flag. The construction of the seventh from the complete depth-three support predecessor, and the least distinct successor of the binary period, are already established by GeneratorThreeDerivation.depthThreeUnit, leastDistinctSuccessor and generatorThree. The current record reuses that exact Fold carrier and evaluates the original period, whole and boundary witnesses; no later observation selects its states.

1391. Coordination-form equivalence and the forced distinction order

A retained form is F=(C,A,W,E). C=(c₁,…,cₙ) is the complete composition-label word; A=(a₁,…,aₙ) is the attachment-mode word; W contains one nonempty three-axis word per occurrence; and E retains the distinct unordered adjacency pairs. The constructor requires n≥1, |A|=|W|=n, and each edge joins two distinct positions in {1,…,n}. Each orientation cell is structural EmptyOne or one of the two Fold fibres. Three counts axis positions; it does not introduce a third fibre.

Every occurrence permutation σ is generated. Let pσ(σ(i))=i be its inverse position map. For that order, form the complete vertex and edge words

  Vσ(F)=((cσ(1),aσ(1),Wσ(1)),…,(cσ(n),aσ(n),Wσ(n))),
  Eσ(F)=sort({sort(pσ(u),pσ(v)) : (u,v)∈E}).

The source canonical signature is the lexicographically least complete pair:

  K(F)=minlex{(Vσ(F),Eσ(F)) : σ∈Perm({1,…,n})}.

The native implementation enumerates this complete list and folds its exact lexicographic minimum. completeVariantMinimum binds the returned canonical value to that fold; exhaustiveOccurrenceOrders binds its input to the existing complete occurrence-permutation generator. No occurrence map is selected in advance. Removing only the orientation component gives K₀(F), which still retains every composition label, attachment label and adjacency.

Comparison first requires equal positive width and equal sorted composition words. For admissible L and R, the exact-equivalence decision is K(L)=K(R). The source then determines the distinction by the following ordered implications:

  K(L)=K(R) ⇒ same-equivalence-class;
  K(L)≠K(R) ∧ K₀(L)≠K₀(R) ⇒ attachment-class-distinction;
  K(L)≠K(R) ∧ K₀(L)=K₀(R) ∧ K(M(L))=K(R)
    ⇒ mirror-complement-class-distinction;
  K(L)≠K(R) ∧ K₀(L)=K₀(R) ∧ K(M(L))≠K(R)
    ⇒ orientation-adjacency-class-distinction.

Here M exchanges fibre-one with fibre-two at every occupied cell. Structural EmptyOne remains structural EmptyOne; the source mirror reconstructs its default identity. Thus the mirror operation changes neither the occurrence labels nor the retained edges.   C′=C·c,  A′=A·a,  W′=W·w,
  E′=E·((p,n+1) : p∈P).

Every prior component is retained as a prefix. EmptyOne adjacency and an empty endpoint tuple both add no edges. The complete constructor is applied again to the extended form, preserving its original guards.

  I_s(G)=|{w∈G : pᵢ(w) XOR pⱼ(w)}|     for a held contrast,
  I_s(G)=|{w∈G : pᵢ(w) AND pⱼ(w)}|     for a boundary pair.

An empty incidence is retained as structural EmptyOne. Supports with equal incidence form one level; distinct incidences form separate levels, ordered from absence to increasing positive count. Every level retains its complete support members. For adjacent incidence counts i<j and N retained ligands, the structural separation is (j−i)/N, with an absent lower rank contributing no incidence. For four complete-axis occurrences, each contrast sees none and every boundary pair sees four; the multiplicities are (2,3) and separation is 4/4=1.

  dₗ=mᵤ/(mₗ+mᵤ),   dᵤ=mₗ/(mₗ+mᵤ),

Consequently the six-axis balance distances are (2/5,3/5), while the four-axis distances are (3/5,2/5). Removing the interaction restores one five-member level, no adjacent separation and structural absence of the two binary balance distances.
