1399. Insertion, extrusion, migratory insertion and elimination pathways

The pathway law retains the complete adjacency transformation. A held carrier is identified by its family and label. For two endpoints a and b, the original _edge operation puts the lesser endpoint first under lexicographic comparison of (family,label):

  e(a,b) = (a,b) when (family(a),label(a)) <= (family(b),label(b)),
  e(a,b) = (b,a) otherwise.

This fixes the stored orientation of an undirected adjacency. The native edge operation preserves that ordering. Each transformation retains the carrier sequence C, before and after adjacency sequences B and A, removed and added sequences R and N, a held pathway class k and the complete process-component sequence P:

  T = (C,B,A,R,N,k,P).

The constructor requires distinct carrier support with |C| >= 2, no self-adjacency and no duplicate edges in B or A. Every endpoint of every before or after edge must belong to C. Writing braces for the set of edges represented by a retained sequence, the original complete-difference tests are

  {R} = {B} \ {A},
  {N} = {A} \ {B}.

The comparisons are set equalities, exactly as in v3; the original removed and added sequences remain retained as supplied. The pathway-class family and nonempty composition are also checked. traceRetains proves retention of every field, and traceDifferences proves both displayed equalities in the native set representation for every accepted trace.

For three distinct carriers X, Z and Y, insertion replaces the original X-Z adjacency with X-Y and Y-Z:

  C = [X,Z,Y],
  B = [e(X,Z)],
  A = [e(X,Y),e(Y,Z)],
  R = B,  N = A,
  P = [insertion].

Consequently, the before/after counts are 1 and 2, and the removed/added counts are 1 and 2. insertionDerivation proves this entire construction for every accepted source assembly; the original witness checks these exact counts.

Extrusion is the exact reversal of an insertion trace. It retains the same carriers and exchanges the adjacency states and their corresponding differences:

  Extrude(C,B,A,R,N,insertion,P)
    = (C,A,B,N,R,extrusion,[reverse-insertion]).

The reverse differences follow directly:

  {removed_reverse} = {N} = {A} \ {B},
  {added_reverse} = {R} = {B} \ {A}.

The no-self-edge, distinctness and endpoint-membership guards are preserved when B and A are exchanged. reversedTraceAccepted proves this guard preservation for an accepted trace. insertionInverseExists then proves that extrusion succeeds for every accepted insertion and returns the displayed reverse record. extrusionRetains proves all its field equalities, including

  after(Extrude(T)) = before(T),
  carriers(Extrude(T)) = carriers(T).

Generic elimination is kept as a separate pathway class; it is not substituted for the exact insertion inverse.

Migratory insertion retains both migration and insertion in its composition. With metal occurrence M, migrant X and inserted carrier Y, the source constructs

  R = [e(M,X)],
  N = [e(X,Y)],
  P = [migration,insertion].

The metal-inserted adjacency e(M,Y) is retained, while e(M,X) is replaced by e(X,Y). migratoryDerivation establishes all these fields. The post-seal exact analysis computes the common-edge count from the native before and after sets; the original construction gives one common edge.

  B_source = unique([e(A,X),e(B,Y)]).

Its new product adjacency depends on the original exact centre identity comparison:

  N = [e(A,B)] when A differs from B,
  N = [e(X,Y)] when A equals B.

The after state is N and the removed support is B_source. eliminationDerivation proves the complete assembly and retains the original held composition

  [two-eliminand-loss, new-unsaturation-ring-or-carbene-boundary].

This product boundary remains held while the adjacency transformation is exact. The original distinct-centre witness removes two source edges; the single-centre witness retains three carriers. All original constructor guards are reapplied to both branches, including self-edge and exact-difference rejection.

1400. Metal clusters: complete connected support, direct bonds and ligand bridges

The metal-cluster law retains an entity E, its ordered metal-centre support C, and the complete relation sequence R. A relation is

  r = (left, right, mode, bridge_support),
  mode in {direct-metal-bond, bridging-ligand-path, held-grouping-relation}.

Both endpoints are distinct held metal centres. A bridging relation carries a positive sequence of held bridging-ligand occurrences. The other two modes carry no bridge support. The original constructor retains that sequence exactly, including any repeated bridge occurrence supplied to it. relationRetains proves all four fields. The generated bridge sequence for positive count n is

  B_n = [bridge(left,right,1), ..., bridge(left,right,n)].

Cluster support contains at least two distinct metal centres. The entity family is cluster-entity, the relation sequence is nonempty, and the centre count equals |C|. Duplicate relations are excluded using the original key

  key(r) = (min(label(left),label(right)),
            max(label(left),label(right)), label(mode)).

Thus endpoint reversal does not create a second relation of the same mode. Distinct modes between the same endpoints remain distinct, and bridge-support multiplicity does not alter this key.

Connectivity is computed from the first centre, R_0 = {C[0]}. Each complete ordered scan examines every relation and adds an unreached endpoint whenever its other endpoint is reached. Let S_R denote that scan. The source repeats

  R_(k+1) = S_R(R_k)

while a scan changes the reached set, and accepts precisely when the final reached set equals the set of C. Mutual inclusion, rather than cardinality alone, supplies this equality. The constructor does not add a separate membership restriction on every relation endpoint: a wholly disconnected outside relation component remains governed by the original reached-set test.

Termination follows from the supplied endpoint occurrences themselves. Let U be the sequence containing both endpoints of every relation. Define

  m_U(X) = sum_(u in U) [u is not in X].

Adding an unreached endpoint decreases m_U; repeated occurrences in U can decrease it by more than one. Retaining a reached endpoint leaves it unchanged. Every scan either leaves the entire reached sequence unchanged or strictly decreases m_U. Consequently the original repeated scan terminates. Its result R_* satisfies

  S_R(R_*) = R_*.

The native closure operation follows this exact loop. finiteScanEqualsClosure proves, for every finite relation sequence and initial reached sequence X, that an executable scan with more than m_U(X) iterations equals that loop. Since m_U(X) <= |U|, endpointBoundScan derives the executable bound |U|+1 directly from the supplied relations. reachedExact and reachedClosed connect the cluster operation to this equality and fixed point. The bound introduces no scientific parameter or caller-selected cutoff.

The direct and bridging counts are derived from the full relation sequence:

  d(R) = |[r in R : mode(r) = direct-metal-bond]|,
  b(R) = |[r in R : mode(r) = bridging-ligand-path]|,
  Q(n) = PositiveCount(n) for n > 0; Q(0) = EmptyOne.

The complete cluster record is

  (E,C,R,PositiveCount(|C|),Q(d(R)),Q(b(R))).

clusterRetains and forcedRetains establish these fields, the actual connectivity condition and the supplied centre-label construction. Held grouping therefore need not be relabelled as a direct bond or ligand bridge. The two-centre direct witness has d=1. The two-centre bridging witness contains two bridge occurrences but one bridging relation, so b=1. The held-grouping witness has structural EmptyOne for its direct count.

For an attached centre x and retained anchor a, the original operation constructs one relation r(a,x,mode), appends x to the existing centre labels and appends r to the existing relation sequence:

  C_labels' = C_labels ++ [x],
  R' = R ++ [r(a,x,mode)].

A bridging successor generates one bridge occurrence. Every original constructor guard is reapplied. appendRetains proves retention of the entity, complete prior relation sequence and centre-label construction for every successful append; namedCentreCount and appendCount establish

  centre_count' = |C| + 1.

The class counts obey the exact extension equation

  count_mode(R ++ [r]) = count_mode(R) + [mode(r) = mode].

For a closed reached sequence X containing a but not x, attachedCentreStep establishes

  S_(R ++ [(a,x)])(X) = X ++ [x].

Subsequent scanning and the final set-equality test remain the source operations. The original successor witness has three centres. A supplied third centre disconnected from the sole relation is rejected.

1401. Primitive local-solid formula and retained occurrence extension

A local solid motif retains the complete occurrence sequence O. The species name s(x) is the part of an occurrence label before its first # separator. Species are listed in first-occurrence order, and the complete multiplicity of each listed species is

  n_s(O) = |[x in O : s(x) = s]|.

For the ordered species list (s_1,...,s_k), the original primitive-formula operation computes

  g = gcd(n_(s_1),...,n_(s_k)),
  F(O) = [(s_1, n_(s_1)/g), ..., (s_k, n_(s_k)/g)].

Division is exact natural-number division in the source construction. The stored formula entries carry held chemical-species labels and positive counted values. The occurrence sequence itself is retained; gcd reduction changes the formula coefficients, not the underlying occurrence census. For two A and two B occurrences, g=2 and the primitive vector is (1,1). Adding one A occurrence changes the counts to (3,2), whose gcd is one, and the primitive vector becomes (3,2). Species order follows the original first occurrence, including when B precedes A.

The native speciesName, speciesLabels, speciesCount and primitiveFormula operations preserve these source operations and their failure behavior. formulaEntryRetains proves that an accepted formula entry retains its supplied species and positive count, while primitiveCountPositive establishes positivity from the counted-value representation.

The complete local-solid record is

  S = (motif, O, B, F, A, K, scope, handoff),

where B is the ordered sequence of local bond pairs, A is the repeat-axis support, and K is positive second-constituent occurrence support or structural EmptyOne. The original constructor requires positive distinct occurrence support, the exact recomputed primitive formula, one to three distinct generated repeat axes, and distinct valid bond pairs whose two unequal endpoints occur in O. Ordered bond pairs retain their orientation: (a,b) and (b,a) are distinct supplied pairs. Empty local bond support is admitted by the original constructor. An EmptyOne constituent retains its identity there, and positive constituent support retains all its occurrences.

The ownership labels are fixed as

  scope = (ownership, composition-and-local-bonding),
  handoff = (ownership-handoff, materials-bulk-response).

solidRetains proves that every accepted constructor result retains all eight fields. It does not replace an explicit local adjacency sequence with an averaged coordination number.

For a supplied species s, the original successor computes n_s(O)+1 as its next occurrence index and constructs x = occurrence(s,n_s(O)+1). It then applies

  O' = O ++ [x],
  B' = B ++ [(anchor,x)],
  F' = F(O').

All constructor guards are reapplied. appendDerivation proves these exact field relations for every successful successor, including recomputation of the primitive formula and retention of motif, repeat axes, constituent support and both ownership labels. appendCounts gives

  |O'| = |O| + 1,
  |B'| = |B| + 1.

occurrenceRetains identifies the generated family and the exact species#index label. The successor is therefore a retained occurrence-and-bond extension with a recomputed formula, while the Chemistry-to-Materials ownership handoff stays fixed.

1401.1. Complete primitive-vector correspondence and generated local motif

The whole-vector derivation connects the returned formula to its generating occurrence census. Write L(O) for the species labels in first-occurrence order and N(O) = [n_s(O) : s in L(O)]. For every accepted primitiveFormula result F, completePrimitiveVector establishes

  N(O) = [n_1] ++ N_tail,
  g = fold_left(gcd, n_1, N_tail),
  [(label(f.species), f.primitive_count) : f in F]
    = [(s, n_s(O) / g) : s in L(O)].

This equality covers the entire returned sequence in its source order. rowReading establishes each returned label and quotient, and rowVector carries that equality through the complete sequence construction. The first count initializes the gcd fold exactly as in v3's reduce(gcd,counts). An empty count sequence produces the original failure rather than supplying an alternative divisor or a formula row. Every accepted quotient is retained as a PositiveCount.

The local_solid generator begins with the supplied ordered positive species counts [(s_1,n_1),...,(s_k,n_k)]. It constructs every indexed occurrence:

  O = concat_[j=1..k] [occurrence(s_j,1), ..., occurrence(s_j,n_j)].

The occurrence label is s_j#index. The source lookup derives its species key and integer index from that label, retains the last occurrence for a repeated lookup key, and resolves every declared bond pair through the completed lookup. With lookup T and the supplied ordered bond-key sequence [(a_i,b_i)], the generated local adjacency is

  B = [(T(a_i),T(b_i)) : i in source order].

Missing keys fail before construction. A repeated lookup key does not remove occurrences from O: the complete occurrence sequence still reaches the original constructor and its distinctness guard. Bond pairs retain their supplied orientation and order.

A rank above three fails at the generator's first guard. The second constituent is generated as

  K_m = [guest-1, ..., guest-m] for a positive supplied occurrence count m.

1402. Exact defect chemistry: reference and observed occurrence supports

A reference motif retains each site and its expected species. An occupancy records either a species occurrence or structural EmptyOne at that same site; an interstitial supplies an additional occurrence. Let R be the ordered reference species list and O the occupied species list followed by the interstitial species list. The observed-support derivation preserves precisely this concatenation and excludes only EmptyOne occupancies.

For each species x in first-occurrence order over R concatenated with O, define
  r_x = count_R(x),  o_x = count_O(x),
  missing_x = PositiveCount(r_x - o_x) if r_x > o_x; EmptyOne otherwise,
  added_x = PositiveCount(o_x - r_x) if o_x > r_x; EmptyOne otherwise.
The two directional supports retain separate positive counts. A reconciliation row cannot have both a positive missing support and a positive added support. The Lean theorem missingAddedExclusive proves this property for every accepted row. vacancyRetains proves that the reference site is retained with its exact EmptyOne occupancy.

For any nonempty occurrence list L, let x_1,...,x_k be its distinct species in first-occurrence order and n_i = count_L(x_i). Its primitive formula is
  g = gcd(n_1,...,n_k),  F(L) = ((x_1,n_1/g),...,(x_k,n_k/g)).
The completePrimitiveVector theorem proves the entire returned vector equals these ordered quotients, using the gcd folded over the same complete count vector. Applied separately to R and O, this yields the reference and observed formulas.

For R=(A,A,B,B), the unchanged motif has primitive formula (1,1) and EmptyOne defect support. Removing one A occupancy gives O=(A,B,B), formula (1,2), missing_A=1 and added_A=EmptyOne. Adding a native A interstitial gives O=(A,A,B,B,A), formula (3,2). Replacing an A with C gives O=(A,C,B,B), formula (1,1,2), missing_A=1 and added_C=1. Vacancy, substitution and interstitial classes are emitted in that order when their corresponding support condition holds. Foreign observed species force extrinsic origin; a defect using only reference species has intrinsic origin. The four original operational witness propositions are proved by Lean kernel reduction.

1403. Inorganic acid–base and redox reaction networks

A Lewis step retains five components: its step identity, pair provider P, pair acceptor A, the ordered electron pair (e₁,e₂), and the resulting adduct Q. The source requires distinct chemical identities P, A and Q, and two distinct electron-carrier occurrences. Thus its retained data are
  L = (step, P, A, (e₁,e₂), Q),
  P ≠ A, P ≠ Q, A ≠ Q, e₁ ≠ e₂,
  participants(L) = (P,A,Q), |pair(L)| = 2.
The provider, acceptor and adduct are retained together with the exact pair; an unstructured mixture is not substituted for this record. The native constructor checks the original label families, distinctness and pair support in the original order. lewisRetains proves that every successful construction returns all five supplied components unchanged. exactPairCount proves that every accepted Lewis step has exactly two retained pair occurrences.

A redox step similarly retains
  R = (step, D, A, E), E = (e₁,...,eₙ), n > 0,
  D ≠ A, eᵢ ≠ eⱼ for i ≠ j,
  participants(R) = (D,A), transfer_count(R) = n.
Oxidation and reduction use this one retained electron sequence. There are no independently chosen donor-removal and acceptor-receipt carrier sequences. The original reversal operation constructs
  reverse(R,step') = (step', A, D, E).
The theorem reverseConserves establishes the endpoint exchange and exact equality of the electron sequence for every successful reversal. The constructor and reverse operation retain the source's guards; redoxRetains establishes all four returned fields, and positiveTransfer proves that every accepted redox step retains a strictly positive number of electron occurrences.

A network is the ordered record N = (identity,S,L,R,Pth), comprising a positive finite distinct species sequence S, Lewis-step support L, redox-step support R and ordered step path Pth. Structural EmptyOne represents an absent transition class; at least one class has positive transition support. Let T be the Lewis step identities followed by the redox step identities. The original path checks are
  |Pth| = |T|, set(Pth) = set(T), |set(T)| = |T|.
The constructor also requires every transition participant to belong to S. These conditions retain every distinct transition identity exactly once in the ordered path. They allow the path order itself to differ from the storage order of the two transition classes. The source rejects an omitted participant, duplicate step identity, incomplete path or wrong transition class. The native boundary representation preserves both a retained empty tuple and EmptyOne when supplied directly to the constructor, and preserves their original guard priority.

For an appended redox step R* with endpoints D* and A*, the original successor is
  S' = ordered_unique(S ++ [D*,A*]),
  L' = L, after the original empty-class normalisation,
  R' = R ++ [R*],
  Pth' = Pth ++ [step(R*)].
Here ordered_unique keeps the first occurrence of each full held identity. appendRetains proves these exact returned sequences, and appendPathCount gives |Pth'| = |Pth| + 1. The same network constructor rechecks conservation, participant coverage and the complete path. No named-reaction exception is introduced.

The original witnesses give a Lewis network with three species, one step and two pair occurrences; a redox network with two species and a two-electron transfer; the exact reversed transfer; and a combined successor with five species and two ordered steps. The fifth witness rejects a Lewis network from which the adduct species is omitted. All five are proved from the actual native operations. The complete grammar has eight binary axes—carrier, species, acid–base, adduct, redox, coupling, path and extension—and therefore 2⁸ = 256 alternatives. Native enumeration and decision proofs preserve the original source coordinate names and elimination decisions.

The empirical procedure retains fifteen target surfaces from five sources: seven development-observed records and eight unopened identity-only records. Each prediction word contains the sealed premise, six identity values and four network-law labels. Prediction sealing precedes target release and comparison. 1406. Exact finite conformer generation and equivalence

A molecular carrier consists of a positive finite atom-labelled graph G=(V,E). Its admitted bond records have distinct endpoints, are normalized as (min(u,v),max(u,v)), contain no repeated normalized edge, and connect every retained position. Starting from the first position, the original simultaneous expansion is
R₀={v₁},
Rₖ₊₁=Rₖ ∪ {u,v : {u,v}∈E and (u∈Rₖ or v∈Rₖ)}.
Each expansion retains Rₖ and stays within V. If the cardinality does not change, the expansion is fixed; otherwise |Rₖ₊₁|>|Rₖ|. Since |Rₖ|≤|V| and |R₀|=1, the finite native bound |V| reaches the same fixed point as the source loop. The constructor requires that fixed point to contain every position. This is the source's connected-carrier admission, rather than an assumption that arbitrary atom records are connected.

For the ordered rotor census r₁,…,rₘ, each held alphabet Aᵢ is positive, finite and distinct. Its complete reversal map ρᵢ has the same state domain and satisfies ρᵢ(ρᵢ(a))=a. The assignment generator is the exact Cartesian product
Pₘ=A₁×⋯×Aₘ,
Pₘ₊₁={a++[b] : a∈Pₘ, b∈Aₘ₊₁},
|Pₘ₊₁|=|Pₘ|·|Aₘ₊₁|.
Completeness follows by decomposing a retained assignment into its first state and remaining word. Uniqueness follows from distinct alphabet states and injectivity of list construction. Thus every admitted state word is generated once; no coordinate tolerance or energy cutoff enters generation.
